Volume One:
Emperors, Ministers, and Confucian Scholars.
Second, the Buddha and Patriarchs; Third, the Dharma-body Buddha and Form-body Buddha.
Chapter Four: Monasteries, Halls, Stupas, Temples, Chambers,
Doors, Bridges, and Roads (with Appendices)
Chapter Five: Questions on the Dharma from the Patriarchal Teachings;
Discourse on Dhyāna-Samādhi and Awakening to the Great Way.
Sixth: Demonstrating to the Assembly and Examining Disciples through Staff and Shouts,
Part Seven.
Section Eight: The Round Mirror Reflecting Capacities; The Master-Disciple Tradition;
Examining and Expounding the Scriptures; Ancestral Verses on Discourse and Debate.
Eighth: Names of the Head Administrative Officers, Attendants, Dharma Relatives,
Nuns, and Novices.
The Tenth:
The Realm of the Person; The Eleventh: The True Image of the Mind, Eyes, Limbs, and Body.
Section Twelve: Dwelling in the Mountains (including the Opening of the Hall), Dwelling in Hermitages and the Precepts (including Ordination),
and Pilgrimage, Prostration, and Visitation.
Wandering Mountains (with appended verses of farewell), Dispatching Letters, Following Transformation, Responding to Transformation,
Divine Marvels, Cause and Effect, Bathing, Reclining and Resting— Thirteenth.
Chapter Fourteen: Inquiries on Illness, Medical Arts, Divination, Medication, Transformation, Mourning Rites,
Annual Festivals, Untying Knots, and the Sun, Moon, Wind, Clouds, Snow, and Rain.
15. Water and Fire;
Robes and Alms Bowls;
Clothing and Ornaments (including Needles); Shoes and Socks; Precious Jewels; Lutes and Chess.
16. Curtains and Canopies, Boats and Oars;
Ritual Implements: Mallets, Whisks, Rosaries, Vases, Staffs, and Umbrellas.
Seventeenth: Mirrors, fans,
utensils, knives, swords, bows, arrows, and antiques.
Section Eighteen:
Grains, Meals, Congee, Fried Cakes, the Five Tastes, Tea,
Soup (Tea-picking appended), and Vegetables.
Nineteenth: Field Vegetation (including Bamboo), Flowers and Fruits, Incense and Lamps, Sweeping,
and Firewood.

Dragons, Tigers, Oxen, Deer, Cats, Dogs, Turtles, Fish, Hares,
Snakes, Birds, and Beasts.
*Chanlin Leiju*, Scroll One:
Emperors, Ministers, and Confucian Scholars—
Emperors.
King Aśoka provided a meal for thirty thousand great arhats within his inner palace. As the King personally distributed the incense, he saw that the first seat was unoccupied.
The King asked, "Why is there no one at this seat? One venerable elder replied, "This is the seat of the Venerable Piṇḍola-bharadvāja.
This man has seen the Buddha in person. The King asked, "Where is this man now? The elder replied, "For the time being..."
"Wait a moment. Having finished speaking, Piṇḍola descended from the sky. The King invited him to take a seat and paid his respects, but Piṇḍola did not acknowledge him.

The King then asked, "I have heard that you, Venerable One, personally saw the Buddha come; is this true? Piṇḍola brushed back his eyebrows with his hand and pointed to them, saying, "Do you understand?
The King said, "I do not understand. Piṇḍola said, "The Dragon King of Lake Anavatapta has invited me."
The Buddha’s fast. The old monk was also included among their number.
Wuzu Keqin came forth and said, "How shameful! Cuiyan Ruozhen said, "Tell me, where did you see it?
Even if the snow were falling and the lake light were drifting and shimmering, do not speak of such dreams. Baoning Daoyong.

Daiyun said: "Rare, rare indeed! Foxing Tai said: "Although King Ashoka fed thirty thousand great arhats, he nonetheless did not recognize Venerable Piṇḍola. Since King Ashoka did not recognize him," [the story continues].
"Do you all recognize it yet? If you do not, I shall point it out for you.
Thereupon, he took up his staff, descended from the meditation seat, stood, and said, "What is it?"
Foyin Yuan’s verse says: "Raising his eyebrows to show King Aśoka, At that time, both ordinary and sage were beyond discussion.
Later, when facing the assembly, it was difficult to gather them back; Above the eyes, as before, two tufts grow long. Baoning Yong said:
Our Buddha personally beheld Piṇḍola: his eyebrows were long, his hair was short, and his two eyes were coarse.
King Aśoka still harbored doubts like a fox. *Oṃ mānida hsi hsu lu*. Fohuiquan said: "When a single film obscures the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion;
meeting on a narrow path, it is difficult to avoid. Great King, do you recognize this old monk?"
His eyebrows were like snow, long and reaching the ground.
Once, while the King of East India was inviting the Venerable Prajñātāra for a meal, the King asked: "Everyone here recites the sutras;
why is it that you alone do not? The Master replied: "When this poor monk exhales, his breath does not involve external conditions; when he inhales..."
Not dwelling within the realms of the aggregates, he constantly turns such sutras as these, numbering hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of scrolls.
Fenyang Shanzhao said: "This merely exhausts the venerable one's mental power.
Tiantong Juexin’s verse says: "The cloud-rhinoceros gazes at the moon, its brilliance radiant; the wooden horse roams the spring, its vigor unrestrained."
A pair of cold, azure eyes beneath the brows—how could one reading scriptures ever penetrate the ox-hide? With a mind of clarity, one transcends vast eons;
with heroic power, one breaks through the heavy encirclement. At the pivot of the wondrous circle, the spiritual mechanism turns.
Hanshan forgets the path he came; Shide takes him by the hand and returns home together. Xichan Xu said: "The incoming breath has never dwelt [anywhere]."
Regarding the aggregates and elements: when exhaling, how could one ever involve oneself in the myriad conditions? A single note of a fisherman’s flute leaves the southern marsh;
as before, one sleeps deep within the reeds.
King Kaniṣka, wielding his sword, asked the Venerable Siṃha, "Have you realized the emptiness of the aggregates? The Master replied, "I have."
He attained the emptiness of the aggregates (*skandha-śūnyatā*). The King asked, "Since you have attained the emptiness of the aggregates, are you free from birth and death?
He replied, "I am already free from birth and death. The King said, "Since you are free from birth and death, may I beg for your head from you, Master?

He replied, "Even my body is not mine; how much more so my head? The King then beheaded him, whereupon white milk surged forth several feet high. The King’s arm fell off of its own accord, and he died seven days later. Thus it was recorded.
Ziguang sighed at the outset, saying, "Why did my father bring this calamity upon himself?
Xuansha said, "Even the Great Master Shizi could not manage his own head.
Xuangjue challenged him, saying, "Tell me, was it struck or not struck? He added, "Xuansha spoke thus because he wanted people to act."
The Master does not wish for someone else to be the master. If he did wish for someone else to be the master, then the aggregates (*skandhas*) would not be empty.
If he does not wish for someone else to be the master, where does Xue Sha’s meaning lie in saying this?
Try to judge it! Fenyang Zhao said in his alternative verse: "I know you will not be stingy. Bajiao said: "Selling jewels and encountering a blind Persian."
Langya Jue said: "Jibin was fond of a single-edged sword, but alas, there were no eyes upon it.
The Venerable One was a fine lion, yet he did not know how to turn back and leap. Cuiyan Zhi said: "At that time, the Patriarch extended his neck."
The King raised his sword. At such a time, if someone had been able to advise him and stop him, this public case would remain unresolved to this day.
How will the monks of today resolve it? Xuedou Xian said: "A masterful sovereign naturally possesses [the authority]."
The *Haixin Xin* (Verse on the Seal of the Ocean) says: "In the center of the primordial chaos, a single aperture opens; It distinguishes clarity from turbidity and arranges the Three Powers.
It was solely because of that one stroke of the sword at night when the opportunity presented itself That courage failed and the soul was startled, never to return. Foyuan Yuan said:
On the banks of the Yangzi River, willows flourish in spring. The floating catkins bring sorrow to the traveler at the ferry crossing.
At twilight in the farewell pavilion, a single sound of the *qiang* flute is heard; you head toward Xiangxiang, while I go to Qin. Gushan Gui said: "The boatman goes down to Yangzhou."
Floating duckweed follows the flow of the water. A single note of the *Hemanzi* melody moves the sorrow and grief of a thousand ages.
Jingshan Guo said: "To kill a man, one must be a man who kills. With a single stroke, he is cut in two.
Though his head and limbs may be severed by the edge of the sword, how can they compare to the *chuduo* drill of the Qin era?"
Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty encountered the First Patriarch, Master Bodhidharma, as he arrived in Jinling from the Western Heavens by sea.
The Emperor asked, "What is the primary meaning of the holy truth? The Master replied, "Vast emptiness; there is no saint. The Emperor asked, "Who is it that stands before me?
The Master replied, "I do not know. The Emperor failed to attain realization. The Master then broke off a reed, crossed the river, and went to the Wei kingdom. Later, the Emperor...
He brought this up and questioned Master Zhigong. Zhigong asked, "Your Majesty, do you recognize this person? The Emperor replied, "I do not.
Zhigong said, "This is the Great Being Avalokiteśvara, who transmits the Buddha’s mind-seal. The Emperor said, "I shall dispatch a messenger to summon him.
Zhigong replied, "Do not speak of summoning him by Your Majesty; even if all the people of the nation went, he would still not return."
Fenyang Wude said in his place: "Your disciple’s wisdom is shallow. Baoning Daoyong said in the Emperor’s place, showing his tongue to demonstrate it.
Quandaodao’s verse says: "Ordinary and sage entangled, the emotion not yet forgotten; when suddenly there is no sage, one is startled into madness."
"Prince Liang had no strategy; he was simply caught in a turmoil caused by the barbarians.
Xuedou Xian said: "The Holy Truth is vast and open—how can one discern it? When asked, 'Who is facing me? he replied, 'I do not know.
Because of this, he crossed the river in secret; how could he avoid the thorns of life? Though the whole nation pursued him, he did not return. For ten thousand ages, all is empty."
"Remembering each other? Stop remembering each other! When the pure breeze pervades the earth, how can it have limits?
The Master looked left and right and said, "Is there any patriarch here? Call him over and let him wash the old monk’s feet. Baoning Yong said:
"When it has been forged until glowing red, strike it once more; sparks fly out in countless numbers from all sides. A perfect, ten-part diamond drill indeed!"
Laid out before the gate, to whom shall it be sold? Wang Yi said: "The primary meaning is vast and empty, transcending the Emperor of Forms.
Without consulting the almanac for many years, how can one debate the spring equinox and summer solstice?
The white crane of Liaodong has departed without a trace; half of the Three Mountains falls beyond the blue heavens. Fojian Qin said: "It begins to cry."
A single stroke of the bell at the Agoka Gate: the sun is warm, and the Azure Dragon sleeps soundly. Again, the drum atop the Phoenix Terrace is struck;
yet in the dead of night, the auspicious phoenixes do not yet flutter their wings. The imperial foundation is as eternally firm as a boulder;
the barbarian monk has wasted his life’s strength in vain. Pointing back toward Shaolin, he says, "Go back! A gust of spring wind scatters the flowers in disarray. *Taiping* (Peace and Stability)
An ancient said: "The Gate of the First Principle of the Noble Truths is vast and empty; who is there to be honored as a sage? How laughable!
In the third month of Jiangnan, the partridge cries out amidst the village of a hundred flowers. Changling Zhuo said: "Not knowing how to be a guest, you trouble the host;
your face shows no shame, with little joy and much anger. Xuetang Xing said: "The butcher of Western Heaven..."
The son’s spirit was fierce and bold; his crimes in deceiving and oppressing the Divine Land could not be escaped.
Emperor Liang pressed him head-on with a light squeeze, and indeed raised the "Sword that Saves Living Beings. Fodeng Xun said: "He unfurls his banners and arrays his troops, seeking victory at once.
Who knew the Imperial Chariot would not personally campaign? He firmly grasps the banner-staff and withdraws his ranks, until he reaches the Peak of Heroism and does not dispatch a single soldier."
Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty asked the Great Master Bodhidharma, "Since I ascended the throne, I have built temples, transcribed scriptures, and ordained monks beyond counting.
I do not know what merit these deeds possess. The Master replied, "In truth, there is no merit. The Emperor said, "Why does the Master say there is none?
The Master replied, "These are merely the small fruits of the human and celestial realms, causes tainted by outflows (*āsrava*). They are like a shadow following a form; though..."
"There is that which is not real. The Emperor asked, "What are the truly real merits? The Master replied, "Pure wisdom is wondrously perfect;
its essence is inherently empty and still. Such merits as these are not to be sought through worldly means."
Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty invited Master Fu to lecture on the sutras. When the Master ascended the seat, he struck the desk once with his measuring ruler and immediately descended.
The Emperor was startled. Master Zhi asked the Emperor, "Does Your Majesty understand? The Emperor replied, "I do not understand.
Master Zhi said, "The Master’s lecture on the sutras is finished."
Baizhang Yuan said: "Fotuo Dashi and Zhigong were both passed over by Emperor Wu of Liang in a single document.
Zhengjue Yi’s verse says: "The long parting from the Twin Śāla Trees had its cause; the sovereign of Jinling yearned for the benevolent man."
"How excellent! Having ascended this lofty seat, with a single strike, the Great Thousandfold World passes beyond the dust of the mundane. Xuedou Xian said:
"Had he not cast his body away at the Twin Śāla Trees, he would have stirred up dust and grime in the land of Liang.
Had it not been for the Elder Zhizong at that time, he too would have been a sorrowful refugee from a fallen nation. Baizhang Yuan said: "When did the Great Being ever attain realization?"
"Expounding the Sūtra. Master Zhìgōng’s skillful means merely assisted him; with one sweep of his hand over the desk, nothing remained to be grasped.
This left King Liáng staring wide-eyed. Císhòu Shēn said: "When the Great Being expounded the Sūtra, his sweeping of the desk became the commentary."
A single pill dispels myriad ailments; there is no need for the "donkey-rush" medicine. Fojian Qin said:
"Upon the table, a single sound rings out—*bing-bao-bao*. This is already a layer upon layer of added footnotes. For what reason does King Liang not turn his head?
Master Zhigong takes the error and follows it further."
Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty asked National Teacher Huizhong, "After you, Master, have passed away, what will you require?

The Master replied, "Donor, please build a seamless stūpa for this poor monk. The Emperor said, "I request the Master’s design for the stūpa. After a long silence, the Master asked, "Do you understand?
The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I have a Dharma-heir disciple named Dayuan who is well-acquainted with this matter."
The Emperor requested that he be summoned and questioned. After the Master passed away, the Emperor issued an edict for Danyuan to inquire about this matter, asking, "What is the meaning of this?
Danyuan replied, "South of Xiang, north of Tan; therein lies gold filling the entire land. Beneath the shadowless tree, the boat is joined."
"In the Lapis Lazuli Hall there is no one with true knowledge.

Xuedou Xian took up this case and said: "Setting aside for a moment that Suzong did not understand, does Dan Yuan understand? It takes nothing more than saying, 'Please, Master, show me the model for a stupa.
All the patriarchs of the Western Heaven and this land, when pressed by such a challenge, could not help but [fall into difficulty].
Taking south for north, someone may come forward who is unwilling to comply. I would ask you: "Which of these is the seamless stupa?
Shending Yin said: "If the National Teacher’s previous function had not been clearly understood, [this would not have occurred]."
Next, I ask: Tan-yuan’s verse was likewise like this. Tell me, is it perfect or not?
Although it is a skillful means, you must understand its essence before you can attain it. Do you understand? Shen-ding will provide four turns of phrase for all of you:
"South of Xiang, north of Tan—the Way for Ruler and Minister exists. "Within lies gold sufficient to fill a nation"—this is the pure essence, wondrous and eternal.
Beneath the shadowless tree, they board the same boat; a thousand sages follow one and the same track. Upon the lapis lazuli palace, there is no one to recognize them;
the paths of the ordinary and the sage are severed. If you understand it in this way, you will certainly not be deceived. This is how I, the old monk, have annotated it.
Furthermore, this would be to辜负 (gu fù) the National Teacher. Wuzu Yan said: "In front are pearls and lapis lazuli;
behind are agate and coral. To the left are Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta; to the right are Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.
In the center there is a banner that, when blown by the wind, cries out: 'Hulubulu, hulubulu!'"
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: The seamless stupa is difficult to see; The clear pool does not permit the blue dragon to coil.
Layer upon layer, falling apart; Round and round, casting shadows. For ten thousand ages, it is shown to people. Yunyan Yin said:
A *stūpa* within a shadowless grove— Its single seam is utterly perplexing. Whenever meeting someone, I wish to pull it out and show it.
"Do you still recognize the old man of Nanyang? Luohan Nan said: "The seamless stūpa stands precariously; its jeweled bells dangle from eight sides.
The Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot touch it; beneath a hundredfold locks, the golden hammer falls.
Baizhang Yuan said: "By whose hand was the seamless stūpa built? Although there is a model, it does not exist."
Worthy of transmission. How can one forcibly write it down when there are no levels? It shall forever hang above the Lapis Lazuli Hall.
Changling Zhuo said: "The seamless stupa remains perfectly round. If you know the essential point, ask Danyuan;
the donor should receive this profound meaning. Bringing the entire earth within, offer a single word."
Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty asked National Teacher Huizhong, "What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies? The Master rose and said, "Do you understand?
The Emperor replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Bring me the pure pitcher for the old monk."
Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty asked National Teacher Huizhong, "What is the samādhi of non-contention?
The Master said, "Donor, you are walking upon the crown of Vairocana. The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Do not mistake this for your own pure dharmakāya.
(In one version, there is a slight variation.)
Xuedou’s verse says: "The Teacher of a Nation is but a strong name; Nanyang alone was permitted to spread his excellent reputation.
The Great Tang supported the true Son of Heaven, Who once trod upon the crown of Vairocana. It further says: "The iron hammer smashes the golden bones;
Between heaven and earth, what else remains? The ocean of three thousand lands is clear and still at night; One does not know..."
"Who enters the Azure Dragon’s cave? Fojian said: "At every step one treads upon the crown of Vairocana; yet this is not one's own pure body.
Wondrously entering the gate of emptiness, one attains the mark of emptiness—the liver and gall of the Patriarchs, the very spirit of the Buddhas."
Daguixiu said: "The author’s pure regulations have no peer in the world; once he grasped the golden pincers atop the Dragon Pavilion.
How excellent it was that he pierced through the crown of Vairocana, until even Mañjuśrī laughed and nodded his head."
Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty asked National Teacher Huizhong, "What Dharma did you obtain at Caoxi?
The Master replied, "Does Your Majesty see a single cloud floating in the sky? The Emperor said, "I see it. The Master said, "It is nailed down and hung there."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said, "A good thing is not as good as having none.
Emperor Zhuangzong of the Tang dynasty asked Chan Master Xinghua Jiang, "I, Your Majesty, have acquired a treasure from Central China, yet there is no one who can appraise its value.
The Master said, "Please let Your Majesty show me this treasure. The Emperor then took both hands and pulled up the ends of his head-wrap (*fuhou*).
[The Emperor] showed it to him. The Master said, "Who would dare to offer a price for the treasure of a sovereign?
The Emperor was greatly pleased. Xuangjue then questioned him: "Tell me, did Xinghua agree with Tongguang or not? If he agreed with him..."
"Where was Xinghua’s eye? If he did not agree with Tongguang, where did the fault lie? Xuedou said:
"What the Most Honored One has attained can only be observed from the sidelines. Had it not been for Xinghua being a master of the Way, he would have likely paid a high price [for his error].
Cuiyan Zhi said: "At that time, Xinghua’s move was truly like being utterly intoxicated."
"How do you resolve this now? Yunfeng Yue said, "The true does not conceal the false; the crooked does not hide the straight.

Those with eyes will discern it. Huanglong Xin said, "Although Xinghua acted according to the occasion on that one instance, how could he avoid burying His Imperial Majesty? Had I been Xinghua at that time, I would have simply addressed him..."
The Way. A pearl from a clam is obtained, yet it has no use; this is to teach him that hereafter he shall have a separate livelihood, so as to avoid mutual stagnation.
Now, if someone were to ask you, Senior, how would you appraise its value?
The *Beitazuo Song* says: "The treasure of the sovereign is truly difficult to repay; Xinghua manifested in form and uttered a word as his strategy.
With both hands he spread out the feet of his head-wrap; the imperial decree was hung upon the Phoenix Pavilion. Baizun Wendu said:
The Prince of the Northern Tribes bends his bow and shoots; the General of the Southern Land looks up to watch.
Upon the sands, nothing remains but a slanting shadow, as it flutters straight into the clouds. Master Yixian of the Upper Hall said: "With palms extended, I present them to you, O Elder Bhikṣu.
How could I dare offer a light price for the Sovereign’s treasure? The entire court is filled with harmony and the Dragon’s countenance is pleased; yet alas, the Hu..."
The monk smiled and nodded his head. Tiantong Jue said: "The sovereign’s matter is spoken for those who know the sound;
the whole world inclines its sincere heart like humble vegetables. He brings forth the priceless treasure of the Central Plains, which is not the same as the jade of Zhao or the gold of Yan."

As soon as the Buddha-mind spoke, the supreme treasure was recovered from the Central Plains; though the entire nation could not contain it, once it fell into the hands of Zhang Xiangru, its glorious fame filled the Great Tang.

The King of Min invited Chan Master Xian of Luoshan to open the hall for formal instruction. As the Master ascended the seat, he gathered up his *saṃghāṭī* robe and said, "Take care," then immediately descended from the seat.
The King of Min stepped forward, took the Master’s hand, and said, "How is this assembly at Vulture Peak any different from today?
The Master replied, "I thought you were just a worldly man."
Dongshan Cóng’s verse says: Luo Shan could not restrain his impatience; He fully displayed the family style with a single roar.
The ink would be as vast as a mountain, yet writing could never exhaust it; Monks, do not seek it within the realm of meaning. Baizhang Yuan said:
Flurries of snow-light shine upon the heavens of Min. The Lord of Min rejoices at this encounter, all the more delighted.
Once the spring breeze blows across the great earth, not a single flake remains before the steps. Shushan said: "Upon the seat of Mount Sumeru, he folds his *kāṣāya*;
from the ocean-mouth, the tidal sound proclaims the Great Function. The Great Donor, Lord of the World, possesses the power of refined discernment; this is the auspicious [legacy] of Vulture Peak."
The assembly was further illuminated.
The King of Min presented a silver bedstead to Xuefeng. A monk asked, "The Master has received such offerings from the Great King;
how will you repay him? The Master pressed both hands against the ground and said, "Strike me lightly! Strike me lightly!"
A monk from Shushan asked Xuefeng, "What was the meaning of your light strike? Shushan said, "A melon-pickle stuck on top of one's head;
the tail hangs down level with the heels."
Fenyang Shanzhao’s Verse says: "Because he asked, 'How does one repay the debt of gratitude to the Lord? Having raised [the question], he gathered it all back and sat upon the essential ford.
If wind and waves stir at the prow of the boat, The flowing sands fill the eyes and no person is seen. Dongshan Chong said:
The King of Men, in his deep faith and respect, sent a bed for delivery. He asked those practicing meditation nearby, "Are you too busy?

One who had begun the work spoke in a low voice, "Strike sparingly. "Who can discern the complete victory within inferiority? Baoning Yong said: "I do not know with what I shall repay the King’s grace.
When the wind rises over the rivers and lakes, the waters wrinkle their faces; a single ancient sail departs on its whim—whom does it accompany?"
He then passed through the Heavenly Gate. Zhengjue Yi said: "One receives an ox from a person, yet returns a horse to that person.

To offer such a thing as a gift is a refined and elegant way of repaying kindness. Nowadays there are many who receive great favors, yet one does not know who among them is the one who repays the debt of gratitude."
The King of Min presented one tangerine and one orange, each sealed in its own package, and dispatched an envoy to deliver them to Xuefeng.
He asked, "Since they are of the same color, why are their names different? Xuefeng returned the packages exactly as they were sealed. The envoy then hurried back to ask Xuansha about it;
Xuansha simply covered both packages with a single sheet of paper.
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: “Mandarins and tangerines, sealed by the King of Min with his own hand; He brought them forth to directly question [the Master] regarding the ‘Wind that Struck the Hu.
The tall man entering the water is clearly present; Yet when he further questioned Xuansha, it was not understood. Fenyang opens the celestial path for you:
The jeweled monastery and golden realms are empty within the azure void. Baoning Yong says: “The King of Min dispatched two kinds [of fruit].”
[The offering] was presented. Xuefeng returned it with a seal. "The human relations between superior and inferior were both perfectly fulfilled;

there was no need to further divide what was already whole. Yanshou said: "When the tangerine is brought forth, there is no need for doubt. For an iron ox to be bitten by a mosquito is surely foolish.
Since the King of Min still does not understand the Master’s intent, I request Xuansha to apply another blow of the awl."
A monk asked Zen Master Touzi Qing, "Master, you have just offered incense to pray for the Emperor’s longevity.
May I ask how many years the current Emperor has lived? The Master replied, "The moon embraces the distant red cassia; the stars bow to the high North Star."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: The six kingdoms are at peace; congratulations on this holy year. The jeweled curtains are drawn high before the bright moon.
How could the Golden Wheel refuse to sit upon the throne? There is no need to strike the still-whip at the vermilion steps.
The minister, Li Ao, the Prefect of Langzhou, had long admired the spiritual influence of Chan Master Yan of Yaoshan. Although he had repeatedly invited him, the Master did not go.

Thereupon, Li Ao entered the mountains specifically to pay his respects; with solemn attire and the etiquette of a guest, he went directly before the Master’s seat. The Master sat upright, looking at a sutra.

He paid no heed at all. Li then said, "To see the person is not as good as hearing of their name. He brushed aside his patched robe and walked away. The Master called out to him; Li turned his head back. The Master said, "How can you hold the ears in honor while treating the eyes with contempt? Li then prostrated himself in homage and asked, "What is the Way? The Master pointed toward the sky and then pointed to the water pitcher, asking, "Do you understand? Li said, "I do not understand. The Master said: [The Master said: "When the great earth is overturned, the blue heavens are revealed. When the blue heavens are overturned, the great earth is revealed. When the great earth and blue heavens are both overturned, the Buddha-Dharma is revealed. Li was greatly enlightened. He bowed and departed. Later, he went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked, "Where have you come from? Li said, "From Baizhang. Mazu asked, "What kind of Dharma did that old fellow teach you? Li said, "He said, 'When the great earth is overturned, the blue heavens are revealed. When the blue heavens are overturned, the great earth is revealed. When the great earth and blue heavens are both overturned, the Buddha-Dharma is revealed. Mazu laughed and said, "Baizhang has a mouth like a bowl, yet he cannot swallow a single grain of rice. Li said, "If it were not for your words, I would have gone back to ask him about this. Mazu said, "Even if you had gone back to ask him, he would have given you the same answer. Li said, "How so? Mazu said, "Because he would have known that you had already heard it from me. Li was greatly enlightened. He bowed and departed. Later, he went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked, "Where have you come from? "Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher. Upon this, Li attained realization and presented this verse: His body has been refined until it resembles the form of a crane;
Beneath a thousand pine trees, he sits with two volumes of scripture. I have come to ask about the Way, with no other business; Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher.
Xuánjué held up the verse and said: "Tell me, does Prefect Li’s statement praise him or clarify him? One must possess the eye of a traveling monk to perceive this.
Fényáng Zhāo composed a verse on it: Clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar; Fearing you would misinterpret them as mere confusion.
Fenyang asked: "Listen, you ghost-souls! Reveal your names through the manifestation of true spiritual power.
Tianning Liang said: "The worthy minister of Longxi ascends Mount Yaoqiao; clouds are in the azure sky, water is in the pitcher. Wind stilled, clouds dispersed, the void is revealed alone;
the jade maiden at the Celestial Gate has never closed the door. Baiyang Shun said: "The ancients asked the Way, and again..."
"What is it said? 'The water is in the jar; the clouds are in the sky. One's native land must be returned to, and upon returning, one finds it:

the clouds and moon at the parting pavilion, the boat at the river crossing. Master Wujin said: "Clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar; the eye follows the pointing finger and falls into a deep pit.
The wildflowers by the stream cannot withstand the bitter frost and wind; what need is there to speak of traveling the bottom of the deep sea?"
Yuantong Xian said: "The clouds are in the blue sky, the water is in the jar; Hand in hand with you, we walk through the crimson heavens.
Before one knows it, the cold night has turned to dawn; A single sheet of red light rises over the sea."
Prefect Li asked Guizong, "In the teachings it is said that Mount Sumeru can contain a mustard seed; I have no doubt about this.
But when it says a mustard seed can contain Mount Sumeru, is that not mere idle talk? The Master said, "People say you, Prefect, have read ten thousand scrolls of books."
"Is this so? [The Master] asked. "How can it be thus? The Master said, "From head to toe, you are no larger than a coconut.
Where would you place ten thousand scrolls of poetry and the classics? Li bowed his head and remained silent.
The *Fohuiquan Song* says: "Releasing the sun and moon reveals their brilliance; Gripping heaven and earth makes them dark.

A single stroke with no turning back— Thorns grow everywhere on the ground. The dragon palaces and ocean treasuries are not many; The sparks of flint and flashes of lightning are not swift. Have you not seen?
Beneath Mount Zixiao, by the side of the ink-well, The Eight Divine Horses, wind-swift as they were, could not catch up."
Heoshan Fang said: "A mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru verifies the patriarchal style; the clear mechanism is distinct, its subtlety inexhaustible.

If you wish to know the origin of the ten thousand scrolls of books, leap out from within the mirror of one's own wisdom. Foxin Cai said: "A mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru—this arouses extraordinary doubt.
Casting aside zither and books, I knock upon the gate of Chan. Suddenly I hear that the ten thousand scrolls cannot conceal it."
In this state, a sudden turn of the divine mechanism is known only to oneself; it is known only to oneself. The red cassia tree is uprooted along with its roots and brought back home.

When Cheng Shangshu and the Great General entered Yunju Mountain to present offerings, they asked Zen Master Ying, "The World-Honored One had a secret word, which Kāśyapa did not conceal. What is the World-Honored One’s secret word? The Master called out, "Shangshu!"
Cheng assented. The Master asked, "Do you understand? Cheng said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand, the World-Honored One has a secret teaching;
if you were to understand, Kāśyapa would have nothing hidden."
Fadeng held up his whisk and said, "Tell me, is that which is called out a secret word? Or is the response a secret word?
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the World-Honored One’s secret word? Fadeng replied, "When did he ever obtain anything secret? Donglin Zong said, "How strange!
For twenty years, Hongjue was like a wild goat hanging from its horns—no tracks, no trace. Yet when..."
Once pressed by the Minister of State, he was left with nothing but water and mud, becoming an object of ridicule and wonder.
Fadelan was like one who lights a golden lamp at noon and splashes ink at midnight. Donglin was not so;
when asked, "What is the secret word? he replied, "Where is it not secret? Tell me, is there any fault in speaking thus?
After a long silence, he said, "There is no need for anyone else. Xingkong replied, "When meeting people, speak only three parts of the truth;
do not yet cast your whole heart out."
An ancient worthy composed a verse: "The World-Honored One’s secret words are difficult to conceal; Kāśyapa, Kāśyapa, sees them as mere dust.
For ten thousand autumns and ten thousand springs, all is dark and vast; The scorched-tailed beast was originally but a tiger."
The Governor of Yingzhou invited Chan Master Fengxue to ascend the seat within the yamen. The Master said:
"The heart-seal of the Patriarchs resembles the mechanism of an iron ox: if it moves, it is sealed; if it stays still, it is broken. What about when it neither moves nor stays still?"
"Sealing is precisely non-sealing. At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "I, so-and-so, possess the faculty of the Iron Ox;
I request the Master not to apply the seal. The Master said, "One who is accustomed to hooking whales and leviathans in the vast depths, yet sighs over the frog-like strides of one stuck in the mud.
Lupi stood there lost in thought. The Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not offer a word? As Lupi hesitated, the Master struck him.

With a single strike of his whisk, the Master said, "Do you still remember the *huatou*? Try to bring it up. As the Provincial Governor (Tai-shou) was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk.
The Governor said, "The Buddha-dharma is fundamentally the same as the royal law. The Master asked, "What principle have you perceived, Provincial Governor?
The Governor replied, "If one hesitates to sever what must be severed, it will instead invite chaos. Thereupon, the Master descended from his seat.
Nantang Jing said: "What a grand battle of Dharma! Does the assembly still wish to recognize Fengxue? His golden arrowhead is seasoned from a hundred battles;
his iron whip is powerful, yet he harbors resentment for lacking an enemy. Do you wish to recognize Elder Lupi?"
It is said that entering the mountains to capture a tiger is easy; it is only when facing the fishing trap that one realizes catching fish is difficult. Do you wish to know the Governor of Yingzhou?
He has already received the good news from the True Man. Between the human realm and the heavens, there is no further doubt.
Xuedou’s verse says: “Having captured Lupi, he mounts the iron ox; The weapons and armor of the Three Mysteries have not yet been lightly requited.
By the waters that flow toward the sea at the foot of King Chu’s city, A single shout once caused them to flow backward.

Baoning said: “The iron-ox mechanism stands like a precipice at the tip of the blade; The precious sword is brandished, its strokes crisscrossing in ten directions. An entire army of rebels is ground to dust.”
The victory song is sung in unison as all returns to peace. Yuanwu said: "The standards of the successive sages never let anything pass.

If you attempt to leap over the iron ox, he strikes your head and shatters it. Lupi was about to cut through [the doubt], yet hesitated; in the flash of lightning and the flight of stars, he was captured alive.
With a shout, his pivot of action was like a thunderclap; the weapons and armor of the Three Mysteries shook the monastic forests. *Tiān* (Heaven).
Tongjue said: "The mechanism of the iron ox—sealing it and breaking the seal—is to transcend the crown of Vairocana’s head and yet come to sit upon the tongue of the transformation Buddha.

Fengxue met his match; Lupi suffered defeat. Within the flash of lightning and the spark from flint, beneath the staff and the shout, every detail is clearly distinguished like a bright pearl on a platter. Yet, even if you raise your eyebrows, you have already missed it."
One day, while Minister Chen Cao was ascending the tower with several officials, he saw several monks passing by. One official remarked, "Those coming here are all traveling monks.
Chen said, "They are not. The official asked, "How do you know they are not? Chen replied, "Wait until they draw near and we shall examine them.
After a short while, the monks arrived before the tower. Chen suddenly called out for the Head Monk (*upādhyāya*), and the monks all raised their heads.
Touwang said to the assembled officials, "Do not disbelieve this.
Weishan Zhe remarked, "Minister Chen may truly be said to hold the sun and moon of Confucius in his hands and wear the golden seal of Vairocana upon his waist.
Not only were the Confucian scholars struck with awe, but even the monastics were left at a loss for words. Have you not heard it said that when the opportunity arises..."
"Like a flash of lightning sweeping by; only then can one avoid the illness of dwelling among the reeds. Tiantong Jue said: "When Minister Chen faced me in person, I pointed it out directly;
he could not deceive Changlu by even a single point."
Xuetang’s Verse of Practice says: A single word leaves the nest; A thousand births emerge from the entanglements. Last night the wind and snow were fierce;
The trees broke before the ancient crags.

When Provincial Inspector Yang Jie entered Baolin Monastery, he inscribed the plaque for the Hall of the Seven Buddhas and asked Chan Master Chang, "What is it like when the Seven Buddhas appear in the world again? The Master replied, "Every time we meet, they are new.
Later, while traveling through the mountains together, Yang picked up the stone used by the Bodhisattva to eat and asked, "Since this is a 'rice-stone,' why can it not be chewed through?"
The Master said, "It is precisely because it is too rigid. Yang said, "It still involves redundant words. The Master asked, "I wonder, how would you do it, Director of Judicial Review?
Yang said, "Rigid. The Master said, "That too is but the second moon."
The Confucian scholar Zhang Zhuo, while reading the *Sūtra of the Names of the Buddhas*, asked Chan Master Chongxian of Changsha,
"I have heard the names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, but I do not know in which lands they dwell. The Master replied, "After Cui Hao inscribed his poem upon the Yellow Crane Tower..."
"Scholar, have you ever composed a verse? He replied, "I have not. The Master said, "Even when there is nothing to do, it is well to compose a verse.
Foyuan Yuan said, "Great assembly, the scholar asked where the Buddha resides. Why did Changsha speak in such a manner?
The scholar usually mocks the wind and sings of the moon; why was he [treated] thus before Changsha?"
"A single word cannot be uttered. If this were the Yellow Crane Tower, what difficulty would there be? Listen as this mountain monk breaks through the mystery for you.
He then said: "His countenance is most wondrous; his radiance illuminates the ten directions. In the past, I made offerings to him."

"Now he has come again to pay his respects. Nantang Jing said, "At that time, had it been Nantang, when he was asked about the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas—'I have only heard their names, but I do not know in which lands they dwell'—he would have simply replied:
'Young scholar, young scholar! Why do you value your ears while disparaging your eyes?'"
Sishin Xin’s verse says: Before the Yellow Crane Tower, in the midst of the Dharma battle, A hundred thousand Buddhas raised their banners of victory.
He has no land; where does he dwell? He leaves behind but one poem of great talent. Lingyuan Qing says:

Hearing the name, one is startled through heaven and earth in an instant. When asked further about his dwelling, he replied that his years were complete. Turning his head, he ascends the path back home;
At every door, the road to Chang’an is revealed. Nanhua Bing said: "Though hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have long heard this name, Where can one seek the adornment of their lands?
If you lack the eye of penetrating clarity before your face, You will again follow along with the boat."
The Master descended to Yangzhou. Heshan Fang said: "Do not seek elsewhere for the sacred traces of the thousand Buddhas;
Changsha’s turning of the pivot has its own source. If you wish to know the place where one cannot hide when facing each other, it is the Yingwu Isle before the Yellow Crane Tower."
Baofeng Ming said: "The names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are merely heard; how could their lands not be manifest and complete?
From this moment on, one does not return, yet upon returning, it is attained. Who can vie for the misty scenery of the five tides? Dahong Sui said: "The poem on Huanghe Lou was inscribed by Cui Hao;
throughout ancient and modern times, no verse has matched its rhyme. The moon’s reflection in the autumn sky over a thousand rivers—"
Seal. In the late spring evening, orioles sing everywhere.
One day Layman Pang stood with his hands folded before Danxia; after a short while, he went out, and Danxia did not look back.
The Master stepped back and sat down. Yunxia then stood before the Master with his hands joined in *añjali* for a short while, then entered the abbot’s quarters.
The Master said, "You enter and I come out; there is still business to be attended to. Yunxia replied, "This old fellow goes in and out—when will it ever end?
The Master remarked, "There is not even a trace of compassion in you. Yunxia said, "I have led this man to such a state. The Master [remained silent].
Xunyun asked, "What do you hold? Xuanze then picked up the layman’s head-wrap (*fuhou*) and said, "He looks just like an old master monk.
The layman then took the head-wrap and placed it on Xuanze's head, saying, "He looks just like a young worldly man. Xuanze responded with three "Yes" (*yingnuo*).
The layman said, "There is still the scent of the past lingering here. Xuanze then cast the head-wrap aside and said, "Great! (Da!)
"It looks like a black silk cap. The Master then responded with three "A-ha! sounds. Yunxia said, "How can you forget your former breaths?
The Master snapped his fingers three times and said, "It moves heaven and it moves earth."
Fojian Qin said: "When Danxia and Old Pang meet in the bustling marketplace, they clasp hands atop a thousand peaks;
when they meet atop a thousand peaks, they clasp hands in the bustling marketplace. It is like a bell on its stand: as it is struck, it emits sound.
Struck with great force, it rings loudly; struck lightly, it sounds softly. The sound does not emerge from within, nor does it come from without."
"Just as before the very first strike, where does the sound reside? Each of you should return to the hall and investigate this for yourselves. Daoyi of Dayue said:
"Dana and Old Pang spend their entire lives roaming through all places with supernatural powers; they pervade the entire world—do you still know this?
The momentum of a thousand peaks ceases at the foot of the mountain; the flow of ten thousand streams returns to the sea."
Rong. The *Tudu Ce* says: "Where it is level and easy, it becomes steep and perilous; where it is severed, it is joined again. Pang Gong knocked at the gate three times;
Danxia struck down [the horse] three times. This may be called 'the wind blowing and the grass bending' or 'the water reaching and the channel forming.'"
Examining this closely: it may be acceptable within the sphere of Buddhist ritual, but it is entirely absent from the domain of the patch-robed monk.
As for what it is like within the domain of the patch-robed monk: the sharp edge of his wit meets you face-to-face like a flash of lightning or a flick of a broom. *Du!* (A shout)
The Verse of Nantang Jing says: "Burning the wooden Buddha—what heart or liver does the old man have? Selling the colander—the master’s house is ruined and his people are scattered.
They chase one another, pursue one another, provoke one another, and sigh for one another. How difficult, how difficult! A long sword leaning against the sky shoots light that chills the Dipper;
A blue dragon stirring the sea does not disturb the waves. Look, look! Every household has a path leading to the Long [Road]."
An. Hu Dingjiao went to visit Chan Master Baoshou Zhao. The Master said, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao? He replied, "I dare not say so.
The Master asked, "Can you nail the void? He replied, "Please have the Master break it open first. The Master then struck him. Hu...
Huangbo said, "Do not strike me by mistake. The Master said, "Later on, you will encounter a talkative teacher who will point it out for you.
Later, Huangbo went to Zhaozhou and raised the previous conversation, asking, "I do not know where my fault lies.
Zhaozhou said, "This very seam is still beyond your control. At these words, Huangbo attained realization. (The *Guangdeng lu* contains minor variations.)
Xuedou Xian said, "I would like to strike these three fellows: first, for Zhaozhou’s failure to blind Hu Dingjiao’s eyes;
second, for Baoshou’s inability to shut Zhaozhou’s mouth; and third, for Hu Dingjiao’s failure to let Baoshou off the hook.
The Master suddenly took up his staff and said, "There is yet another one, O assembly!"
At that moment, [Zhaozhou] retreated in haste. Daowei Zhe then struck the meditation seat once and said:
"Although this fellow managed to avoid the blow, it is a pity for Zhaozhou. At that time, had he waited until the other asked, 'Where does my fault lie?
and then struck him across the spine, he would not only have inherited Baoshou’s majestic radiance, but would also have served as a model and a mirror for the monastic community."
Gushan Gui’s verse says: "A single seam is clearly present; To strike it directly is difficult.
Even if you manage to stitch it with nails and clamps, In the end, it will never be perfectly complete. Jingshan Guo says:

"Even if you were to nail this single seam shut, Upon examination, you would find it is not the work of a master hand. Pitiful, these two old Chan masters, Yet they speak of their family secrets to worldly people."
"Ugly! Zen Master Yunmen Wenyan asked a monk, "Is it not true that 'Luminous, silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges' was spoken by the scholar Zhang Zhuo?
The monk said, "It is. The Master said, "Your words have fallen."
Jingshan Daowei said: "The donkey urinates where it finds the damp ground. Fuan Feng said: "I told you not to travel the road beneath the mountain;
indeed, one hears the heart-rending cry of the monkey. Fayun Xiu said: "Where is the point where the conversation falls? Suddenly, someone asked Fayun:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He simply replied to him: [The text here implies he would have answered with a specific phrase or action].
The talk has slipped away. Do you understand? Those with the true eye must discern this. Yue’an Guo said:
"Master Yunmen spread a celestial net to catch dragons and strike phoenixes. This monk, unaware, fell into his trap and landed within his snare.
If it were Fuyan, it would not be so; as soon as he saw him raise the point, [he would have said], 'Is this not...'"
The words of the scholar Zhang Zhuo: "Just tell him that it is not at all surprising that he has not yet reached Yunmen;
yet even so, it is like drawing one's bow after the thief has already fled."
Heshan Fang’s verse says: "Paths crisscrossing, one attains freedom; The sturdy gate is turned, the wondrous fully gathered.
Within this, the secret meaning is hard for people to grasp; With a shout, one must cause the waters to flow backward. Yue’an Guo says:
Ten-thousand-foot Dragon Gate, its momentum leaning against the void; Letting go at the precipice, one discerns the fish and the dragon.
People of this age look only upon the fishing line, Failing to see the reeds facing the red smartweed. Shushan said: "Questioning and answering come and go without partiality;
how can one pass through the iron walls and silver mountains? When seizing and releasing occur according to the occasion, speech falls into error, thereby causing thousands..."
Ancient movements stir the mournful wind.
*Chanlin Leiju*, Volume One;
*Chanlin Leiju*, Volume Two.
The Buddhas and Patriarchs, the Dharma-body, the Buddha-image:
as soon as the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, walked seven steps, and looked around.
Shifang said, "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.
Yunmen said, "Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to a dog, so as to ensure peace throughout the world.
Xuedou said, "I would have immediately overturned the meditation seat. Fayan said, "Yunmen..."
The momentum is indeed great, yet it nonetheless lacks the principles of the Buddha-dharma. At that time, an elder monk spoke on his behalf, saying:
"I thought there was no one to bear witness. Xuedou further commented: "The hook is in the ground of non-suspicion. Lanxi Jue said:
"Yunmen may truly be said to offer this profound mind to the dust-motes and lands; this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness."
Yunfeng Yue said: "Although Yunmen possesses a strategy for settling chaos, he lacks a way to emerge from it himself.
If you can discern this, I will grant that you possess the single eye atop your head."
Dongshan Chong’s verse says: "The eighth day of the fourth month, the Buddha’s birthday; Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth, he declared himself foremost.
Nine dragons spout water to bathe his golden body: Mahāprajñāpāramitā. Quandai Dao said:
Pointing to heaven, pointing to earth, his words ring out clearly. Passing on words and transmitting messages, he emerges from the painted hall.
The messenger still possesses great spirit; the host must surely be extraordinary. Baoning Yong said: "Before the primordial chaos was divided, people were unaware;
as soon as heaven and earth were split apart, the affairs [within] became manifest. Heaven-begotten skill is able to be strange and marvelous; at the end, it yields."
He put on a performance. Master Wujin said: "Taking seven steps and pointing at the heavens—under the staff of a monk, his illness is hard to cure.
What was accomplished after emerging from the mother’s womb? How does that compare to before he had descended upon Jambudvīpa?"
Jingshan Daokai said: "This old fellow was in a hurry as soon as he was born;
taking seven steps like one who has gone mad, he deceives countless foolish men and women, opening his eyes wide as he enters the boiling cauldron. Cishou Shen said:
A single fire casts the golden ball; its perfect roundness costs nothing in tongs or hammer.
Picked up and cast from the crest of a ten-thousand-fathom peak, it strikes down the white phoenix from the edge of heaven.
The World-Honored One had not yet departed from Tuṣita before descending into the royal palace; he had not yet emerged from his mother’s womb before his work of saving sentient beings was complete.
Gushan Gui’s verse says: "He enters crosswise into the sea of right and wrong; he walks with sovereign ease amidst packs of jackals and tigers."
Do not bring right and wrong to judge me; my lifelong probing and analysis are irrelevant to this. Jingshan Daowu said:
"The sharp blade has honey, but there is no need to lick it; in a house of venomous insects, do not taste the water.
By neither licking nor tasting, one avoids transgression; composed, one returns home in brocade."

Wuzu Yan said: "O assembly, let the Bodhisattva Anantagātra’s verse cease for a moment.
Do you all understand how to measure yourselves? If I were to ask the old monk to measure himself, there would simply be no place to begin.

Have you not seen the ancient saying: 'Measuring the Buddha’s seat, his merit is difficult to fathom; offering incense in a small cup, purple clouds gather thickly'? What [is it that cannot be measured]?"
Therefore, such a distinction constitutes a unique springtime for this house.
Zen Master Nanquan Yuan was once asked by Grand Officer Lu Xuan: "In my home, I have a large stone that I have both sat upon and lain upon.
If I were now to have it carved into a Buddha, would that be permissible? The Master said, "It is permissible; it is permissible. Lu...
Yunmo asked, "Is it not so? The Master said, "It is not so; it is not so.
Yunyan said, "When sitting, one is a Buddha; when not sitting, one is not a Buddha. Dongshan said, "When not sitting, one is a Buddha."
"If one is sitting, one is not the Buddha. Baofu Zhan said, "Nanquan was looking at the tower and hitting the tower;
Yunyan and Dongshan were one rising and one falling. Wuzu Jie said, "Nanquan only knew how to change the wind, but did not know how to transform the customs."
Yunyan and Dongshan were dreaming within a dream. Huiqiu Long said: "Although Nanquan was like a mirror that reflects forms at its edge—Hu coming, Hu appears;
Han coming, Han appears—it simply does not admit of critical examination. At that time, had he waited for him to say:
'In my home there is a piece of stone; I have sat upon it and I have lain upon it. I wish to carve it into...'"
“Did the Buddha attain it? [The Master] replied directly: “Do not begrudge your lofty reputation; carve it upon stone.
Vimalakīrti exhausted his heart-mind at this moment. Tiantong Jue said: “To turn function into position, and to turn position into function—this belongs to the masters of the Dongshan lineage.
But tell me, what was Nanquan’s intention? Truly, no needle or awl can penetrate it.”
Chan Master Zhentu Zhenru’s verse says: “Whether attained or not attained, heaven is vast and earth is narrow; whether sitting, lying, or walking, there is no need for doubt.
Zhengjue Yi says: “If you have attained it, you can speak of it; if you have not attained it, you still cannot speak of it.”
"Lord White—when was he ever white? Lord Black—is he truly black? Master Wang of Guichi is the thief among thieves in all the world.
The Great Thief, Dafu Xiangjian, once picked him up. Huanglong Zhen said: "Nanquan obtained it intentionally; how could it be otherwise than not obtaining it?
A virtuous person and a gentleman—their deportment is never errant. Foyan Yuan said: "He personally followed his family..."
Coming from within, what is there in the house? I hold this single stone, vast, firm, and enduring.
Once offered to the Buddha on Vulture Peak, Śakra now merely lifts it with his hand. What does it produce from within the heart? Peace, happiness, and long life.
Once, when Chan Master Danxia Ran visited Huilin Temple in Luoyang, it happened that the weather was bitterly cold.
He consequently took some wooden Buddhas from within the hall and burned them for a fire. The temple steward happened to see this and rebuked him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddhas?
The Master used his staff to stir the ashes and said, "I am burning for their relics (*śarīra*). The steward replied, "Wooden Buddhas—how could they have any relics? The Master said, "Since..."
There were no relics. He requested two more statues and burned them again. Subsequently, the abbot’s eyebrows and beard fell out.
Touzi Qing said, "He did not know how to act as a guest; he needlessly troubled the host.

Ying'an Hua said, "The masters of various quarters deliberate on this, saying that the abbot suddenly gave rise to doubt and thus brought about this calamity. Others say it was because the weather was cold."
He did not heed Danxia’s advice regarding the fire, resulting in the wooden Buddha being burned to ashes and his own eyebrows and beard falling off.
Little did he know that the temple administrator had traded iron for gold—a truly magnificent stroke of fortune.
The Layman Wujin composed a verse: "Snow blocks the mountain gate; frozen, it knows no spring. A single wooden Buddha is split for firewood.
Where the eyes move, the eyebrows fall— For slandering the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.

Touzi Qian said: "The ancient crags are sealed by moss, cold seeps through the door. Birds flying are startled by the peril; beasts running are lost in confusion. Deep in the night, the chill and heat..."
**Tingzhou Huo: "The fishermen are busy at dawn, suspecting [the fire] themselves."** Fodeng Xun said:
"Old Danxia burned the wooden Buddha; the head monk’s eyebrows and beard were just singed. His transgression was always his own doing.
Who says that a thousand falsehoods cannot be traded for one truth? Chuan'an Fang said: "Facing him directly, the upward-moving mechanism is difficult to conceal. This is the ancestral wind."
A gift bestowed upon people for a thousand ages; through layer upon layer of silver mountains and iron walls, one must penetrate them all. It is thanks to the Abbot of Danxia who understood this.
When Chan Master Changzi Kuang first visited Shitou, Shitou asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the summit of Mount Dayu.
Shitou said, "Has the 'single scroll of merit' at the summit of Mount Dayu been completed yet? The Master replied, "It was completed long ago."
"It is so; it only lacks a dot in the eye. [The Master] asked, "Do you not wish for me to dot your eye? The Master said, "Please do so immediately.
Shitou lowered one foot. The Master then prostrated. Shitou asked, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate? The Master replied, "Like a single drop of snow upon a red-hot furnace."
Xuánjué said: "Tell me, does Zhāngzī answer with eyes, or does he answer without eyes?
If he has eyes, why did he ask for his eyes to be opened? If he does not have eyes, it is also said that he has long since achieved them.
How do you resolve this? Fǎdēng spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master may be said to have dimmed vision. Xuědòu Xiǎn said: [He is right.]
"What point is there in the merit of eyeless [images]? Nanhua Bing said: "To call it 'one set of merit' is already a forced designation.
Shitou let down one foot; Changzi said: "It is like a single speck of snow upon a red-hot furnace—this only reveals more leakage.
Nevertheless, although the road at Jiegao is perilous, the traveler at night proceeds even further.
Many. Baoning Yong’s verse says: "A single set of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes; though fully completed, the consecration has not yet been performed.
Behold how spiritual powers manifest beneath the brush; there are further traces of the numinous in the realm above. Tiantong Jue said:
The Eye of Merit atop the Ridge: weary feet casually dangle down. A single snowflake on a red furnace—immediately, all dependence is cleared away.
Master Wujin said: "The old Stonehead is refined and extraordinary; from the tip of his brush he paints forth the Buddha’s two eyes.
On the broken rope bed he casually lets his feet hang down; two divine rays of light are not withdrawn at night. Zhihai.
Chongqing Yun said: "Long-bearded one, you have not yet come from Lingnan; your merit is fully perfected and your eyes are already open. Cherish this place where Sudhana turned his head back;
Mañjuśrī has never descended from the pavilion. Cotang Qing said: "Tearing through the grass and observing the wind, he arrived at Shitou;
the mountain passes are layered and the road is far and winding. On the summit of the ridge, merit has long been perfected. One.

When National Preceptor Huangbo Yun was with Minister Pei, the latter presented a statue before the Master and knelt, saying, "I beg the Master to bestow a name upon it.
The Master called out, "Pei Xiu! Pei responded. The Master said, "I have finished bestowing the name upon you. Pei bowed in reverence.
Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of Prime Minister Pei, gave a shout at that very moment.
Fengyang Zhao’s verse says: "Kneeling before the Master, he entreated him to bestow a name; suddenly, at the vanguard of the encounter, he let out a cry."
If it were not Lord Pei, who would dare respond? It is enough to make even the deaf and blind open their ears. Foyin Yuan said:
"When Lord Pei was in that moment, he had forgotten his name; when called by others, he became alert again.
One does not know what existed before the formation of the fetus—dare anyone defile this numinous nature? Baoning Yong said: "Adorned with the five colors, she comes with her palms joined."
Shangqing said: "The old barbarian has only just established empty names. If you now wish to transcend all the patriarchs, you must proceed upon the Vajra Peak.
Ctang Qing said: "It is not mind, nor is it Buddha. Huangbo calls it out—what thing is this?
From this, Lord Pei recognized empty names; the monks of the world cannot leap out of them."
Chu Anfang said: "Holding it up before him to request his name, Huangbo called out from on high once;
thus he revealed his true face from the past, and from this point forward, he was able to assist in purifying the national style."
When Prime Minister Pei entered Da’an Temple and saw a portrait of a high monk on the wall, he asked the abbot, "The true likeness is worthy of contemplation;
where is that high monk? The abbot was speechless. Pei said, "Is there no Zen monk here?
The abbot replied, "Recently there has been a monk who came to this temple to perform manual labor; he bears much the likeness of a Zen monk—he must be your teacher. Pei—

He was summoned to appear. They discussed their previous conversation, and the Master said, "I request that Your Excellency pose a question. Pei replied, "The true countenance can be beheld; where is the eminent monk?
The Master called out, "Your Excellency! Pei responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Where is the eminent monk? At these words, Pei attained great enlightenment.
Ying’an Hua said: "O Great Assembly! Huangbo spreads his all-encompassing net to strike the leaping, scaled dragons;
Minister Pei sits at his strategic table within the tent, yet he need not hesitate to achieve victory a thousand miles away.
If you can see this clearly and with unimpeded discernment, you may truly be called 'the present as the past. If it is otherwise, then the three-foot dragon-spring sword [will settle the matter]."
The light shines upon the gallbladder; amidst a crowd of ten thousand men, one seizes the high banner.
Chan Master Zhaozhou Shen addressed the assembly, saying: "The clay Buddha does not cross water; the gold Buddha does not cross the furnace;
the wood Buddha does not cross fire."
Baizhang Yuan said: "O Great Assembly! Old Man Zhaozhou’s twelve joints of bone and eighty-four thousand pores have all been cast into your laps at once.
Today, Yuantong, seeing injustice on the road, speaks out for the sake of the ancients.
He strikes the meditation seat with his hand and says: "You must know that the seas and mountains return..."
The enlightened ruler has not yet believed; heaven and earth have ensnared the virtuous man.
*Can*. Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "The clay Buddha does not cross the water; the divine light illuminates heaven and earth.

If one continues to stand in the snow without ceasing, who would not polish away their artifice? The golden Buddha does not enter the furnace; someone comes to visit Zihu. [He counts] the characters on the plaque."
This single word: Where is there no pure breeze? A wooden Buddha does not cross the fire; one must always think of Po-zao-t’uo.
When the staff suddenly strikes home, only then do you realize you have betrayed me. Baizhang Yuan said: "Cast away the clay Buddha and the gold-and-wood Buddha;

Just one sudden strike. Guishan Gui said: "The golden buddha, the wooden buddha, and the clay buddha—passing through the furnace, passing through water, and passing through fire—all enter Zhaozhou’s red furnace.

Monasteries.

As the World-Honored One was traveling with his assembly, he pointed to the ground with his finger and said, "A Buddhist monastery (*brahmacarya-śālā*) should be established at this spot. Śakra [the King of Devas]... [will provide it].
Placing a single blade of grass upon the ground, he said, "The construction of the Brahma-pavilion is now complete. The World-Honored One smiled.
The Celestial Youth Jue composed a verse: "Upon the tips of a hundred blades of grass, boundless spring; Picking it up with a casual hand, its use is intimate."
The sixteen-foot golden body, a mass of merit and virtue, casually takes hands and enters the red dust of the world. Amidst the dust he acts as master;
beyond transformation he comes as a guest. In every place his livelihood is sufficient according to his lot; he does not begrudge that his skillful means are no inferior to others.
When Master Wuzhuo went to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, he took his leave. Mañjuśrī commanded the youth Kuntī to escort him out the gate.
The Master asked, "What is the name of this monastery? The youth pointed behind the Vajra [statue].
The Master turned his head; the temple and the boy vanished together. Only the wild grasses and the empty valley remained.
Dongshan said, "If you wish to observe the father, first observe the son. Wujixing said, "This is a matter for brothers to accomplish together.
Do you understand? When the holy temple suddenly vanished, Wuzhuo’s own eye was directly realized."
[The door] opened. When the youth called out three times, the number was fully accounted for.
Mingzhao Qian composed a verse: "The sacred monastery extends throughout the dharma-realm; Manjusri fills my eyes as we engage in conversation."
Under these words, one does not know how to open the Buddha-eye; turning one’s head, one sees only the green mountain crags. Zhengjue Yi said:
"The temple plaque suddenly shines at the tip of the finger; even the thousand eyes of Mahākaruṇā cannot behold it.
Since first glimpsing the back of the Vajra, until this very day, I have served as a wild cook. Foyin Yuan said: "Though the pavilions have plaques,"
There is nothing at all. Let us try asking the stubborn child who arose at the beginning of the kalpa: Suddenly pointing to the vajra, he looks behind him.
As years grow old, one is often mocked by ghosts. Daowu Zhen said: "The three threes before and after—how many are there? The Great Matter shines with brilliant clarity.
Turning the head, one sees no one who understands emptiness; white clouds fill the eyes as one lies in the wild grass."
Chan Master Zhaozhou Shen asked a monk, "What is a pure monastery? The master said, "A girl with horns.
The monk asked, "Who is within the monastery? The master said, "A girl with horns is pregnant."
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: "Across the chest and cradling the belly, he harbors the dragon seed; Carving his gall and exposing his liver, he touches the phoenix embryo.
Do not say this child is easily obtained; Know that he comes from the depths of agonizing pain. Haoyin Xin says:
"Ha! This old fellow Jie has been so talkative that he has leaked the secrets of this pure monastery all at once.
At the gate of Vajra, there is laughter; within the Hall of Bodhisattvas, there is a sobbing voice. An ancient worthy said:
"Though the monastery is eternally pure, the horned youth conceives in her womb and knows no shame. When there is no spirit, she adds spirit; when there is no wind..."
This is the place where the current flows;
it is a site of refined style. Zen Master Ming of Xiyuan was once asked by a monk, "What is the monastery? The Master said, "A thicket of brambles.
The monk asked, "Who are the people within the monastery? The Master said, "Badgers and otters."
Yuanwu Keqin’s verse says: Not a hair’s breadth left behind, moving freely in all directions. Beyond the threshold lies the vast sky; the Great Space is wide and open.

Roaming at ease within this boundlessness, clear and bright is the meaning of the Patriarchs. Clear and bright is the tip of every blade of grass. Tearing asunder the net of doubt, cutting off the river of craving.
Even if one possessed the power to turn back heaven, how could it compare to resting directly here and now? The Four Crossroads.
On the path, pure and naked; he lets loose the water-buffalo of Guishan.
Chan Master Cheshen of Shimen was asked by a monk, "What is the formless place of practice? The Master said, "The moon shines and the waters are clear;
the green mountains have no divergent paths. [The monk] asked, "Who is the person within the place of practice? The Master said, "I am now speaking to you."
He said, "Do you understand?
Master Dayang Jian was asked by a monk, "What is the formless site of enlightenment? The Master replied, "Not sitting beneath the Bodhi tree;
wandering toward the Snowy Mountains. He also said, "Hanging banners inside the Buddha hall."
A monk asked Chan Master Bao’ai of Mount Shan, “Who resides in this single room, leakless house? The Master said, “No one;
there is nothing that hangs upon the body. The monk asked, “Is there still a position [of abiding]? The Master said, “Not dwelling.”
Chan Master Jinfeng Zhi was once asked by Caoshan, "What have you been doing? The Master replied, "I have been building a house.
Caoshan asked, "Is it finished yet? The Master said, "It is finished. Caoshan said, "That side of the matter is finished, but what about that other side?
The Master said, "I shall wait for one day to report back to the Master. Caoshan said, "So it is, so it is."

Regarding the Hall:
Zen Master Datong of Touzi was asked by a monk, "What is the Hall of the Empty King? The Master said, "It cannot be established."
Chan Master Xuefeng Cunen was asked by a monk, "What is the Hall of the Empty King? The Master said, "Big and small.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha of the Empty King? The Master said, "What is it?"
Chan Master Yunmen Wenyan was asked by a monk, "What is it like when there is no Buddha in the ancient hall? The Master said, "From where does the Brahma-sound come?
Nantang Jing composed this verse: The ancient hall has no Buddha; from where does the Brahma-sound come? Awakening through a call in a dream, the gates of the pavilions open.
A single point of numinous light is free from all dust; Shining through antiquity and soaring into the present, it pervades the nine realms.
Chan Master Yong of Nanyuan was asked by a monk, "What is it like when an ancient hall is restored? The Master said, "The roof-tiles of the bright hall reach down to the eaves.
The monk said, "In that case, the adornments are fully complete. The Master said, "When the grass is cut, the snake's head falls."
An ancient worthy sang: "The mechanism of granting and revoking—how can it be fathomed? To give rise to understanding based on words is truly pitiable.
At dawn, a gust of spring wind arises, Blowing down three or four branches from the courtyard."
When Chan Master Deshan Xuanjian was traveling on pilgrimage, he arrived at Guishan carrying his double-layered robe.
He went straight up to the Dharma Hall, walking from west to east and from east to west, surveying the abbot’s quarters. Guishan paid him no heed.

The Master said, "No, no," and then departed. (Xuedou Xian added a comment: "He has been thoroughly scrutinized. Upon reaching the gate, the Master turned back and said, "Nor should one be so hasty," and then prepared [to enter].
With dignified deportment, he entered again for an audience. As soon as he stepped across the threshold, he held up his sitting cloth (*zuoju*) and called out, "Preceptor!

As Guishan was about to take up his whisk, the Master gave a shout and swept his sleeve out of the hall. (Dong said: "He has seen through him. That evening, Guishan asked the Head Seat, "Is the newcomer still here today?
