The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "When Deshan was a thief, his heart was full of trepidation; when Guishan was a thief, he drew his bow after the robbery.
Jingshan Daoyuan said: "If these two venerable elders met in such a manner, each would lose one eye."
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: One penetration, two penetrations—adding frost upon snow, having nearly fallen into peril.
The Flying Cavalry General enters the barbarian court; how many can emerge completely unscathed? Rush past quickly! Do not let him pass!

Sitting amidst the grass on the summit of a solitary peak. Shangfang Yi said: "Stealing the camp and cutting through the fortifications to enter the central army—this must be a fully perfected stratagem.
Yet the golden mallet in his sleeve has not yet been moved; before the mountain, the cavalry gallop away in profusion. Haiyin Xin said:
"In the deep forest of the tiger’s den, no man reaches it. Those who do reach it must surely be—"
The Hunter: The tiger was startled from its sleep and only just raised its eyes; with a swift leap, it escaped with its life. Fojian Qin said:
"Old Deshan was a master of the Dharma-battle. With a single shout, his voice and radiance roared like thunder and lightning.
To mount the tiger’s head and gather up its tail—to stroke the tiger’s whiskers—this is truly enviable. He rushed down the mountain thirty li in haste, yet he was again..."
Shishuang pursued [the thief] with an arrow.
Chan Master Xuefeng Cun addressed the assembly, saying: "I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion;
I have already met you at Wushan Ridge; I have already met you before the Sangha Hall. Later, Baofu asked:
At Geohu, [the master] said, "Let us meet at the front of the Sangha Hall. "Where shall we meet at Wangzhou Pavilion or Wushan Ridge?
Geohu strode back to the Abbot’s quarters. Baofu immediately lowered his head and entered the Sangha Hall.
Dongchan Zhai said: "Do these two venerable masters meet? Do they see one another or not? Try to judge this. Xuedou Xian said:
"The two elders were indeed correct, yet they only knew how Xuefeng let go; they did not see how Xuefeng held fast.
Suppose a monk were to come forth and ask: 'I wonder, what would Xuedou say? How could it be otherwise?"
"This is not some fellow who merely recognizes auspicious or inauspicious signs through various skillful means.
Is there any monk here who has met him at Wangzhou Pavilion or Wushan Ridge? After a long silence, he said: "Board-carrying Chan practitioners are as numerous as hemp and millet.
Jianfu Xin said: "The ancients were like this; they had only waves that followed the current, but no surging waves against the wind."
Baolin Yuan said: "Xuefeng met [his disciples] at three places; Baofu questioned people at two places;
and Ehu only knew how to hold fast but did not know how to let go. If someone were to ask Baolin, 'At which of these places—Wushiling or Wangzhouting—did you meet them?
he would immediately strike them across the face with his hand. Waiting for them to hesitate, he would then take up his staff and drive them out."
There are three gates. For now, I shall circulate this dialogue with Xuefeng.
Fengyang Zhao’s verse says: "At Wangzhou, Wushan, and before the hall, we meet and encounter one another in myriads."
"Only Goose Lake and Baofu / At this moment meet; they understand the shifting flow. Haoyin Xin said:
"Wangzhou and Wushan constantly meet; / Why do Zen practitioners turn their backs?
Baofu and Goose Lake, though they attained the meaning, / Have never yet deployed their banners when marshaling the troops. Foyan Yuan said: "Secretly, secretly; grandly, grandly; already..."
Two or three. Originally there was nothing; what more could there be? When a fool sees this, he gives rise to joy;
when a practitioner encounters it, his face is full of shame. Jingshan Gao said: "Wangzhou, Wushi, and the Sangha Hall—these karmic consciousnesses are so frantic they cannot be endured.
When the monk’s staff is raised, the five lakes and four seas boil like hot water."
Dahong then said: "Climbing mountains and crossing waters—how much toil! Meeting by chance to inquire about the path.
How laughable is the scholar Pan of Mount Hua, riding his donkey backward on the road to Chang'an."
When a monk asked Chan Master Yunju Jian, "What is it like when one dwells alone on a solitary peak? the Master said, "The seven bays of the monks' hall are left empty;
who taught you to dwell alone on a solitary peak?"
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "Spontaneous and not cultivated, fundamentally perfected; In ordinary response, it is most clear.
He points directly to the road to Chang’an, Yet travelers are unwilling to walk it."
At Sushan, when the administrative monk had finished constructing a memorial stupa for Master Ren and came to inform him, the Master asked, "How much money did you give to the craftsmen?
The monk replied, "Everything was at the disposal of the Abbot. The Master said, "I gave them only three coins."
"I will give him some money. "Shall I give him two coins? "Or shall I give him one coin? "If he can speak [the Dharma], I will build a stupa for you with my own hands.
The monk had no reply. Later, another monk went to Da Ling (i.e., Luoshan) and brought up the previous conversation.
Da Ling asked, "Has anyone been able to speak it yet? He replied, "No one has yet. Da Ling said, "When you return, report this to Shu."
Shandao. Daling said, "If you give him three coins, Master, you will certainly not obtain a pagoda for the rest of your life.
If you give him two coins, you and the craftsman will have produced it with one and the same hand.
If you give him one coin, you will cause the craftsman’s eyebrows and whiskers to fall out. The monk returned and reported this to Shushan, who assumed a formal demeanor.
Gazing afar at the Great Ridge, he prostrated and sighed, saying: "I thought there was no one here; yet the Ancient Buddha of the Great Ridge has emitted light that shoots across this place.
Although it is so, it is still like a lotus flower in the eleventh month. Upon hearing this, Daling later remarked:
"For me to speak in such a manner is already like a tortoise's hair three feet long."
Fushan Yuan said: "Shushan used a chisel to pierce the earth; Daling used a knife to carve out space.

Although these two ancient worthies applied their chisels and knives in error, people of the present day find it difficult even to conceive of a way to respond. Why? Because within their subsequent words there is both inclusion and exclusion.
Nevertheless, though this is so, one must fish for the money lost in the river from within the river itself. Wu’an Keqin said:
In all directions, those who practice share the same wind; from ten thousand streams, waters flow toward the source, and a thousand paths follow the same track.
The Venerable Master Chen often said: "This old monk possesses but a single sword. Beneath this sword lies the intent to kill, yet there is also the path of manifold manifestations.
Observe how he employs it to cut and sever—how unimpeded and brilliant it is on all eight sides! Were it not for this, [it would be nothing].
Shushan’s assessment was comprehensive; who could fail to see that he possessed the resonance of metal and jade?
As for his saying, "If you give him three coins, Master, you will certainly not obtain a pagoda in this life"—it would be a case of laboring without merit.
"If you give him two coins," he said, "the Master and the craftsman will share a single hand, yet one cannot avoid being mired in the mud."
"Carrying water. If you were to give him even a single coin, it would cause the artisan’s eyebrows and whiskers to fall out, such that he could not even manage to splash the water.
Shushan said: 'This too is a lotus flower in the eleventh month. The land is vast and the people are few. Daying said:
'It is already like a tortoise's hair three feet long; there is both the sword that kills and the sword that gives life. O Assembly! "
Tell me, after all, what matter is being clarified? "A lion turning over—everyone look! Fodeng Xun said:
"Shushan emptied his bag to express his gratitude, yet alas, there was still an inch left on the ruler. This monk knew only how to build a pagoda;
it turns out there were no stars on the tail of the scale. At Daling, three coins and two coppers were enough to break through without difficulty. Huiri.
If you were this monk, when Shushan spoke in such a manner, you should simply have replied, "Today my efforts have not been in vain.

Had you produced such a phrase, you would have avoided being disturbed for a lifetime by three or two strings of cash, and you would not have allowed Shushan to broadcast your family’s disgrace abroad.
But as for that lotus flower in the twelfth month and the three-foot-long hair of a tortoise—how do you deal with that?

During the time of the World-Honored One, there was a bhikṣu of dull faculties who lacked the nature of great learning. He was instructed to recite the two characters "tiáo" (broom) and "zhǒu" (broom).
Day and night he recited them; when he recited "tiáo," he forgot "zhǒu," and when he recited "zhǒu," he forgot "tiáo. Every day he reproached himself without ceasing.
One day, as he suddenly recited the two characters "tiáo" and "zhǒu," he attained great enlightenment.

When the Fourth Patriarch, Master Xinxing, was a śrāmaṇera, he paid obeisance to the Third Patriarch and asked, “I pray that the Upādhyāya, out of compassion, will grant me the Dharma-gate of liberation.
The Patriarch said, “Who has bound you? The Master replied, “No one has bound me. The Patriarch said, “Why then do you seek liberation?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. He served him diligently for nine years, after which the robe and Dharma were transmitted to him. He resided at Qizhou.
At Mount Pòtóu, disciples gathered like clouds. They restrained their minds and did not sleep, their ribs never touching the mats.

One day he addressed the assembly, saying, "During the Wǔdé era, while traveling to Mount Lúshān, I gazed upon Mount Pòtóu and saw purple vapors like a canopy, beneath which white vapors were divided into six horizontal paths.
Do you understand this, or not? The assembly remained silent. Huìróng said, "Could this not be the Master’s future [reputation]?"

"Does this not constitute a branch of the Buddha-dharma that has emerged crosswise? The Master said, "Excellent. Emperor Taizong of the Tang dynasty was moved by the Master's Way; though he issued three edicts, the Master did not rise [to accept office].

Consequently, the Emperor bestowed upon him purple robes. Wooden Hermit Yong said: "Behold how the Patriarch, acting for the sake of others, pulls out nails, extracts wedges, unties adhesions, and removes bonds—altogether..."
Do not wound your fingertips or soil your hands; this may be called a single drop of lion’s milk that scatters ten *hu* of donkey’s milk.
You must by no means give rise to arbitrary mental calculations or various intellectual interpretations. Suddenly, seek it at the base of your feet until you find its place of descent;
with a single stroke of the sword held before you, bring it directly to completion.
The son of Wuwei (Wuwei Zi) offered this verse: "The Stupa of Compassionate Clouds, the Master of the Great Physician— Behold it, look up to it;
the two peaks stand towering high. Lanrong could not obtain the Western-coming bowl; It was bestowed directly upon the child on the road to Huangmei.
Cangtang Qing said: "The Way transcends heaven and earth and moves the Supreme One. Though summoned three times by flying letters, he did not leave the clouds. He sought a person..."
The heir of the Zhou family gazes afar at the purple mists of Ox-Head Mountain. Ancient Buddha Min said: "Neither bound nor released;
the side never touches the mat—clearly, it is a single thread running through. Two five-hundred-pieces [of gold]. Foguo Bai said:
"Meeting the Master beyond the birds, he unties his bonds and returns; beneath the Double Peak Mountain, solitary and sublime, he takes up the robe and bowl to benefit others."
[The Master] said: "I am giving this little boy of Huangmei to you. Juefan Hong said: "It is well known that fame and traces can obstruct the Way;
I fear even a formal lineage may burden a person. You who ask about the Dharma, young novice, do not be so talkative.
This hundred-year journey as a guest requires one to blend with the dust of the world. Yunyan added: "Before Niu-tou was born, the plum was already ripe. (From *Wanbu ren*)

In the interval, the pond was completed beneath the moon; the imperial summons arrived three times, yet he remained too weary to open his eyes. At the summit of White Lotus Peak, the radiance shone back and forth.
When Chan Master Jichuan of Panshan first went to attend upon Mazu, he served as a street-walker. One day, as he stepped out the gate, he saw people carrying a funeral bier.
The singer struck the bell and sang: "The red wheel is certain to sink in the west; I know not to which direction the soul shall go.
Beneath the curtain, the sons of filial piety wailed with mournful cries. Suddenly, the Master’s body and mind leaped up in joy as he attained realization. Upon returning, he related this to Mazu.
The Patriarch (Zhaozhou) gave his seal of approval.
A verse by Wenshu Dao says: "The sound of song winds around, the sound of weeping is mournful; It makes one laugh to death—the old, ancient sage of Panshan.
In the dark and murky places of ignorance throughout kalpas, All at once, sudden awakening sends forth radiance. Meng’an Xin says:
In response to this lamentation, one simply accepts it; after all, when has anything ever gone to another place?
With spontaneous exultation, the whole body is revealed, and one finally knows that the entire realm has never been hidden. Fodeng Xun said: "The red sun is certain to sink in the west;
I do not yet know where the soul has gone. When one treads upon the land of one's native home, the original face is stable."
The eyes are one's own mother; the person is simply here, never having perished. On the Tuṣita Heaven it is not like the human world;
you must know that there is a different way of thinking.
Once Panshan was walking through a marketplace and saw a guest buying pork, saying to the butcher: "The finest cuts."
"Bring me one catty. The butcher set down his knife and folded his hands, saying, "District Magistrate, which of these is not refined?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Nanhuabing’s verse says: "This matter is clear and not concealed; In every instance and every thing, they accord naturally.
A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them; Yet they follow the warbling orioles over the low wall."
When Chan Master Wuxie Mo arrived at the place of Shitou, he said, "If our words accord, I shall stay; if they do not accord, I shall depart.
Shitou remained seated as usual. The Master then walked away. Shitou called out after him, "Dharma brother! Dharma brother! The Master turned his head back, and Shitou said:
"From birth until death, it is only this very thing. Why turn your head and twist your brain? The Master suddenly attained awakening and broke his staff in two.
Dongshan said, "At that time, had it not been for Wuxie, my late teacher, it would have been difficult to uphold. Nevertheless, even so..."
It is as if one were still on the road. Changqing said, "Dangerous. Cuoyan Zhi said, "Shitou sat down; Wuxie departed immediately.
Shitou called after him, which resulted in a great deal of trouble. Yunfeng Yue said, "Big or small, Shitou could not sit still nor hold fast.
For a fellow like this who carries a wooden board, once he has been let go, he should have left it at that; why did he call him back?"
[The Master] turned away. He had been deluded by him, claiming, "I have attained enlightenment here. It is like dreaming of such a thing on a donkey-year [an eternity].
Foyuan of Fuyan wrote a verse on this: "On the road or at home, how can one repay? Do not seek the former master as a mere precedent."
Majestic as the universe, like a sovereign king, yet he could not avoid being half-devoid of a skull. Kumoku said:
"If one wishes to go, call out loudly to bring him back; at that moment, the eye and mind open simultaneously.
If you wish to know that which does not rely on the power of cultivation, let life and death drift freely as they come and go."
When Chan Master Xiangyan Xian was at Mount Gui, Mount Gui, knowing him to be a vessel for the Dharma and wishing to stimulate his spiritual radiance, said to him:
"I am not asking you about the learning and understanding you have acquired throughout your life, nor what you have memorized from scriptures and commentaries.
Before you emerged from the womb and before you could distinguish east from west, try to speak a single word regarding your fundamental matter; I wish to take note of it."
The Master was bewildered and had no reply. After reflecting for a long time, he advanced a few words to set forth his understanding, but the Mountain [Shishuang Qingzhu] refused them all.
The Master said, "I beg the Master to explain it for me. The Mountain said, "What I have explained is merely my own view;
what benefit would that be for your own eyes? The Master then searched through all the sayings he had collected from various quarters, but not a single word [matched].
He could offer no response. He then sighed to himself, saying, "A painted cake cannot satisfy hunger. Thereupon, he burned them all, declaring, "In this life I shall not study the Buddha-dharma.
I will instead become a long-wandering monk who prepares gruel and rice, so as to spare my mind and spirit from toil.
He then took his leave. Arriving at Nanyang, he beheld the traces left by National Teacher Huizhong and settled there. One day, while clearing away weeds...
While the grasses and trees were being struck with tiles and pebbles against bamboo, producing sounds, he suddenly burst into laughter; in that instant, he was awakened to a vast clarity.
He immediately returned to bathe, burned incense, and prostrated from afar toward Mount Mí, saying: "The Great Compassion of the Master is a kindness exceeding that of my own parents.

Had he explained this to me at that time, how could there be the situation I face today? He then composed a verse, which began: "A single strike causes all that is known to be forgotten; no longer..."

Provisionally practicing refinement, his every movement reveals the ancient path; he does not fall into the trap of silent stillness. Leaving no traces anywhere, his deportment transcends both sound and form.
Those who have attained the Way in all quarters unanimously declare this to be the highest capacity.
Xuedou’s Verse Commentary says: "Rice and gruel nourish this sick body as the seasons change; fundamentally, there is neither delusion nor enlightenment to concern itself with it.
Without cause, I struck the bamboo by the hermitage gate; even until now, I remain halfway there."
When Chan Master Louzi was passing through the marketplace, he stopped briefly beneath a wine shop to adjust his socks and belt.
He happened to hear a person on the upper floor singing a song that went: "Since you have no heart [for me], I shall simply let it be. At this, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
From then on, he was known as Louzi. This account appears in the *Commentary on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra* by Chan Master Changqing Xuan.
Cishou’s *Deep Verses* say: "Singing on the upper floor, his speech is elegant; Since you have no heart, I shall also desist.
Striking upon the slave-girl’s inner thoughts— All lifelong affection has turned cold and silent. Baofeng Ming said:
Since you have no mind, I too shall rest. This body has neither joy nor sorrow; when hungry, it eats, and when weary, it sleeps.
Let the falling flowers follow the current as they drift away. Focijian said: "If you have no mind, I too shall rest.
Within the curtain of the swan-patterned bedchamber, she is too weary to raise her head. When the household servant asks about this profound meaning, she smiles and points to the gauze [curtain]."
The moon through the window was at its peak in autumn.
Master Mihu instructed a monk to ask Yangshan, "Do people of the present day still require awakening?
Yangshan replied, "Since awakening is not non-existent, what can one do about it falling into the 'second place'? Upon hearing this, the Master approved.
Touzi said, "Azure Clouds. Now, although Yangshan spoke thus, did he manage to avoid falling into his own trap?
If he avoided it, there is still one person who is utterly unwilling to grant him approval. If he did not avoid it, he likewise falls into the second rank.
Although Mishan may have approved of him, does he himself still possess a way to emerge? All you people—
Try to examine this closely. If you can examine it through, both [the teacher and the student] will dissolve like ice melting.
If you cannot examine it through, do not act rashly. Ying’an Hua said: "Mihu applied the essential tongs and hammer; Yangshan displayed the business of the sword’s edge.
These two elders are truly worthy of honor within the school of preaching. However, if one turns toward the patch-robed monks..."
"O monks, you are all people who have eaten the staff.
Touzi Qing’s verse says: "I ask a person atop the peak of the emerald crags; though he points to the end of the mountains, he has not yet found rest."
Though one may avoid the command of the Double Ninth Festival, how can this compare to the numinous sprout that does not transgress the spring?

Tiantong Jue said: "The third head distinguishes awakening from delusion; quickly cast off your hands and abandon the fish-trap and rabbit snare. When the merit and title are not yet exhausted, calluses form on the hands;
though wisdom is difficult to know, it eventually bites the heel. The hare grows old as the ice-disk weeps autumn dew; the bird shivers in the jade..."
The trees are bright at dawn and the wind is chill. Holding it up, Daoyang discerns the true from the false; with not a single blemish or flaw, he values the white jade disc. Foyuan said:
"If a thousand awakened ones say there is no sorrow, who would be willing to believe them when they speak of the 'second head'?
After the cold food festival, the mountain flowers are silent and still; the sun sets in the west and the water flows east."
When Chan Master Dongshan Jia was previously at Yunyan, he asked about "insentient beings preaching the Dharma. Later, when he took his leave, the Master still harbored doubts.

Consequently, while crossing a stream, he beheld his own reflection and attained great enlightenment regarding the former principle. He composed a verse, saying: "Be most careful not to seek it from others;
It would be far removed and distant from me. Now I go forth alone, And everywhere I encounter him. He is now precisely myself; I am now..."
It is not that; one must understand it in this way before one can accord with suchness (*tathatā*).
A verse from *Fundamental Enlightenment* (*Benjue*) says: "Movement and stillness have always been co-existent from the beginning; turning one's head, one suddenly meets him face-to-face."
Even if it were so, it would still be laughable. To call it "suchness" (tathatā) is, moreover, circuitous.
Once, when Chan Master Xuefeng Cun was at Aoshan Inn with Yantou and Qinshan, they sat in meditation during the first watch of the night.
Yantou said, "Why do you not go to sleep? You are like a village tutelary deity; some day in the future, you will bewitch people's households."
The Master [Zhaozhou] was away; when he returned, the Head Monk pointed to his chest and said, "I am not yet settled here.
Zhaozhou said, "I thought that after this you would go to the summit of a solitary peak, build a grass hut, and propagate the Great Teaching.
Yet you are still making such remarks. The Head Monk said, "I do not dare deceive myself. The Head Monk continued, "If it is truly so, then according to your realization—"
[The Master] said, "Each and every one comes forth. Where it is appropriate, I shall bear witness for you; where it is not appropriate, I shall eradicate it for you.
The Master said, "When I first arrived at Yanguan, I saw him ascend the hall and expound upon the meaning of form and emptiness, through which I attained a point of entry.

[Yunmen] said, 'From now until thirty years hence, you must strictly avoid mentioning this. The Master said, 'Furthermore, because of Dongshan’s verse: "Strictly avoid seeking it by following after others... "Tiao... [The text trails off here.]
Tiao said, "I am estranged from you. Tou said, "If it is like this, you have not even mastered saving yourself.
The Master said, "Later I asked Deshan, 'In the matter of the ancestral Dharma-lineage, does a student have any share in it? Deshan gave me a blow with his staff and said, 'Say something!
At that moment, it was as if the bottom had fallen out of my bucket. Tou shouted, "Have you not heard: 'That which enters through the gate...'"?

"It is not a family treasure. The Master asked, "How is it so? Tou said, "In the future, if you wish to propagate the Great Teaching, let each and every word flow forth from your own breast and bring it forth to cover heaven and earth.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and cried out repeatedly, "Elder Brother, today at last is the completion of the Way on Mount Ao. Elder Brother, today..."
This was when Ao Shan first attained the Way.
Jiaochong Guang said: "Just as Yantou said that 'everything flows from one's own breast,' tell me:
did Xuefeng’s three previous awakenings flow from his own breast or not? If they did..."
"It flows forth from within one's own breast," he said, "yet the path is still not yet secure.
If it does not flow forth from within one's own breast, from where else could it come? Is there anyone who can cut this through? If you can cut it through—"
It is not only Xuefeng who attained enlightenment on Mount Ao; all sentient beings throughout the entire universe have simultaneously realized perfect awakening.
If you cannot say this, how can you speak of "attaining enlightenment on Mount Ao"? Even if one were to transmit the mind at Shaoshi, one would still not have seen it even in a dream.
Foyan Yuan’s verse says: "The Tortoise Mountain where he attained the Way is enough for people to pass down; Is it not that the story from before has yet to be completed?
Fortunately, Xuansha knew the beginning and the end: 'His whole body, red and raw, is in the fisherman's boat. Kumu Cheng said:
He has spoken of the causes of his coming and going throughout his entire life; in the end, it is difficult to meet one with a sincere heart.
If one suddenly accepts it for oneself, the family enterprise is established; even a piece of rubble, when picked up, is a treasure. Fodeng Xun said:
"A man of spirit and heroic ambition strives outwardly, but his efforts are in vain. Only when he reaches Mount Ao and opens his eyes to look does he finally realize the nature of his own house."
Its applications are inexhaustible.
Dàchánfó Tōngchánshī was once under the assembly of Guīzōng Chángchánshī. One night, he suddenly cried out, "I have attained great enlightenment!
The assembly was startled by this. The following day, Guīzōng ascended the hall, gathered the assembly, and asked, "The one who claimed last night to have attained great enlightenment—"
[Zhaozhou] came forward. The Master stepped out and said, "I am [Zhaozhou]. Yunmen said, "What principle have you seen that you speak of 'great enlightenment'?
Zhaozhou replied, "The nun was originally a woman. Yunmen remained silent, yet marveled at him.
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: "Awakening does not depend on manifold hardships; Understanding comes about in a mere instant.
To insist that it must be performed by a nun or a woman— What a fool to mistake piled snow for a silver mountain! Baoning Yong said:
At midnight, his voice rose high like that of a minor deity. Within this clarity, there is distance and intimacy.
Now, following custom, they pass on its resonance; they even say, "The nun is a woman. Da Hong then said:
"When one has awakened, it is the same as when one was unawakened. Why need one further tell others? When the thief’s loot is exposed, there is no place to hide it; thus he says, 'The nun...'"
The aunt is the daughter. Caotang Qing said: "In the fifth month, when the fierce heat is at its peak, sweat flows down one's back beyond description.
When a pure breeze sweeps across the earth and strikes the face, it merely adds more dross to the eyes of a great Chan master."
Huanglong Zhen said: "A child learns to follow the vermilion; where it is red, he turns his back on the black. If you bring a sheet of white paper, not a single dot can be applied.
If one were to apply it, it would instead become smoke and ink smeared upon the paper."
When Venerable Yan’yang first visited Zhaozhou, he asked, "What is it like when one brings nothing forth?
Zhaozhou said, "Put it down. The Master said, "If I bring nothing forth, what is there to put down? Zhaozhou said, "Then carry it away.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Later, while residing on a mountain, a snake and a tiger would come to his hand to eat from him.
Huanglong Nan’s verse says: Not a single thing can be brought forth; it cannot be borne upon the shoulders. In a single word, one suddenly realizes what was wrong;
within the heart, there is boundless joy. Once malice and poison are cast from the mind, even snakes and tigers become intimate friends.
A pure breeze has blown for several hundred years; even to this day, it has not ceased. Zhenjing Wen says: Moving from the high to the low, he exercises his sovereign authority.
The gates of liberation open; how pitiable is the lack of faith! Failing to obtain the true, wondrous secret of the Empty King, One is led astray and dragged along by sounds and forms.
Foyan Yuan said: "Exerting all one's strength, one cannot let it go; Applying all one's effort, one cannot lift it up.
I thought there was nothing at all, But it is originally my own. Seeing that which is my own, Great joy arises in the heart. Spontaneously...
Now this family business flourishes; in a single move, it spans ninety thousand *li*. The Ancient Buddha Min said: "If you bring nothing at all, I will teach you to let go.
In vast awakening to non-arising, all worldly concerns are cast aside. Tiantong Juo said: "It does not hinder one’s skillful execution of the subtle opening move;
yet one feels self-reproach for the mind’s coarseness as it bumps its head against the board. When the game is over, the girdle is loosened."
The axe handle rotted away; washing clean one's mundane bones, one joins the immortal journey.
When Chan Master Xian of Luoshan first visited Shishuang, he asked: "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not cease? Shishuang replied: "You must become cold ashes and withered wood;
you must go where a single thought lasts ten thousand years; you must go where the lid covers the vessel; you must be pure clarity, utterly free of a single speck."
He departed. The Master did not approve. He went again to visit Yantou to inquire about his previous question. Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases?
At this, the Master attained great enlightenment. Tiantong Jue’s verse says: "He cut through the old entanglements and smashed the foxes’ den; the leopard strips away the mist..."
The dragon sheds its skin and changes its bones by riding upon the thunder. *Du!* What thing is this, with its ceaseless arising and ceasing?
Master Fayen Yi and Master Xiu Zongxian were traveling together when they passed through the quarters of Chan Master Dizang Chen.

Hindered by the snow, they stayed for a short while to rest. Chen asked, "Where are you going on this journey? The Master replied, "I am traveling as a wandering monk (*xingjiao*). Chen asked, "What is it that you are doing?"
Regarding the matter of traveling as a mendicant, the Master said, "I do not know. Zang said, "Not knowing is most intimate.

The Master then joined three others in reciting the *Zhao Lun* (Treatise by Sengzhao) until they reached the passage, "Heaven and earth share the same root as I. Cheng asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as yourself, or are they different?
The Master said, "The same. Cheng held up two fingers and stared intently at them, saying, "Two! He then immediately rose and departed.

The Master was about to set out on his journey when Fayan Chen saw him off at the gate. Chen asked, "Upādhyāya, you usually say that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only.
Now, look at this stone in the courtyard; tell me, does it reside within the mind or outside the mind?
The Master replied, "It is within the mind. Chen said, "For a traveling monk, what possible reason could there be for placing a piece of stone inside his mind?"
"Head-ya. The Master was at a loss for a reply and immediately requested a definitive resolution. For nearly a month thereafter, he presented his views and explained his reasoning.
Baolin said, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this. The Master said, "I am at the end of my words and exhausted of principles. Baolin said, "..."
If one discusses the Buddha-dharma, all views are established as such. Under these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Tiantong Jue’s verse says: "Now, having fully studied as he did then, he has cast off all finicky subtleties until reaching the state of non-knowing."
Whether short or long, let it be; do not cut or patch it. Whether high or low, let it be; maintain it naturally level. Use the family resources as needed according to the occasion;
move through the fields at ease, walking wherever the steps lead. The affairs of my thirty years of wandering—clearly, I have brought shame upon my own eyebrows.

Chan Master Hugu Cheng and Dharma Master Yanhua were together at Baoci Monastery in Hunan. On one occasion, when Master Cizheng ascended the hall, Yanhua stepped forward and asked, "What is the true nature of the Buddha?
Cizheng replied, "Who does not possess it? Yanhua was not satisfied with this answer and subsequently requested instruction from Master Cheng.
The Master said, "Simply ask. Yanhua repeated his previous question. The Master replied, "Who possesses it? At these words, Yanhua attained realization.
Upon attaining realization, he said, "Whether the Head Seat is among the assembly or serving as abbot, I vow to assist him for the rest of my life.
Later, Huazhi also succeeded his teacher in presiding over Huguo Temple.
Buddha Xingtai’s verse says: "Three in the morning, four in the evening—how little! Four in the evening, three in the morning—how much more!
If one cannot discern the measure of such amounts, From this, the confusion between existence and non-existence arises.
To avoid such confusion: Oṃ sūru siri svāhā."
When Chan Master Nanquan Yuan of the Great Way was asked by Zhaozhou, "What is the Way? the Master said, "The ordinary mind is the Way.
Zhaozhou asked, "Is it still necessary to seek after it? The Master said, "To intend to seek it is already to deviate. Zhaozhou asked, "If one does not intend it, how can one know it?"
"This is the Way. The Master said, "The Way does not belong to knowing, nor does it belong to not-knowing. Knowing is deluded awareness; not-knowing is indeterminate.
If one truly penetrates the Way that is free from doubt, it is like the great void—vast, open, and expansive. How could one forcibly impose distinctions of right and wrong?
At these words, Zhuzhou suddenly awakened to the profound essence.
Songyuan Yueyun said: "The blue sky and the bright sun—what have you awakened to? Puh! Puh! Puh! The dragon pearl is shattered in the depths of the azure dragon’s lair.
Yunfeng Yue’s verse says: "Ordinary mind is the Way; take a step and enter the wild weeds. One cannot help but sigh for the old man Wang."
The Master said: "In the end, one cannot understand it; the jade hare and golden crow fly and run as they please. Fojian Huiqin said:
"If you wish to recognize the ordinary way, let the true nature be itself natural. When rowing a boat, you should lift the oars; when riding a horse, you must apply the whip."
If you encounter hunger, eat; when weary, you should sleep. All arises from conditions, yet that which is obtained is not itself a condition.

That which is obtained is not itself a condition—this one must clearly realize for oneself. To see the bright moon in the rain, to draw clear spring water from within fire, to stand upright with the head thrust into the earth, or to lie flat with the toes pointing toward heaven—one must understand it in this way to truly accord with reality.
Regarding "Patriarchal Chan," Jingshan Hongzhi said: "I urge you not to weary your spirit in vain; To call it 'ordinary' is already to miss the mark.
It is utterly flavorless and cold, Yet every time it is raised, it is ever new. Gushan Huiguo said:
"If you say that the ordinary mind is the Way, You are adding branches to the branches above. To cling to it as if it were skin-tight..."
The undershirt is as if stripped away; he calls him over and adds eyebrows to his eyes.
Zen Master Yanyuan of Yaoshan was asked by a monk, "What is the supreme treasure within the Way? The Master said, "Do not be sycophantic. The monk asked, "What is it like when one is not sycophantic?
The Master said, "Even the wealth of an entire kingdom could not exchange it for it."
When Chan Master Zhaozhou Shen was with Nanquan, Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying, "The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not the Way.
The Master then asked, "What is the Way outside of things? Nanquan struck him. The Master seized the staff and said, "Be careful not to strike people wrongly in the future!
Nanquan said, "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish; a patch-robed monk is hard to deceive. He then threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
The Abbot [asked]. Xuedou Xian said: "Zhaozhou is like a dragon without horns, like a snake with feet. At that time, he did not care that 'exhausting the law leaves no people';
he simply had to be beaten with a staff and driven out. Langya Jue said: "Have you not seen it said: 'Wine..."
"Drink with those who meet as kindred spirits; recite poetry for those who understand. The Old Monk [Zhaozhou] comments:
"Nanquan cast his hook across the four seas only to catch fierce dragons. His discourse beyond the ordinary was intended to seek out kindred spirits.

Zhaozhou was accustomed to traversing mountain passes and had experienced the frontiers thoroughly; without wielding a blade, he brought peace to the seas and rivers. Even so, tell me, what about these two?"

"Old Man, when meeting face-to-face, is there still superiority or inferiority? After a long silence, he said: "If one does not ascend the tower to gaze out, how can one know the depth of the vast ocean?
Baoning Yong composed a verse on this: Wrapping himself in softness, he conceals his edge as he enters the fray; In a flash he seizes the opponent, leaving their eyes staring wide.
One who decides life and death is a hero among men; one who practices both civil and martial arts possesses the talent of a general and a minister.

Nantang Jing said: "Dragons and snakes can easily be distinguished; It is most difficult to deceive those who wear the patched robe. The nature is pure as the vast autumn sky; The mind is clear as the expansive great ocean.
A hair-tip is seen at the edge of the world; The universe is viewed within the palm of the hand. Of the myriad dharmas, none are his companions; The Western River is but a single drop."

[He] dried it up. Zhaozhou addressed the assembly, saying: "The ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination. As soon as there is speech, there is discrimination and there is clarity.
