Chan Master Tong arrived at Huoshan and said to himself: "Beneath Yunfeng Peak, four staffs [of teaching]; the great Buddha of the world."
"San! The Mountain then called for the rector, saying, "Strike the bell! The Master immediately ran off.
Xuedou Xian said, "Although this fellow was able to change with the occasion, alas, he had a beginning but no end."
The Verse of Xian of Yuantong says: "Having eaten the willow switch, one wanders at leisure; Yet before reaching the secure gate, one refuses to rest.
Beating the drum and ringing the bell are both commands; Who can match such one who knows the occasion and discerns change?"
Chan Master Xinghua Jiang ascended the hall and said, "Today, there is no need for 'how' or 'what.

Simply request to enter directly with a single blade, and I, Xinghua, will provide you with verification. At that time, Elder Minde stepped forward; as he rose from his prostration, he let out a shout. The Master also shouted.
Minde shouted again, and the Master shouted once more. Minde performed a prostration, and the Master said, "If it had been anyone else, they would have received thirty blows of the staff."
"A single blow cannot compare [to this]. Why? Because Minde understood how to employ a shout not as a mere shout," and he then descended from his seat.
Shoushan Nian said: "Observe how Xinghua acted in such a manner; why did he let him pass?"
"Venerable Elders, tell me: in what sense does one shout not function as a single shout?
Is it the first shout, or is it the second shout? Which is the guest, and which is the host? Although this is so, you must examine it with great care.
After a long silence, he said: "Both have faults; both are without fault. Take care! — Langhuan (Lanxi Daolong)
Yaojue said: "Tell me, how is it that one shout does not function as a single shout? If Xinghua had not had these subsequent words, he would have left the whole world in doubt.
Even so, those who understand this are rare. Songyuan Yue said: "Xinghua’s hook and line ruined his household;
Mingde seized him by the hair and brought him to the yamen. Yet he further says that he understands 'one shout does not function as a single shout.'"
The function of the single shout is such that one does not know how it overwhelms and extinguishes the very style of our Linji school. Have you not heard it said:
"A master does not wait for the pecking and the breaking;
if they coincide, both are lost"? Haiyin Xin’s verse says: "When dragon and tiger cross paths—this is that very moment. There is no room for hesitation; already there is a discrepancy."
"A single shout, clearly not functioning, yet causes Zen practitioners to harbor a particular doubt. Yunxi Gong said: "A fierce dragon emerges from the water;
a tiger leaves the mountain. Winds rise on all four sides, swirling through ten thousand acres of mist.
If one possesses the True Eye of Aniruddha, one will traverse the three realms and turn one's back upon the heavens. Gushan Gui said: "Entering directly with a single blade..."
One must deliberate. In the space of a single thought or gesture, the roles of guest and host are distinguished;
one must not allow Master Minde to pass by. One must know that Xinghua’s staff was intimate and direct. Jingshan Daowu said: "Hand-in-hand in the dark, they ascend a high mountain;
when day breaks, each goes their own way. How many travelers on the road who have not yet returned? With eyes wide open, they fall straight into a deep pit."
Xinghua was approached by a fellow practitioner who had come to visit him. As soon as the monk entered the Dharma Hall, the Master gave a shout; the monk also shouted.
After the monk had walked two or three paces, the Master shouted again; the monk also shouted. In a moment, the monk drew near, and the Master raised his staff.

The monk shouted once more. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow, still acting as the host! The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him, driving him straight out of the Dharma Hall. The Master then...
He returned to the abbot’s quarters. A monk asked, "What words did that previous monk use to provoke the Master?
The Master said, "That fellow just now possessed both the provisional and the real; he had both illumination and function.
I reached out my hand and drew a line before him, yet at this point, it was of no use. For a blind fellow like this, if I do not strike him, what am I waiting for?"
At that time, Yuanwu Keqin said: "The sword in the Prince's treasury; the drum of lethal poison shaken. A flash of lightning cannot match its swiftness;
a peal of thunder cannot equal its majesty. It may be called one who is skilled at driving the oxen of the plowman and able to seize [the reins]."
The food of a hungry man is simply like the mutual exchange between host and guest.
Setting aside for a moment the aspects of illumination and function, or the provisional and the real—where exactly did Xinghua make that single stroke with his hand before the man’s face?
If you can see through this clearly here, you may shoulder the treasury of the true Dharma-eye of Linji. If, however, you have not yet distinguished the mud from the water, you have not yet...
"Exempting the blind donkey from following the great crowd. Ying'an Hua said: "Xinghua’s gate and walls are eight thousand feet high;
his ancestral house laws have always been stern. This monk has secretly penetrated the heavy barriers, wishing to see the spring colors within the cave. It is well, indeed it is well."
In either case, both parties fail to gain the advantage. As for Xinghua’s saying, “I take my hand and draw a line before him”—how about that?
Before heaven is established, hell is already formed.
Gushan Gui’s verse says: A thunderclap startles heaven and earth; how could one bear to listen with ears covered?
You must know that Old Xinghua—half of it is mere human sentiment. Tuan’an Xiu says: It is just like an executioner of fierce and heroic spirit who strikes a single blow at the throat;
when the five viscera—the liver and heart—are all sliced out, only then does one realize that the King’s Law does not spare anyone.
Rao. Jingshan Hongdao said: "The Mohe sword is held in hand; the heavenly demons' hearts fail them. You clear-eyed monks, do not engage in further conjecture.
Jianmen Anzhu said: "The tall pines do not change their four-season green. How many are clear regarding seizing and relinquishing in the moment?
When the army is defeated, it cannot withstand being swept away by a broom; the pupils in one's eyes are the people standing before you."
Xinghua said to the assembly, "I have heard that one shouts in the long corridor and shouts in the rear quarters. My sons, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly.

Even if you could shout Xinghua up to the thirty-third heaven and then dash back down so that he has not a single breath left, wait until Xinghua has recovered and risen again, and I shall tell you that it is still not enough. Why is this?"
This! I have never scattered real pearls behind a purple silk curtain for you people to pick up.
Why do you shout and bellow so recklessly in the midst of empty space?
Master Xingtao of Fuxin said: "Driving the plow and losing the ox; snatching food from a starving man; smashing the bright moon-jewel;
striking out the marrow of the phoenix. This may truly be called the most noble among the noble, the most refined among the refined.
His magnificent reputation has remained unceasing to this day. I venture to ask the assembly: Just as Xinghua said, "I have never yet entered the purple silk curtain..."
"Scattering pearls within. How do you understand this? If anyone says 'Pshaw! [in response], I know you cannot leap out. Water Hermit said:
"Xinghua was indeed so, yet it is much like eating salt when hungry. If it were Cuiyun, it would not be thus.
He would wait until you had bellowed until Mount Cuiyun shook, and then he would say to him: 'You are playing with...'"
Regarding the "scent of gruel and rice," Gushan Gui’s verse says: "True pearls scattered within a purple silk curtain; Zen practitioners pass them down, yet all merely skim the surface.
Clapping hands, 'Ha-ha!'—opening my mouth to laugh: Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his servants. Jingshan Daokai said:
To the assembly he fully proclaims the Magadha command; how could this be idly opening two flaps of skin?
With a shout, the blind donkeys gallop off in a herd; in a dream, he topples the five Sumerus.
Chan Master Yangqihuai asked Ciming, "When the dark birds warble their cries and leave the clouds to enter the jumbled peaks, what then?
Ciming said, "I am walking through the wild weeds; you, too, have entered a deep village. The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle to pass;
let me ask another question. Ciming then gave a shout. The Master said, "A fine shout! Ciming shouted again, and the Master also shouted. Ciming shouted twice in succession.
"Ho! The Master then bowed. Songyuan Yue said:
"These two are father and son. It is like playing with a pearl: it does not touch the hand, it does not fall to the ground, and it does not abide in space;
yet there is nothing mysterious or subtle about it. How can one even blink an eye here? He let out a shout.
Baizhang Yuan’s verse says: About to bring forth the pearl of the black dragon, he meets a great merchant; The golden platter is set in motion, its radiance overflowing.
There is no need for a single word to discuss its high value; Taking each other by the hand, they return home to laugh many times.
*Chanlin Leiju*, Volume Six; *Chanlin Leiju*, Volume Seven:
Circular Signs (*yuánxiàng*), Responding to Capacities (*duìjī*), Host and Guest (*bīnzhǔ*), and Family Style (*jiāfēng*).
Regarding the "Perfect Circle": Chan Master Nanquan Yuan was traveling with Guizong and Magu to visit National Teacher Zhong.

When they reached the middle of the road, the Master drew a perfect circle on the ground and said, "If you can speak, then we shall proceed. Guizong sat down within the circle, and Magu immediately...
He performed a woman’s bow. The Master said, "If that is so, then you will not go. Zong asked, "What kind of mental activity is this?
The Master then called him back; he did not go to pay his respects to the National Teacher.
Xuánjué said: "As for Nánquán speaking thus—was it a word of approval or a word of disapproval?
Yúnjū Xī said: "Recently he went to pay his respects to the National Teacher; why did Nánquán instead call him back?
Tell me, what was the meaning of the ancients? Yúnjū Yuán said: "The spirit of Guīzōng and Mágù."
Wang Yuru fell within the circle of Nanquan. At that time, seeing him draw a circle, he shook his sleeves and departed;
even if Nanquan had possessed further supernatural powers, it would still have been three thousand li short.
Baoning Yong, for his part, clapped his hands and laughed loudly as he returned to Guizong, then rose and left. Tiantong Jue said: "If I had seen him at that moment..."
He then swept away the circular diagram (*maṇḍala*). Not only did he shatter Nanquan’s den, but he also left Guizong with no place to rest his body.
Magu displayed his skill but could not prevail; Nanquan said, "If that is so, then I shall not go."
Indeed, indeed. Fenyang Shanzhao’s verse says:
The National Teacher wished to see many kinds of meaning; Sitting upright and composed, he invited [the monks] to look.
Without departing, they heard it with a single sound and understood; Having long served in the ranks, they seized the banners and flags. Xuedou Xian said:
The archer shoots his arrow at the monkey; why does it circle the tree so straight? Of the thousands and tens of thousands, who has ever hit its mark?
Calling out to one another, come back home! On the road to Caoxi, do not climb up and down. He further said: "The road to Caoxi is level and smooth;
for what reason, then, should one not climb up and down? Baoning Yong said: "The vast earth is filled [with people]."
A foot of snow; the rivers and lakes are one expanse, impossible to distinguish. A fisherman, clad in his straw raincoat, returns under the moonlight.
Who would say that for a traveler at night, the road is cut off?
Master Daowei Yu once ordered a monk to deliver a letter to Attendant Wang Changshi. After Attendant Wang had read the letter, he asked:
"What have you been saying lately, Master? The monk replied, "A monk asked, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
and the Master held up his whisk. The King asked, "How do the brothers there discuss this? He replied, "'Borrowing form to clarify the mind;
attaching to objects to manifest the principle. The King said, "This is not the principle. It would be well for you, Venerable One, to return to the mountain quickly."
"Such-and-such a person has sent a reply to the Master. When the monk received the letter, he returned with it to present to the Master.
The Master opened it and saw a circle drawn inside which was written the character for "sun. The Master said, "Who would have known that beyond a thousand li there is one who understands?
Yangshan, attending nearby, remarked, "Even so, he is still just a worldly man. The Master said:
"What do you say to this, my son? [Xuefeng] looked up, drew a circle, and wrote the character for "sun" (日) inside it;
he then wiped it away with his foot. The Master then laughed heartily. (In one version, there are slight differences. Baoning Yong’s verse says:
"The Southern Star and Northern Dipper have all shifted their positions; the four seas and nine provinces are like a boiling cauldron."
King Prasenajit’s nose reaches the heavens; Ruci Tathāgata’s feet tread upon the earth.
One day, when the Chan Master Jì of Yǎngshān had a Brahman monk arrive, the Master drew the shape of a half-moon on the ground.
The monk stepped forward, added it to form a full circle, and rubbed it away with his foot. The Master extended both hands; the monk shook out his sleeves and departed.
Chengtian Jian said: "Mount Yang was much like a mute man eating a bitter melon. Yuanwu Keqin said:
"Like pouring lacquer into lacquer, or adding salt to soy sauce; their feathers and down are alike, and their physical forms are the same. Even so..."
Both the Great and Small Yangshans were exposed by a foreign monk.
Benjue’s verse says: "Jizi happened upon an ear-pierced traveler; he once showed him his own home with a half-moon."
The monk Tien left abruptly after half a month; he knew that he had personally encountered a minor Śākyamuni.
While Yangshan was sitting after the morning gruel at Shiting in Hongzhou, a monk asked him, "Does the Master know how to read characters?"
The Master said, "According to one's lot. The monk then circled to the right once and asked, "What word is this? The Master drew a cross on the ground.
The monk then circled to the left once and asked, "What word is this? The Master changed the cross into a *swastika* (卍).
The monk drew a circle and cradled it with both hands in the manner of an asura grasping the sun and moon, asking, "What is this?"
The character "ma" (麼). The Master then drew a circle surrounding the *svastika* (卍) character. The monk then assumed the posture of Lohitya (Louti, 樓至).
The Master said, "So it is, so it is. This is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind. You are thus; I am also thus. Guard and uphold it well for yourself.
The monk prostrated and departed, soaring through the air.
Tiantong Jue’s verse says: The void of the Dao’s circuit is never filled; The characters of the empty seal have not yet taken form.
The subtle operation of the celestial wheel and terrestrial axis, Densely interwoven with martial warp and civil woof. Releasing and gathering, it stands alone and travels everywhere.
The mechanism triggers the dark pivot like lightning flashing across the blue sky; The eyes contain purple radiance like stars seen in broad daylight.
When Minister Chen Cao came to visit Master Zifu Bao, the Master drew a circle. Chen said, "I have come as a disciple;
I was already at a disadvantage, so why must you draw this circle? The Master placed a dot in the center.
Chen said, "I thought you were a merchant captain from the South Seas. The Master then returned to his quarters and shut the door.
Daguizhe said: "Although Zifu was the original furnace and forge, how could he fail to recognize Chen Cao as refined pure gold?
Do you all wish to know Zifu? He casually cast a single hook, startling the dragon from the azure waves."
Huguo Long said: "Zifu bought iron and obtained gold—a scene of great wealth and honor. While this is so, alas, the public case remains unresolved.

Today, as you great beings enter the mountain to meet me, I shall neither draw a circular diagram nor close the door of my abbot’s quarters. Tell me, are you one with the old man Zifu, or are you two?"
Do you know where it lands? Meeting in the bamboo courtyard, there is nothing to do; everyone drinks Zhaozhou’s tea together.
Ying’an Hua said: "Even so, if one arrives at the gate of Tiantong, one will not be let off so easily."
At that time, it was said of Minister Chen Cao: "If my disciple comes in such a manner, he is already missing his opportunity;
how much more so when he further draws a circle? Tiantong opens wide the eastern gate and makes proper arrangements beneath the bright window.
Why? Because there is a gentleman within the gate, and now a gentleman arrives at the gate.
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "Round and round, pearls encircle jade; tinkling, horses carry donkeys. Mounted upon an iron boat, it is entrusted to the carefree traveler of the seas and mountains.
When fishing for the giant tortoise, he casts down a single coil. The Master further said:
"Not a single monk in the world can leap out of this."
The Chan Master Zifu Bao was asked by a monk, "What is the song of the ancients? The Master then drew a circle and faced him with it.
Touzi Qing’s verse on this says: "One tune, two tunes, played deep in the night; Pine winds and rain pass over the mountain ahead."
"Pitifully, Bian Yu has left the Jingshou Mountains. Who is the one who knows this music to take it back?
In response to this prompt, Chan Master Shitou Xiqian asked Qingyuan: "Since you, Master, departed from Caoxi, when did you arrive here?"
[The Master] said, "I do not know when you departed from Caoxi. The Teacher replied, "I have not come from Caoxi.
[The Master] said, "I already know where you have come from. The Teacher replied, "Fortunately, the Master is a great personage."
Furthermore, do not act with haste.
Danxia Chun’s verse says: A wooden man comes to ask the way to the azure heavens; The jade maiden is advanced in years and seems not to hear.
Hand in hand, they walk together back to their native land; The evening mountains are shrouded in layer upon layer of heavy clouds.
Once, while Baizhang Hai Chan Master was standing in attendance with Guishan, Wufeng, and Yunyan, he asked Guishan, "Set aside your throat, lips, and mouth;
how would you speak? Guishan said, "I beg the Master to speak for me.
Baizhang said, "It is not that I refuse to speak to you, but I fear it would cause my descendants to perish hereafter. He then asked Wufeng, who replied, "Master..."
"You must also set them all aside. The Master said, "In a place where there is no one, I shall look up at you with bated breath.
The Master asked Yunyan again, and Yunyan replied, "Does the Master have it yet? The Master said, "I have lost my descendants."
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "Please, Preceptor, speak further: A tiger’s head sprouts horns as it emerges from the wild weeds;
The ten islands have reached the end of spring and the flowers wither away; In the coral groves, the sun shines bright and clear. Preceptor, you too must close your eyes;
Upon the battlefield of dragons and snakes, one observes their stratagems. It makes one long remember General Li: Ten thousand li across the heavens, a single falcon soars."
"Does the Master have it yet? The golden-maned lion does not crouch on the ground; two by two and three by three, they travel the old path.
On Mount Daxiong, he snaps his fingers in the void. Baoning Yong said: "The three sons have all grown up."
Everyone manages their own affairs; among them, the elder brother may resent the younger for losses, and the younger brother may resent the elder for gains.
Fojian Qin said: "I would instead ask the Master to speak of that place where a thousand or ten thousand people do not go."
The bright sun is dim as the sea turns crimson; the clear breeze is piercing as the frosty sky breaks into dawn. "The Master, too, must shut it all away.
Those who come after wish to tread where their predecessors have walked. Though others differ in their sharpness or dullness of faculties, in the end they lose by one move.
"Does the Master have it yet? For now, clarify the ground within yourself; you cannot yet spread your wings against the current.

The wind blows; with youthful ambition to pursue the azure clouds for a thousand miles, Zen Master Nanquan Yuan asked Huangbo, "Is it through the equal cultivation of concentration and wisdom that one clearly perceives the Buddha-nature?
Huangbo replied, "In the twelve periods of the day, do not rely upon or depend on a single thing. The Master said, "Is this not precisely your own realization, Elder? Huangbo—
Wuzu said, "I dare not. The Master said, "Let us set aside the money for the gruel; who will pay the money for the straw sandals? Huangbo did not answer.
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Is it that Huangbo could not reach Nanquan? Yangshan said, "Not so.
You must know that Huangbo possesses the mechanism for trapping a tiger. Guishan said, "Your insight has grown this long!"
Baofu Zhan said, "If it were not for Miaoyan and Daowu, Huangbo would have been buried.
Wuzu Ji said, "Mount Yang was almost like drawing legs on a snake. Yunfeng Yue said, "If one does not sleep in the same bed, how can one know there is a hole in the quilt?"
Foyan Yuan’s verse says: The question and answer have already been clearly refined; how many people see the paradox here?
The youth all resolve the battle-array of dragons and snakes; the aged together chant the songs of children. Fojian Qin said:
Last night the silver hare [the moon] traversed the constellations of the Wicker and the Tail. Suddenly, a gust of celestial wind arose.

It swept away thousands upon tens of thousands of layers of clouds, until the azure sky was as still and silent as frozen water. Haixin said: "When two armies clash in battle, it is not difficult to fight;
but who understands the deployment of troops and the maneuvering of combat? One merely knows how to brandish the spear and charge with the momentum, only to lose one's life and fail."
"How much life is there? Fohuiquan said: "Charging wildly and rushing about, wearying without rest; The grass is deep and the wind is fierce—how much more cause for sorrow!
The lion that turns its body has no place to be found; It leaves travelers only to debate the path."
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Throughout the entire day I have been deliberating with you; what kind of matter has been accomplished?
Yangshan drew a line through the air. The Master said, "If it were not for me, you would surely have been deluded by him."
Foyin Yuan’s verse on the original saying reads: "Throughout the day they deliberate upon the words of the ancient Buddha; at that moment, a single stroke turned it into a grievance.
To this day, Miaoshan still remains—do not say that the lineage has been severed of its descendants. Dizang En said:
Pines are straight and thorns are crooked; crows are black and cranes are white. To deliberate on this at the very end is like drawing a single stroke across the void.
If one speaks of the profound barrier above, it will cause all the Zen travelers from every quarter to run headlong into destruction.
One day, Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Is it appropriate to meet him when he is in the light, or is it appropriate to meet him when he is in the dark? Nanquan then returned to his quarters.
The Master returned to the hall and said, "This old monk was left with nothing to say in response to my question. The Head Seat remarked:
"Do not say that the Master has nothing to say; it is simply that you, Senior Monk, do not understand.
The Master then gave the Head Seat a slap and said, "This slap ought to have been taken by the old man in the hall."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "The real thief has run away; the officer who seized the stolen goods is struck with a staff. He also said:
"If Nanquan had not acted decisively when it was required, he would have instead invited chaos. Yunju Shun asked: "How do you all understand this?
When you try to understand it, you say that the Head Seat fell into Zhaozhou’s trap. But how can you understand it in such a way?"
The Way of Great Folly. Zhaozhou was truly as if he were unconcerned with others.
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "The Great Matter is already manifest and clear; it must be made ten times more perfectly complete."
The head monk in the hall is as black as lacquer; for whose sake does he take a "dark fist" on such a cold day?

Zhaozhou once asked Nanquan, "Please, Master, speak on that which transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations. Nanquan immediately descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The Master said, "This old fellow usually talks a mile a minute, but today, having been questioned by me, he was completely at a loss."
He was unable to offer a word in reply. The attendant said, "It would be better not to say that the Master has nothing to say.
The Master then gave him a slap and said, "This slap should have been taken by Old Wang!"
Yuánwù Qín said: "To harmonize with the light and to harmonize with the dark—this is the fundamental principle of the school.
To seize the tiger’s head and gather in its tail—this is the skillful means of a true master. Nevertheless, even so, it still falls into the secondary category."

The *Zhimen zusu* (Verses on the Succession of the Wisdom Gate) says: "Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations— Only one who knows the author intimately can recognize him.
Leaping down from the meditation seat and departing at once, He lets the hawk pursue its flight through the sky."
When Chan Master Daowu Zhi arrived at Wufeng, Wufeng asked, "Do you recognize the old host Yaoshan? The Master said, "I do not recognize him.
Wufeng asked, "Why do you not recognize him? The Master said, "I do not recognize him; I do not recognize him."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: Where white clouds lie deep, the path is difficult to traverse; To seek its traces is already to involve effort.
The horned sheep hanging from the branch leaves no trace; Yet in its ease, it still falls within the midst of the orthodox and the deviant.
Chan Master Huanglian was asked by a monk, "What is the phrase prior to sound? The Master said, "There is no phrase prior to sound;
ask what comes after the sound.
Touzi Qing composed a verse on this: "The vast road is empty before the kalpa of emptiness; To believe in the 'no-phrase' prior to sound is difficult."
If you wish to exhaustively explore the songs of white clouds over the Canglang River, first look at the stone man revealing half his face.
When Master Heshang Huo was asked by Luoshan, "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not stop? the Master gave a shout and said, "Who is it that arises and ceases?"
Songyuan Yueyun said: "Out of compassion, the ancients had 'discourse that descends into the weeds. Jianfu, however, was not like this.
If someone suddenly asked, 'What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? he would simply give a shout."
Tiantong Jue’s verse says: "Severing the old entanglements, Breaking open the foxes' den. The leopard sheds its mist to change its markings;
The dragon rides the thunder to transform its bones. Ha! What is this thing that arises and ceases in such profusion?"
Chan Master Chongfu Zhi was asked by a monk, "What is the speech that is vast and expansive? The Master replied, "One who has no tongue can speak it.
Touzi Qing composed a verse on this: When speaking words of vast expansiveness, the tongue is not offended; The pure wind and lofty melody drift amidst the azure clouds.
The stone man greedily talks of the affairs of the western peak; unaware, the mist rises from the eastern crag to shroud him. Chan Master Guangde Yizhi was asked by a monk:
"An ancient said, 'Where the path of words is cut off, there is neither past, future, nor present. What is the principle of this? The Master replied:
"How many kalpas have passed since Maitreya entered nirvana? Yet Huiming has still not descended to Kapilavastu."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "Wondrous, profound, perfectly bright—the foremost capacity.
At the time of descending to be born, attaining the Way, and entering nirvana, Whether at Kapilavastu, Magadha, or the twin śāla trees— If you recognize them, they are fundamentally not it."
Cen Master Yunmen asked Qianfeng, "Please, Master, answer my question. Qianfeng said, "Have you even reached me yet?
Yunmen said, "If that is so, then I am late. Qianfeng said, "How so? How so?
Yunmen said, "I thought monkeys were white; now I see there are also black ones."
Ying’an Hua said: "The two elders met as equals, yet among them there was something extraordinary. Today at Kuangxiao, I shall explain the principle for all of you once over.
It was thought that spring had departed with no place to be found; one did not know it had returned to enter right here."
Tiantong Jue’s verse says: "The bowstring and arrowhead mesh together; the net and pearls face one another. Shooting a hundred times, every arrow is never in vain;
gathering all reflections, every light is unimpeded. One attains the *dhāraṇī* of words and phrases and dwells in the *samādhi* of playful sport.
Wondrous within this interval, winding and turning, partial and perfect—necessarily it must be thus. Transverse and vertical, there is sovereign ease."
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the mechanism of the simultaneous pecking and hatching?
The Master said, "An echo. Zhenqing Wen’s verse says: When asked about the mechanism of pecking and hatching, Yunmen replied, "An echo. Yesterday thunder shook the heavens;
Last night the mountain streams rose high. Yuantong Xian said: "The mechanism of pecking and hatching was answered with the word 'echo. This is a mistake."
Empty skies and thunder suddenly pour forth torrents; last night, a deluge rained down until it covered the heavens. In several places, waves and billows battered the fishing boats.
A monk of Yunmen asked: "When it is neither the mechanism before one's eyes nor an event before one's eyes, what then? The Master said: "Overturned."
One saying. Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "Reverse one saying, divide one section; 'dying together and living together'—I resolve this for you.
The eighty-four thousand hairs are not merely phoenix feathers; thirty-three men enter the tiger’s den. Separately, separately! Turbulent, hurried, and frantic."
"The moon in the water. Zhengjue Yi said, "To turn this one statement upside down would clear the bones of men;
ten thousand miles without a single cloud, casting down a mass of snow. Separately, separately! This old Zen elder would rather let his tongue die. Yexuan Zun said:
To speak perversely is mere loquacity; for no reason at all, you have leaked the celestial mechanism. The four seas and nine provinces are needlessly exhausted;
you have flown from the Dragon Palace only to bore into an ant hole.
A monk of Yunmen asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "I do not understand. The monk asked, "Why do you not understand?
The Master said, "Simply maintain this state of not understanding."

The *Zhimen Zusong* says: "Your Majesty asks about the conduct of śramaṇas; the conduct of śramaṇas is most supreme. If one could teach others to realize it, the nature of karma would ultimately be difficult to escape."
Chan Master Nanyuan Yongzhen ascended the hall and said, "Upon this lump of raw flesh, ten thousand fathoms high, it stands like a sheer cliff.
At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "Is it not true, Master, that upon this lump of raw flesh it stands like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high? The Master said, "Yes.
The monk then overturned the rope seat. The Master said, "Look at this fellow making a mess! As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and drove him out.

Nanyuan. Ying’an Hua said: "This too is 'inviting a thief to ruin one's house. Had it not been for this monk’s daring to pull at the tiger’s whiskers, how could Nanyuan’s great merit from his many battles have been seen?
Nevertheless, Mingguo, let me provide you with another path: upon the bare flesh-ball..."
"Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. If a monk comes forth, he strikes him across the spine. Why? Because it is "the sword that kills and the blade that gives life.
Let those with eyes see! *Tuduce* says: "Do not trust what is straightforwardly straightforward; you must guard against benevolence that is not truly benevolent.
Although this monk brags recklessly about his heroism, Nan-yuan’s is the handiwork of a true master. Nevertheless, it is beautiful indeed.
"Excellent! If it were Jingshan, it would not be so. As soon as he heard the monk say, 'Is this the Master's words?
he would have struck him immediately. Why? Because at the point where one tests a person to the ultimate degree, one knows them the moment they open their mouth.
Songyuan Yue said: "This monk was entirely cautious yet displayed great boldness. Old Nanyuan was also fortunate to have such a son."
Gushan Gui’s verse says: "Holding the white sun in his palm, Covering gold coins with his tongue;
Standing like a sheer cliff of a thousand fathoms, His radiance pierces through the Brahma heavens. Jingshan Guangzhao says: "Upon the lump of red flesh, its use is intimate;
The host and guest have their reasons, yet each finds it difficult to prevail. When two camels meet face-to-face, There is no one upright in the world today."
The Chan Master Zhishan of Jinfeng. A monk asked, "What is it like when the four seas are at peace? The Master said, "You are still a man standing on the steps."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: The smoke and dust of the four seas have already settled; The bright moon before the window shines cold upon people.
No reward is granted to the general for his great achievement; I am suddenly weary of beholding the jeweled horse and golden trappings.
Chan Master Baoci Yu was asked by a monk, "I have heard the ancients say: 'When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed; when thought changes, the essence becomes distinct.
But what is it like when emotion has not yet arisen? The Master said, "Obstructed. The monk asked, "Since emotion has not yet arisen, what is there to be obstructed?
The Master said, "This young fellow has not yet met the right person."
Langya Jue said: "Baoci’s [action] was not necessarily an entering of the mud and water;
according to the gate of the patch-robed monks (śramaṇas), it is far, far removed. Huanglong Xin said: "Baoci was indeed obstructing Great Compassion with his minor compassion.
This monk also suffered a grievance together with him. The boatman had not yet met the right person. People nowadays often engage in such judgments of right and wrong."
[The Master] said, "I have understood it. I do not understand it in terms of right or wrong. How would you explain it? After a long silence, he said: "In the heavens, all stars bow toward the North;
among men, there is no water that does not flow east. Kaifu Ning said: "Baoci’s single barrier is the life-vein of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Releasing and gathering, it is unfathomable to sages and ordinary people alike. Whether it is a barrier or not a barrier—how can this be explained? Take it up and carry it away!"
The Odes and Documents return to his former hermitage; wild flowers and singing birds share the same spring. Tianyi Huai’s verse says:
"Once separated from Baozi, the life-vein of the patch-robed monks [is revealed]. If you wish to recognize the 'one thread,' it is two five-hundred-pieces.
Baizhang Yuan said: "If even the insentient are still separated, how can one pass through? Between a hair and a silk thread lies the path."
Ten thousand layers. A pity that those who run empty-handed at both ends cannot see its essence directly. Master Dazhongde said:
"Separated. In a cloudless blue sky, thunder crashes. Among the monks of the monasteries, as numerous as rice and hemp, how many are there who are true *siddha* adepts?"
Chan Master Qingfeng Chu was asked by a monk, "The Great Matter has already been accomplished; why then is it as if one has lost one's parents?
The Master said, "Without the spring breeze, the flowers do not bloom; yet once the flowers have bloomed, they are blown down."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "Having returned to your home mountain, do not be negligent. Exert all your strength to serve your parents morning and night.
When the mechanism is exhausted and effort forgotten, and gratitude and duty severed, One becomes an unfilial icchantika."
Master Chao of Shanglan was asked by a monk, "What is the fundamental matter of Shanglan? The Master said, "It is not borrowed from the thousand sages;
how could it be sought through the myriad functions? The monk asked, "When there is neither borrowing nor seeking, what then?
The Master said, "Can you possibly pick it up and place it in your own hands?"
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "A single expanse of empty clarity is fundamentally wondrous and perfect; within it, there is neither right nor partiality.
The auspicious grasses on Jewel Peak have no roots or stems; they do not await the labor of spring, for their color is naturally fresh."
When the Venerable Daigen Fu first arrived at Xuefeng, as soon as he ascended the Dharma Hall, he looked around at Xuefeng and immediately went down to see the administrative officials.
The next day, he returned to the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects and said, "Yesterday I offended you, Reverend.
Xuefeng replied, "I know it is such a matter; let it be. Later, a monk asked Yunmen, "What was the point of offending him? Yunmen—
He struck him.
Xuedou Xian said at the point where [Furong] saw and knew: "A spiritual teacher of fifteen hundred people was felled by Old Fu with a single glance;
he immediately raised his white flag of surrender. He also said at the point where [Furong] simply stopped: "As expected. At the very end:
It is said: "Even if you were to strike hundreds of thousands of ten-thousands of millions of people, what use would that be?
You must have the people of the entire earth eat the staff before you can truly establish Xuefeng. But tell me, what kind of eye does Elder Fu possess?"

The *Haixin Xin Song* (Verses on the Seal of the Ocean) says: General Li Guang was his peerless equal throughout past and present; he penetrated deep into the enemy's camp and preserved his life to avoid harm.
Without moving a blade or a shield, he won a small victory, and to this day his illustrious reputation remains celebrated along the frontier passes.
Chan Master Chongyun was asked by a monk, "What is it like to return to the root and attain the essential meaning? The Master said, "Long ago I forgot;
I do not recall the arising of dust.
Touzi Qing composed a verse on this: "The family is ruined and the people gone—where can one rely? Without mind and without sequence, I speak of seeking a homecoming."
For ten years, one forgets the path by which one came; should one briefly recall even a fragment, one knows nothing at all.
A monk asked West Chan Chan Master of Shuzhou, "What is the state that is beyond thought and deliberation? The Master said, "Who has seen the void nod its head in the night?"
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "A single point of numinous clarity—six senses cannot contain it. So manifest! Why need one strain one's eyes further?
The message within this is difficult for people to entrust; Only empty space nods its head in the dark."
Chan Master Suīyán Yàn asked Jiāshān, “In this way it is easy; not in this way it is difficult. In this way and in this way one is alert;
not in this way and not in this way one dwells in the realm of emptiness. ‘In this way’ and ‘not in this way’—I beg the Master to speak quickly.
Jiāshān said, “I am deceiving you, Dàlǐ. The Master then gave a shout, saying, “This old monk!”
"What kind of time is this? he said, and immediately went out. Later, a monk reported this to Yantou. Yantou said, "Alas!
This branch of our Buddha-dharma is being carried away in such a manner."
Fojian Qin said: "When Ruiyan asked thus, the wind did not rustle the branches; when Jiashan answered thus, the rain did not break the clods of earth;
when Yantou spoke thus, the grain ripened in harmony and the village elders sang for joy. Even so, all of them lacked awakening. Why?
Because worldly affairs should be judged by the standard of fairness; the human heart is difficult to reconcile with."
"The lunar disc is level. Daoyi Zhi said: "In Shuigan’s place of inquiry, the truth emerged from the prisoner's mouth;
when Jia Shan met someone, he extended his hand. Yantou possessed the skill of judgment. Their brilliance has shone through ancient and modern times.
Even so, each has their own basis. If one examines them closely, they are merely stirring up waves where there is no wind."
Chan Master Bāiyún Zàng was asked by a monk, "What is the place of profound depth? The Master replied, "A short man crossing a deep stream.
Dánxiá Chún composed a verse on this: "The white-haired youth possesses even greater wisdom; At the third watch of midnight, he crosses the vast and boundless."
Moving back and forth spontaneously without interruption, without needing a boat or a floatation bag, he reached Huanglong through the Wind Cavern.
Huanglong asked, "The stone horn pierces the path through the clouds; what is the meaning of this hanging cord? The Master said, "Red clouds enshroud the jade image;
the peaks embrace the mountains and rivers. Huanglong said, "If that is so, then you have come along with me. The Master said, "Together."
Still speaking in a low voice, Touzi Qing’s verse says: "A priceless bright pearl hangs in the dark; At night, one is about to thread it through a wooden man.
Who would have known that the earthen ox saw it? It swallows it into the abyss of crimson clouds and azure waves."
Chan Master Tong’an Zhi was asked by a monk: “How can one proclaim that which is beyond the reach of the two levels of teaching? The Master said:
“Not encountered in the partial; not lost in the profound.”
Dana Chun’s verse says: "This side and that side are both hard to encounter; A single phrase, free from self-interest, does not dwell in the center.
The crimson sun sinks behind the western peaks, Leaving but its solitary shadow to illuminate the eastern stream."
Fayan asked Xiu, the Mountain Master: "A hair's breadth of difference results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. How is this so?

Xiu said, "A hair's breadth of difference results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. The Master said, "If you speak thus, how can it be right? Xiu said, "I am simply like this; what about you, Elder Brother?
The Master said, "A hair's breadth of difference results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth. Xiu then prostrated himself.
[The student] bows.
Dongchan Qi said: "The mountain master responded in such a manner; why was he not accepted?

When [the student] later requested further instruction from Fayan, he also spoke in just this way, and [the student] was thereby able to proceed. Tell me, where does the point of doubt and error lie?"
"If you can see through this, then it is said that the Venerable Dao has a source. Wuzu Faian came out and struck him across the back with his staff.
Baoning Yong, acting on behalf of Master Xiu, said: "Even if you understand it in this way, how could you have attained it? Yuanfeng Man said: "Alas!
Master Xiu was truly a great practitioner, yet he had his eyes changed for a clay pellet. Do you know this yet?"
He further said: "To prostrate at the back is also to prolong imprisonment and increase wisdom. Jingshan Daokai said: "Fayan and Master Xiu were like drawing out silk from a spool;
their continuity was so dense and subtle that they upheld the tradition of the Dizang school.
One could say it was as if light filled their eyes. But if they were under the gates of Deshan or Linji, they would have had to buy more straw sandals to travel on foot."
Only then can it be attained. Why is it so? A difference of even a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
From where does one obtain this news?
Fengyang Zao’s verse says: The Master intentionally questions his fellow man; A single blow divides the two paths by a hair’s breadth.
Upon re-examination, the intent becomes clear; naturally pure and white, it does not arise from hearing.
Baoning Yong said: "Shicheng asked his fellow practitioner intimately: 'Without speaking of east or west, he directly pointed south.
The two paths of light and dark, coming and going, remain indistinct and winding amidst the mist and mists. Zhengjue Yi said: "How pitiable and how laughable is this cultivation!"
Master of the Mountain: Rising from the ground, one falls upon the ground. Face-to-face, the primary function is impossible to conceal;
it makes one recall the old Yunmen. Foyin Yuan said: "At that time, the six states were already at peace;
once peace had endured for long, they knew nothing of war. Master Xiu exchanged this for a 'long-snake' formation; everyone in the world understands life and death."
Tiantong Jue said: "When a fly sits upon the head of the scale, it causes the balance to be skewed; for ten thousand generations, the weights and measures have shone upon this inequality.
Only when the exact measure—down to the smallest fraction—is seen in its true nature, does it ultimately concede to the fixed star of my scale."
A monk with the Dharma-eye asked, "What is the matter of kalpas as numerous as dust motes? The Master said, "It is all present right now.
Yang Cigong composed a verse on this: The matter of kalpas as numerous as dust motes Is all present right now. The Patriarch did not understand; He sat facing the wall in silent contemplation.
Chan Master Lian-shan Guan was asked by a monk, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "Jade-green points through the color of lapis lazuli;
though red dust fills the eyes, not a grain of sand is seen."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: “The kalpa-fire blazes forth, yet the abode is formless; At the golden gate, one beholds no jade-pavilioned mansion.
In the jewel-heaven, clouds are thin and the Milky Way is clear; In the vast surging waves, how could the sands be moved?”
Chan Master Huangbo Huai went to visit Shushan. It happened that he was in the midst of the assembly in the Dharma Hall for formal practice.

The Master first looked over the great assembly and then posed a question, saying, "What is it like when one departs in a single kṣaṇa? Shushan said, "It fills and obstructs empty space; how will you go?
The Master said, "Filling and obstructing empty space is not as good as not going. Shushan ceased speaking. The Master then descended from the hall.
In front of the Sangha Hall, the Head Seat said to the Master, "Just now I observed that your response to the Abbot’s words was most extraordinary.
The Master replied, "This was merely impulsive; it was truly accidental. I venture to hope for your compassionate instruction regarding my ignorance and delusion.
The Head Seat asked, "In a single kṣaṇa, is there still any room for deliberation? At these words, the Master attained realization.
Xichan Xu’s verse says: "To fill the void is not as good as not going; the past and future limits are severed, and now there is no dwelling.
Riding backward upon the Buddha hall, he exits through the three gates; then he takes those three gates and hangs them upon the pillar."
Whenever the Third Patriarch, Chan Master Yuan, saw a monk approach, he would simply say, "A pity! A pity! The monk would ask, "Why do you say it is a pity?
The Master would reply, "If you do not show pity now, when will you?"
Foyan Yuan’s eulogy says: "Exhausting all one's strength, there is nothing that can be done; it is like pressing down a cow as it eats grass.
Without the patterns of brocade and embroidery, it is difficult to discuss elegant compositions."
Chan Master Huanglong Nan was asked by a monk, "What is it like when there is neither going nor coming? The Master said, "The three peaks of Mount Hua stand upside down.
The monk asked, "What is it like when there is both going and coming? The Master said, "The wind blows the willow catkins, rolling them like balls of fur."
The *Lingguang Guansong* (Verses on the Contemplation of Spiritual Radiance) says: "The Western maiden with skin like ice and snow, Her makeup is exquisite, her brows artfully painted.
A bystander’s brush may skillfully transmit her likeness, But how can she be seen from outside her door?"
Master Caoshan Benji was receiving guests. A monk asked about the five ranks in relation to the host. The Master said, "Which rank are you asking about now?
The monk replied, "I have come from the position of partiality; I request that the Master receive me within the position of correctness. The Master said, "I do not receive you. The monk asked, "Why?"

"What do you mean by 'not receiving'? The Master said, "I fear it would fall into a state of partiality. The Master then asked the monk, "As for this 'not receiving,' is it a response to the guest or not?
[The monk] replied, "It has already been a response to the guest. The Master said, "So it is, so it is."
Dana Chun’s verse says: Within the moon, the jade hare conceives in the night; In the sun, the golden crow broods its egg at dawn.
The pitch-black Kunlun walks through the snow; Turning his body, he shatters the crystal bowl.
Chan Master Suiyan Yan spent his entire life in the practice of constant sitting (*ekāsanika*). He would frequently call out to himself, "O Lord," and then respond to his own call.

He would then say, "Stay alert! In the future, do not let others deceive you. Later, a monk arrived at Xuansha’s place. Xuansha asked, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Suiyan. Xuansha asked, "What words or phrases did he use to instruct people?

The monk recounted the aforementioned story. Xuansha said: "‘Lord’—this is the name of the Buddha. ‘Response’—this is the name of the Dharma. ‘Stay alert!’—this is the name of the Sangha. If you can understand this, You will never again be deceived by others."
The first case is "playing with the spirit. It is truly strange. He asked again, "Why did he not remain there?
[The monk] replied, "He has already passed away. Zhaozhou said, "Can you still call out to him now and get a response? The monk had no reply.
Xuedou Xian said, "Heaven! Heaven! Yunfeng Yue said, "Making a living inside a ghost cave.
He then asked a monk standing nearby, "Do you recognize this old fellow Ruiyan? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Baoning Yong spoke on his behalf: "Why does the Abbot not hear [you] even when facing him?"
The *Foguo Baishou* (White Verses of Foguo) says: "Throughout one's life, constantly call out to the Host; Not being deceived by others, you are utterly unique.
Where has this present clarity gone today? Pine and cypress trees fill the mountains as a mournful wind arises. Zuyin Ming says:
A curved crescent moon gathers three stars; who can believe that the Mind-King is fundamentally at peace?
How laughable is the old abbot of Ruiyan, calling out in the deep night, forcing himself to be alert! Gushan Gui said: "The one Lord has died."
The single protagonist is alive; if one understands how to manipulate the essential spirit, both ends are thoroughly liberated.

Baiyang Shun said: Calling out oneself and responding to oneself is already alert and clear; One cannot be deceived, for the principle is not slight. The fragrance of the white lotus in the pond has not yet ceased;
The mountain colors before the eaves are green throughout the four seasons.
Chan Master Changqing Lǐng was asked by a monk: "When there is a question and an answer, the roles of guest and host are clearly distinct; but when there is neither question nor answer, what then?
The Master said: "Everyone they meet says they have retired from office, yet among those beneath the forest trees, not one has ever been seen."
The *Zhimen Zusong* says: Everyone says, "My mind has come to rest. But when questioned, where has it ever been?
Words and heart at odds, deceiving oneself; Driven along by the swift river of karma.
Regarding the family style of Great Sui Chan Master Zhen: A monk asked, "What is the family style of the Master? The Master said, "Painting a winnowing basket with red earth.
The monk asked, "I do not understand how this principle works. The Master said, "The winnowing basket has a rim; the rice cannot leap out."
Nantang Jing’s verse says: "Drawing a winnowing basket with red earth— Round and complete, without a single crack.
Even the Buddha-eye cannot see it; The Sea God does not know its price. Shaking up dust and raising clouds, there is nowhere to seek it;
Mountains high and seas wide, the white clouds are deep. Ying’an Hua says: "The winnowing basket has a rim; the rice cannot leap out. All the monks under heaven are naked..."
Keli: One must further turn back the pivot at the very top. Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, it is as black as lacquer.
Chan Master Puchan of Shaoshan was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Rootless grass on the summit;
without wind, the leaves sway of themselves."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: The solitary peak of Wondrous Summit is uniquely lush; A celestial, numinous sprout that never touches the ground.
Its verdant leaves sway of their own accord without a breeze; Its fragrant scent does not seek to rival the charms of spring.
