It disperses the canopy of heaven without a mind; It sustains the carriage of earth with power. It penetrates the profound source of a thousand ages; It establishes the pattern for the myriad forms.
The Way meets within the dust of every land. Everywhere is Samantabhadra. The gates of the multi-storied pavilion stand open.
"Everywhere is Maitreya.
While Master Yaoshan Yan was reading a sutra, a monk asked him, "Master, you usually do not permit people to read the sutras. Why [is that]?"
“What is it that you look at yourself? The Master said, “I am merely trying to cover my eyes. [The monk] asked, “May I learn this from you, Master?
The Master said, “If you were to look, even ox-hide would be pierced through.”
Changqing said, "What fault is there in the eye? Xuanjue said, "Tell me, does Changqing understand Yaoshan’s meaning or not?
Fenyang Zhao’s verse says: "Having reached the bottom, what further doubt could there be? Those who penetrate this are rare; even with such earnest instruction, it is still entrusted [to others]."
Entrustment. Every phrase is a profound mystery. Baoning Yong said: "Who can share this medicine for covering the eyes?
When the ox-hide is pierced through, the bones and hair turn cold. How many know of the five lakes and four seas? Densely written characters and sparse lines are all of one kind. Kumu Cheng said:
"Though there are a thousand mountains' moons before the gate, within the room there is not a single speck."
Dust. If the *palm-leaf* [scriptures] or the *tūṣāra* (frost/snow) obstruct the eyes, one must know that even the pure ground can delude people.
When Chan Master Linji Xuan entered the monks’ hall with Wang, the Palace Attendant, Wang asked, “Do the monks in this hall study the scriptures?
The Master said, “They do not study the scriptures. Wang asked, “Do they practice meditation? The Master said, “They do not practice meditation. Wang said—
"You do not study the sutras, nor do you practice Chan. In the end, what are you doing? The Master said, "I am teaching you all to become Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Wang said, "Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. What then?
The Master said, "I took you for a mere layman."
Touzi said in distinction: "Official, how can you value the ears and despise the eyes? Jingqing said in his commentary: "Recently, I have been throwing bricks to draw out jade. Weishan Zhe said:

"Attendant Wang may truly be called a gentleman of the Confucian gate and a master craftsman of the Chan gate. Had it not been for his clear discernment, how could right and wrong have emerged so sharply? Baizhen Yuan said: **Translation:** Touzi spoke differently, saying: "Official, why do you value the ears and despise the eyes? Jingqing’s commentary says:

"Lately, I have been throwing bricks to draw out jade. Weishan Zhe said: "Attendant Wang may indeed be called a gentleman of the Confucian school and a skilled artisan of the Chan school. Were it not for his clear power of discernment, how could right and wrong have been so sharply distinguished? Baizhen Yuan said:
He said, "The assembly, Linji truly possesses the one eye. If it were Yuan Tong, however, it would not be so.
'Though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a film. What then? I took you for a mere worldly man."
Let the great assembly try to judge this. Ying’an Hua said: "The wind blows and the grass bends; the leaves fall and one knows autumn.
Although Linji’s hammer was his fundamental tool, Changshi possessed the eye at the crown of his head.
Even so, when the Prefect entered the mountain today to meet this old monk, although there was no monastic hall to reach, there was likewise no Buddha-dharma to deliberate upon.
This alone is the point where he stands head and shoulders above others. But tell me, what serves as the proof? This very thing serves as the proof.
Jing-shan Gao’s verse says: "The rarest events, both mundane and supramundane, must rely on those of transcendent capacity to be revealed."
"Taking the very hands that mend the robes and stir the soup, he turns the True Wheel of the Tathāgata.
When Guiling praised the Chan Master’s return, his original teacher asked him, "What studies have you undertaken?
The Master replied, "It is exactly as it was before I left. Later, while the teacher was reading a scripture, a fly struck the window. The Master said, "The world is this vast!"
"Vast indeed! Why must you poke your head into old papers? The Master asked this with a look of surprise. The teacher replied, "I have a verse now:
'Unwilling to exit the Gate of Emptiness, even throwing yourself through a window is quite extraordinary; for a hundred years, one has pored over old papers.'"
Regarding the moment of emergence, Baizhang Cloud’s verse says: Seeking light out of craving, one drills through paper; how many difficulties lie in the inability to penetrate!
Suddenly, one stumbles upon the path from whence one came, and only then realizes that all along one has been deceived by the eyes.
Chan Master Muzhou Zong was asked by a monk, "Can one breath turn over the entirety of the Great Canon?
The Master said, "What kind of *bi-luo-chui* (meat pie) is there? Bring it here quickly!"
Gushan Gui’s verse says: "Muzhou only loved the sharpness of the awl's point; this monk did not see the squareness of the chisel's head.
Even if one could turn over hundreds of thousands of scriptural treasuries, such offerings as these would still be considered ordinary. Jingshan Guangzhao said:
A single breath turns the entire Great Canon: sudden and gradual, partial and perfect, provisional and real. Boundless wondrous meanings shine forth brilliantly;
yet originally, not a single character has he recognized.
Cen Master Yunju asked a monk, "What sutra are you reciting? The monk replied, "The Vimalakīrti Sūtra. The Master said, "I am not asking about the Vimalakīrti Sūtra;
what is it that you are reciting? At these words, the monk attained realization.
The *Fohuiquan* (Verses on the Spring of Buddha-Wisdom) says: "I do not ask what Vimalakīrti was thinking; a Korean hawk has flown through the clouds.
When the staff-tip strikes, there is no majestic spirit; how lamentable is Paozhuo of Mount Song! Wúwéizǐ says:
What one contemplates is indeed the Vimalakīrti Sūtra; each time it is raised, it becomes more refined. The parrot cannot return to its native land;
for the most part, its speech is too clear. Tianzhang Shan said: "When asked about the sūtra, do not ask about contemplating Vimalakīrti.
Do you clearly see what is being contemplated? If you wish to enter the ocean of dharmas as numerous as motes of dust, a single word will unfold them."
There is no need for much effort to emerge. The site of enlightenment is like clouds; following the wind, one is about to reach Yangzhou.
But the wind shifts the prow and the waters flow backward; reaching the shore in an instant relies entirely on the strength of the three old mariners—have no cause for worry.
Nantang Jing said: "Mount Sumeru is so high its peak cannot be seen; the great ocean is so deep its bottom cannot be seen.
Though one sifts through dust and stirs up clouds of soil, there is nowhere to find it. Turn your head around and you will bump into your own home."
While lecturing on a sutra, Zen Master Nanquan Yuan asked a Dharma master, "What sutra are you lecturing on? He replied, "The *Sutra of Maitreya’s Descent to Be Born in the World*.
The Master asked, "When will Maitreya descend to be born? He replied, "He is currently in the heavenly palace; he has not yet come. The Master said, "There is no heaven above."
"Maitreya, there is no Maitreya beneath the earth.
Dongshan raised this question to Yunju Deng, who said, "There is no Maitreya above the heavens; there is no Maitreya beneath the earth."
I do not know who gave him this name. When Dongshan was asked this, his meditation seat shook;
he then said, "When I was at Yunyan, I once asked the Old Man [Zhaozhou], and my brazier shook.
Today, being asked by you, I am covered in sweat all over. Dayang Yan said, "If the old monk raises it now, is there anyone who can understand?"
The questioner brought forth a question, saying, "The earth is shaking. Jingshan Daowu said, "It is not that the Zen seat does not tremble or the brazier does not shake;
however, these three great elders would have had to wait until Maitreya descends to be born in order to truly see Nanquan.
Suddenly, if a monk were to come forward and say, "There is no Maitreya in heaven," [the three elders would be seen].
Since there is no Maitreya below, how can one be instructed on how to respond to him? Simply say to him: "This old monk is at fault.
Foyan Yuan composed a verse on this: "The meditation seat was startled and shaken by the tea-soup; It provoked the descendants to act like no true men."
With his staff, he struck him repeatedly on the head, saying, "This shall also cause you to know the Red-Bearded Barbarian.
The Dharma Master Liang of West Mountain went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked, "What sutra do you lecture? The Master replied, "The Heart Sutra.

Mazu asked, "With what do you lecture it? The Master replied, "I lecture it with the mind. Mazu said, "The mind is like a skilled performer; the intellect is like the one who accompanies the performance."
The Master said, "If the mind cannot explain it, perhaps empty space can? [The student] replied, "Indeed, empty space can explain it.
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. The Patriarch called out, "Master of Sutras! The Master turned his head. The Patriarch asked, "What is this?
At these words, the Master attained sudden and great enlightenment and prostrated himself. The Patriarch said, "This..."
"Stupid teacher! Why do you prostrate yourself? At these words, the Master was so overcome that sweat poured from his entire body.
He then returned to the assembly and said, "I have spent my life lecturing on the sutras, believing that no one could equal me.

Today, however, Master Ma asked me a single question, and all the effort of my life has been dissolved like ice melting away. He then ceased his lectures and entered the Western Mountains, where he was heard from again.
Kaixian Ying said: "The teachings state that the eyes born of one's parents see the entire trichiliocosm.
As for Master Liang, where is he right now? Has he consumed the hundred herbs and hidden himself on a divine mountain?"
Is it that you maintain yourself through the power of meditative concentration while dwelling deep in mountain crags?
Or is it that your supernatural transformations are difficult for the eyes of worldly men to perceive? Or have you perhaps cast off the physical body to realize the bliss of nirvana?
Can anyone see this right now? If you can see it, you will be a monk with clear vision; but if you have not yet reached this state, do not simply stumble upon it by chance.

Regarding the "Pillar in the Dew" (Lùzhù), Zhengtang’s verse of explication says: "The bowstring is difficult to tie into a fine mandarin duck; how could one plant thorny burrs along the imperial path?"
It is laughable that the talkative old man Xiangyan says, "This year’s poverty is even worse than last year’s. Dongshan Kong said:
"Master Ma has blinded Master Liang; once he entered the Western Mountains, he never returned. I have thirty-two willow switches;
I shall send them to this wooden board in the mountains."
When the Venerable Fu of Taiyuan first served as a presiding master (zuozhu), he was lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* at Guangxiao Monastery in Yangzhou.

A Chan practitioner who had been stranded at the monastery by the snow went there to attend the lecture out of a desire for merit. When the lecture reached the section on the three causes of buddha-nature and the dharma-body of the three virtues, [Fu] said:

He spoke at length on the subtle principles of the Dharmakāya, whereupon the Chan practitioner laughed in derision. After the lecture ended, the Master invited the Chan practitioner for tea and asked him:

"My own aspirations have always been narrow and inferior; I have merely interpreted the meaning according to the texts. Having just been ridiculed by you, I fear there are points where I have failed to reach the truth. I humbly hope you will instruct me.
The Chan practitioner replied, "I truly laughed because the Master does not recognize the Dharmakāya. The Master said, "If this is how you explain it, what [is the Dharmakāya]?"
"It is not right. [The student] said, "I request the Master to explain it once more. The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the vast void:
vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, horizontally it spans the ten directions; it encompasses the eight poles and includes the two polarities.

Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade. The meditator said, "I do not say that what the Master has explained is incorrect; it is simply that what he has explained..."
"The reality of the dimensions and boundaries of the Dharma-body has not yet been recognized within you. The Master said, "Since it is so, you, a practitioner of Chan, should explain this to me.
[The student] asked, "Master, do you believe it? The Master replied, "How could I dare not believe it? [The student] said, "If that is so, Master, please suspend your lectures for ten days.
Sit upright in meditation within your room, withdrawing the mind and gathering the thoughts. Regarding all things, whether good or evil—"

He said, "Leave it for a while. The Master followed his instructions exactly. From the first watch of the night until the fifth watch, upon hearing the sound of drums and horns, he attained sudden and clear enlightenment.
He ran to knock on the Zen master's door. The Zen master asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I.
The Zen master scolded him, saying, "I taught you to uphold the Great Teaching and proclaim it in place of the Buddha; why have you come here tonight drunk and lying down?"
In the street, the Master said, "Zen Master, from now on I shall no longer dare to pinch the nostrils of my biological parents while lecturing on the sutras.
The Zen practitioner said, "Go for now; come tomorrow to see me. Thereupon, the Master ceased his lectures and traveled everywhere to visit various masters.
An ancient worthy composed this verse: "A single melody of the Xuanhe wind draws it long; When Master Fu hears it, the notes of Gong and Shang emerge.
To this day, the traveler in Yangzhou at night Vainly listens to the plum blossoms as they break his heart."

Regarding the discourse on doctrine: The World-Honored One was approached by the brahmin Dīrghanakha, who sought a debate. He made a prior agreement, saying, "If my doctrine falls, I shall cut off my own head.
The World-Honored One asked, "What is the thesis of your doctrine? The brahmin replied, "I take the non-acceptance of everything as my thesis."
The World-Honored One asked, "Do you see this as receiving [the teaching]? Zhi then shook his sleeves and departed.

When he reached the middle of the road, he realized his error and said to his disciples, "I must go back and cut off my own head to apologize to the Buddha. His disciples said, "It would be fortunate indeed to achieve victory before the assembly of devas and humans;
why should you cut off your head? Zhi replied, "I would rather have my head cut off before those who possess resolve than before those who lack it."
Having emerged victorious before the assembly, he sighed and said: "My thesis has failed in two ways. If this view is accepted, the point of defeat is coarse;
if this view is not accepted, the point of defeat is subtle. No one among gods, humans, or those of the two vehicles knows where my thesis fails;
only the World-Honored One and the great Bodhisattvas know where my thesis falls. He then returned to the presence of the World-Honored One and said:
"Since my doctrine has been defeated at both points, I shall cut off my head to apologize to the World-Honored One. The Buddha said, "In my Buddha-dharma, there is no such thing as this.

You should turn your mind toward the Way and leave the household life. Thereupon, the five hundred followers all simultaneously threw themselves before the Buddha, left the household life, and realized arhatship. (A variant version differs slightly.)

The Seventh Patriarch, Venerable Vasumitra, was once requested by Buddhanandi to engage in a formal debate on doctrine. The Patriarch said, "O Benevolent One, where there is debate, there is no true meaning;
where there is true meaning, there is no debate. If you intend to debate for the sake of meaning, it will ultimately not be a discourse on true meaning.
Buddhanandi, realizing that his teacher’s principle was superior, submitted with deep respect and humility.
The eleventh patriarch, Venerable Nayśa, was asked by Aśvaghoṣa: "I wish to recognize the Buddha; what is it?
The patriarch replied, "If you wish to recognize the Buddha, that which you do not recognize is it. [Aśvaghoṣa] said, "Since the Buddha cannot be recognized, how can one know it is him?
The patriarch said, "Since the Buddha cannot be recognized, how can one know it is not him? [Aśvaghoṣa] said, "This is the meaning of the saw. The patriarch said, "That is the meaning of the wood."
He asked again, "What is the meaning of 'saw'? Maming replied, "It is the same as for you, Master. Maming then asked, "What is the meaning of 'wood'?
The Patriarch replied, "You have been sawn apart by me. Thereupon, Maming believed and submitted.
The Twelfth Patriarch, the Great Being Aśvaghoṣa, formerly served as a non-Buddhist practitioner.

He would always carry a spear with a sword suspended from its tip and travel through the five regions of India, seeking out those to debate his doctrine. He declared, "If my doctrine falls, I shall cut off my head to apologize.
Hearing that Venerable Pārśva had a great reputation, he specifically requested to debate him. Pārśva asked, "What do you take your doctrine to be?"
The Patriarch said, "As for all verbal expressions, I am able to refute them all. Hui-xi then sat there in silence.
The Patriarch departed with a look of indignation, reviling him, saying, "I heard that you possessed great wisdom; yet when debating with me, not a single word could you utter.
Having traveled halfway on his journey, he said to his disciples, "My argument has fallen into error; my words were merely empty talk."
He was able to defeat them all. Since they had no further words to offer, [the opponent] thought, "I shall defeat myself," and was about to turn back and decapitate himself in apology.
At that time, the Venerable Pārśva transformed him so that he turned his heart toward the Dharma; together with his entire retinue, they then simultaneously went forth as monks.
The Patriarch’s Verse:
The Sixth Patriarch Master was poor and sold firewood to support his foster mother. He went to the Fifth Patriarch to seek the Dharma.

The Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Lingnan. The Patriarch asked, "What do you wish to seek? The Master said, "I seek only to become a Buddha. The Patriarch...
He said, "The people of Lingnan have no Buddha-nature; how can they attain Buddhahood? The Master replied, "People have north and south, but how could the Buddha-nature be like that?

The Patriarch, knowing he was of a different capacity, rebuked him, saying, "Go and work in the wine vats. The Master then entered the rice-pounding hall and began pounding rice while wearing a stone belt around his waist.
Later, when the Fifth Patriarch addressed the assembly, seeking a verse to bestow the robe and the Dharma, the Head Monk, Great Master Shenxiu, [composed one].
He presented a verse, saying: "The body is the Bodhi tree; The mind is like a bright mirror stand. At all times, diligently wipe it clean;
Do not let dust and grime settle upon it. When the Master heard this, he responded with a verse: "Bodhi originally has no tree; The bright mirror is likewise no stand.

From the beginning, there is not a single thing— Where, then, could dust and grime settle? The Patriarch silently recognized him. That night, he summoned the Master into his room and [instructed him] in secret.

He manifested the Dharma-eye of the Mind-essence and transmitted the command of the robe and bowl. Crossing the river, he passed over Mount Dayu to the south and returned to Caoxi to open the Dharma-gate of Dongshan.
Huanglong Xin’s verse says: "The Sixth Patriarch was no hero of those days; he hired another to write on the wall while he himself merely plastered it over."
Clearly there is a verse that says, "There is nothing," yet he accepted a single alms bowl from another house.

Fohui Quan said: "The single stream of Caoxi is cold from ancient times to the present; because you, Master, came, you stirred up waves and ripples. Carrying your bag, people at Mount Yuling pursued you in vain;
carrying stones, the multitude at Huangmei found it difficult to recognize [your true nature]. Foguo Bai said: "Seven hundred eminent monks in a dream..."
At midnight, under the moon, he returned alone to the south. Selling firewood and husking rice were his domestic affairs;
for what reason did he personally transmit the robe of the sixth generation? Zuyin Ming said: "A single verse hit the mark, and the entire assembly was subdued.
A hundred birds came, carrying flowers one after another. Remembering the path back to his ancestral mountain, he passed the robe through the Nine Rivers at midnight."
Caotang Qing said: "From among seven hundred monks, one was chosen: 'Originally there is nothing, and thus we are intimate.
At night he passed on the robe and bowl to Caoxi; the iron tree blooms in the spring of the second month."
The verse by Master Fudaishi of the Twin Trees states: "Night after night, one embraces the Buddha in sleep; Morning after morning, one rises together with him.
Whether rising or sitting, we are always in each other’s company; In speech and silence, we dwell together. Not a hair’s breadth separates us, Like a shadow following its form.
If you wish to know where the Buddha goes— Xuedou said: "Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes"— It is simply this very sound of your voice."
Xuansha said, "The Great Master Fu Daoshi of great and small caliber recognized nothing more than this 'brightly shining and spiritually alert' state.
Xuanjue challenged him, saying, "Tell me, did he recognize it or not? If he recognized it, he is Maitreya, the one destined for succession;
thus, he could not have recognized it. If he did not recognize it, then Xuansha’s words must not have been in vain. Xuedou Xian.
It is said: "The patch-robed monks of the world cannot leap out of this. Even those whose mouths hang on the wall have another aperture;
once they have been scrutinized, they are struck. It is further said: "Xuansha’s case is like striking the grass and startling the snake. Cuiyan Zhi said:
Whether you acknowledge it or not, next year there will be new branches; the spring wind continues to stir them without ceasing.
Tianyi Huai said: "Who has the melody of the Shanyu to trade for a city of illusory silver? After a long silence, he said:
"Having once suffered the bitterness of frost and snow, one is startled even by the falling of willow blossoms."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: When you wish to sleep, you sleep; when you wish to rise, you rise. Washing the face, the skin glows;
sipping tea, the beak is moistened. The great ocean gives birth to red dust;
level ground rises in waves. Ha ha! A-he-he! La-li-li! La-li!
The Verse of Master Fu says: “There is a thing prior to heaven and earth, Formless and fundamentally silent.
It is the lord of the myriad phenomena, Yet does not wither with the four seasons.
(Yuanzao Dharma Master is an alternative attribution. Yunfeng Yue said: “Tell me, what thing is this? Daowu added: “The water rises and the boat rises higher.”
Zhenyun said: "Let me ask you: what kind of thing is this? Do you recognize it? If you recognize it, then heaven and earth, the great land, and all the myriad phenomena will be clearly illuminated.
If you do not recognize it, you will be squeezed by external objects and unable to turn yourself around.
Langya Jue said: "What a fine verse! Yet it has become two separate pieces. If anyone can examine it thoroughly, I grant that they possess one [eye of wisdom]."
"A single eye. Baoning Yong held up his staff and said, "Do not call this a 'staff'!
Wuzu Yan said, "The ancients speaking thus may be called 'spreading flowers upon brocade'; it is truly extraordinary.
How do you all understand this? Today, Bailian follows the capacities of later students and does not begrudge [the effort]."
The eyebrows are also expressed in verse: "Existence within existence; non-existence within non-existence; the subtle within the subtle; the coarse within the coarse. Master Pang’s verse says:
"In the ten directions, all gather together; each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting the Buddha."
"The mind attained the top rank and returned home.
Baizhang Yuan said: "Every day we act and function, speaking of yellow paths and white ways.
If you call it 'mind,' there is no time of attaining the top rank; if you do not call it 'mind,' there is likewise no time of attaining the top rank. Now tell me, what is it?"
"How can one attain the 'Pass with Honors' in the Heart-Emptiness examination? After a long silence, he said: "I told you it was a dragon, yet you stubbornly refused to believe;

as expected, you have seized the embroidered banner and returned. Daopei Zhe said: "Under the gate of Huiguang, one is directly assisted to transcend and ascend without passing through the formal stages of the examination.
Since you all have arrived here, the winds and clouds are spread across the earth and your fangs and claws are already formed; you need only—"
"Lacking the sound of thunder, one’s tail is scorched. Now, for all of you, I shall strike the sudden thunder!
With this, he struck the meditation seat with his staff and descended from it. Cangtang Qing said, "Now, is there anyone who has attained the 'Passing of the Mind' at the top of the list?
Even if one were to attain the 'Passing of the Mind,' they are still only halfway to the gate of Baofeng. Tell me, what is it like to reach [the end]?"
"What is the first phrase? After a long silence, he said: "Wherever there is a path to ascend, even those of superior stature will walk it.
Fohuiquan’s verse says: "The head-wrap is dusty, the boots and robes are tattered; in the field where Buddhas are chosen, there are not two."
If one attains the Way and returns home with an empty mind, that single blow upon the crown of the head is difficult to let pass.
Zen Master Dongshan Jia’s verse on awakening to the Dharma preached by insentient beings says: "How wondrous! How wondrous!
The preaching of the insentient is inconceivable. If you try to hear it with your ears, you will never understand; Only when you hear it with your eyes do you truly know."
Nantang Jing’s verse says: "How wonderful! How wonderful! The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms are all treasures; every head and every object manifests the family's precious jewel.
To those who do not recognize them, they are but weeds."
Cen Master Yangshan Ji asked Xiangyan, "I have heard that you, my junior brother, have recently composed a verse on the realization of the Way. Try reciting it for me.
After Xiangyan had finished reciting it (the verse is found in the section on Realizing the Way), the Master said, "This is merely something you fabricated during your leisure time.

Xiangyan then offered another verse, saying: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is the first true poverty. Last year I lacked even the space for a single awl to stand upon."
"This year there are no awls," the Master said. "You have only attained the Buddha’s Zen; you have not yet attained the Patriarch’s Zen.
Later, Xiangyan presented another verse, saying: "I have a device; with a blink of an eye, I show it to him. If he still does not understand, I shall call for the novice.
The Master said, "I am glad that you, my junior, have now understood the Patriarch’s Zen."
Xuánjué challenged him, saying: "Tell me, are the Buddha-dhyāna and the Patriarchal-dhyāna distinct or not?
Chángqìng Líng said: "Sit down on them both at once. Yúnjū Xī challenged him, saying: "Among the assembly, it is debated that the Buddha-dhyāna is shallow and the Patriarchal-dhyāna is deep.
But why did Xiāngyán at that time not ask, 'What is the Patriarchal-dhyāna?'"
"Zen. If one were to set aside this question, where would it be? Langya Huijue said:
"Emperor Wu sought immortality but did not attain it; Wang Qiao sat upright and ascended to heaven. Dayang Qingzhe said:
"Xiangyan may be said to have not a single tile above and not a single point for his staff below—naked and bare, utterly clean and clear, with nothing to grasp. If not..."
This was Yangshan. He almost let this fellow off. Why? For unless one endures the power of snow and frost, how can one know the steadfast character of the pine and cypress?
Nantang Jing’s verse says: "When sound is not sound, only then does one see the Way; where form is not form, that is immediate emptiness."
Only after a hundred refinements does fine gold become a vessel; only after a sharp sword is ground anew does its efficacy appear. Kumoku originally said:
"To have no land and not even a needle’s point is not yet poverty; to know there is nothing and still maintain the state of having no self—that is poverty.
Lately, my own poverty has become extreme; I do not see the person who was poor in the beginning.
*Chanlin Leiju*, Scroll Eight; *Chanlin Leiju*, Scroll Nine.
Names of Head Monks (*tou-shou*), Administrative Officers (*zhi-shi*), and Attendants (*shi-zhe*).
The nun-disciple and novice Xingdong,
whose name was Master Boyuan Zhe, arrived together with Master Dongshan and his senior companion, Master Mi. The Master asked the two elders, "What is it?"
[The Master asked: "Where do you come from? [Dong] said, "From Hunan. [The Master] asked, "What is the surname of the Military Governor (Kanchalsi)?

[Dong] said, "He has no surname. [The Master] asked, "What is his given name? [Dong] said, "He has no name. [The Master] asked, "Does he still attend to affairs of state? [Dong] said, "There are naturally the halls and offices [for such matters]."
The Master asked, "Did you go in and out? He replied, "I did not go in and out. The Master said, "How could it be that you did not go in and out?
Dong shook his sleeves and left. The next morning at dawn, the Master entered the hall and called the two senior monks forward.
The Master said, "Yesterday, when I questioned you on the matter, your words did not accord with my intention; I have been uneasy all night. Today, I ask you to provide another turn of phrase. If..."
"This accords with my old monk's intention. He then opened the gruel and stayed together for the summer retreat. Yunmen said, "I ask the Master instead: [what about] 'entering and exiting'?

without applying rouge or powder, she possessed her own radiant splendor. Though the dark gate is secured with golden locks, she cannot be detained;

For forty-nine years there has not been a single word. With a sudden pull, the golden locks of the celestial qilin are severed;

Master Linji Xuan addressed the assembly, saying: "Upon this ball of red flesh, there is a true person of no rank who constantly enters and exits through the gate of your faces.
Those of you who have not yet attained verification, look! Look! At that time, a monk came forward and asked: "As for..."
"What is this 'person of no-position'? The Master descended from his rope-seat, seized the monk, and said, "Speak! Speak! The monk was speechless.
The Master gave him a slap, pushed him away, and said, "What kind of dried-up dung-heap is this 'person of no-position'?"
Xuefeng Cun said, "Linji is very much like a white-handed thief. Xuedou Xian said, "Now, a skilled thief is unknown even to gods and ghosts.
Since he has been seen through by Xuefeng, Linji was no good hand at it.
He then called to the assembly, saying, "Today Xuedou has changed your eyes for you all. If you do not believe me—"

"Each person should return to their own quarters and examine it for themselves. Langya Huijue said, "Linji may truly be said to have crossed over the nine bends of the icy river and picked up his whole body upon the edge of a sword."
Baizhang Yuan’s verse says: "The spring breeze surges, warming heaven and earth; Everywhere, the mountains are hidden within mists and clouds.
The True Person of No Rank cannot be sought; Falling flowers are seen again as they follow the flowing stream. Baoning Yong said:
Stirring up dust and scattering soil, there is nowhere to hide; entering and exiting through the face, it is truly fierce and bold. To urinate and defecate is but a trivial matter;
amidst this vast expanse, who can distinguish between stench and fragrance? Foyin Yuan said: "The Bian-jade is flawless, its brilliance eclipsing the sun.
Though the King of Qin coveted it, he could not outwit it. Alas, it has now fallen into the hands of Zhang Yi; with a single sweep, it is cleared away."
The wind fills the road as he returns home. Tongzhao said: "Linji spoke of the 'True Person of No Rank. I urge you not to seek it further.
On the Bird Path there is no merit, and those who travel it are rare; at the top of the hundred-foot pole, one must reach it for oneself."
As soon as the Buddha-mind speaks, sound and form do not disturb the eyes and ears; heaven and earth have always shared the same root.
Suddenly encountering a crying bird beneath the crags, one turns the body and arrives again at the pine gate.

Linji’s informal discourse (xiaochan) says: "Sometimes I take away the person but not the environment; sometimes I take away the environment but not the person; sometimes I take away both person and environment;
and sometimes I take away neither person nor environment. Kefu stepped forward and asked, "What is taking away the person but not the environment?
The Master said: "The warm sun brings forth life, spreading a carpet of brocade; the infant’s hair hangs down."
[The whisk] was white as silk. [A monk] asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master said, "The imperial decree has already been issued throughout the land;
the general beyond the frontier has cut off all smoke and dust. [The monk] asked, "What is 'seizing both person and environment'?

The Master said, "Ping and Fen have already submitted; he dwells alone in one region. [The monk] asked, "What is 'neither seizing person nor seizing environment'? The Master said, "The King ascends [the throne]."
The jeweled palace; the village elders sing and chant.
This accords with the verse of restoration, which says: "To seize the person but not the environment—this is itself the source of confusion.

If you wish to seek the profound meaning, your deliberation will only lead to reproof. The pearl of the black dragon shines brilliantly; the shadow of the moon and cassia tree sways. Face-to-face, there is nothing.
Mutually conflicting, one would still be entangled in the net. To seize the object but not the person—searching for the truth through words, where is it real?
To ask about Chan is for Chan to be a delusion; to investigate principle is for principle to be alien. The sun shines and the cold light grows faint; the mountains sway and the verdant hues renew.

Even if you were to attain a profound realization, it would be no more than dust in the eye. When both person and environment are simultaneously seized, the true command has been exercised from the beginning.
Regardless of Buddhas or Patriarchs, they speak of the sentiments of the holy and the ordinary; yet to attempt to violate this is like encountering a wood-blind man with a "blowing-hair" sword.
To advance further in seeking a wondrous realization is to deliberately strike at one's own vital spirit.

When person and environment are both unassailable, when the intent of reflection is not biased, when host and guest do not differ in their speech, and when the principle of question and answer is complete—then one treads upon the moon in the clear pool and pierces through [the veil].
The Azure Sky cannot clarify its wondrous function; beings remain submerged in the absence of conditions.
When Zen Master Datong Ji was asked by a monk, "What is the person of original nature? the Master replied, "We dwell together, yet we do not know one another."
[The student] said, "If that is so, I shall go to pay my respects. The Master said, "In secret, one writes of a grieving heart;

please prepare a meal at the time of the midday offering, eat it yourself, and then send one portion back to me. The monk prepared the meal, ate it himself, and [forgot to send the portion].
He then threw all his household affairs into total disorder and remained lying on his bed. The Master waited for a long time for him to come, but when he did not, he returned.
Seeing the monk still lying there, the Master lay down at one side as well. The monk then got up and left. Later, after the Master had settled elsewhere, he said:

Identifying the Star of the Platter. Zhandang Zhun said: "This old fellow Zhaozhou was more prone to anger than joy;

Zen Master Longshan was dwelling in a hermitage. When Zen Master Dongshan Jia and his senior companion, Master Mi, were traveling on pilgrimage, they saw vegetable leaves floating in a stream.

there, indeed, they see an old bhikṣu with bushy eyebrows. This bhikṣu—how cold and shrill! He takes the pure breeze as his thread.

He wished to abandon his hermitage to travel widely for study. That night, the local deity informed him, "Master of the Hermitage, there is no need for you to wander.

When he questioned him, the Dragon raised a single finger. The Master suddenly attained great enlightenment and no longer traveled elsewhere. Thereafter, whenever anyone asked him anything, he would only raise a single finger.
At the time of his death, he said to the assembly, "I have obtained the 'one-finger Zen' of the Heavenly Dragon;
I shall never exhaust its use throughout my life. He then raised a single finger and passed away.
Changqing addressed the assembly, saying, "Fine food is not fit for a person who is already full.

Yunju Xi said, "As for Xuansha speaking in such a manner, did he approve of him or not?"

Did Zhizhe still attain awakening? If he did, why is it said that his realization was muddled?

Once he cast a piece of wood into the vast ocean, the night waves together received the blind turtle. Foguo said: "The mechanism of question and answer is not easily met;
without money, it is hard to cultivate fine elegance. When there is something on the mind that cannot be spoken, one can only be busy."

When Chan Master Xuefeng Cun was residing in a hermitage, two monks came to pay their respects.

Upon seeing them approach, the Master propped open the hermitage door with his hand, stepped out, and asked, "What is this? The monks also replied, "What is this? Thereupon, the Master lowered his head and returned to the hermitage.
Later, the monks went to Yantou, who asked, "Where have you come from? They replied, "From Lingnan. Yantou asked, "Have you ever been to [Xuefeng]?"...
Xuefeng asked, "Have you been there? The monk replied, "I have. Xuedou asked, "What words or phrases did he say? The monk recounted the previous conversation.

Xuedou asked, "What did he say? The monk said, "He was speechless; he simply lowered his head and returned to his hut. Xuedou sighed, "Alas! In the beginning, I regretted not telling him the 'final phrase.

The Master said, "Although Xuefeng was born of the same lineage as I, he does not die of the same lineage as I. If you wish to know the final word, it is simply this.

One must discern: going and returning from north, south, east, and west; deep in the night, we look together at the snow upon a thousand crags. Baizhang Yuan said:

The staff that transformed the pond into dragons; the shuttle that allowed the potter’s family to hibernate. Those born from the same branch have their destiny;

One day, she instructed the girl to embrace the hermit firmly and asked, "At this very moment, what is it like?

This can be known. One day, atop a hundred-foot pole, one makes a "loss. It requires exhausting all the strength of one's lifelong efforts;

Master Guishan Yan addressed the assembly, saying: "All you monks say you go to various places to study and learn.
But I wonder, what is it you seek to penetrate? What is it you seek to learn? Is there anyone here who has attained such penetration? If there is, please come forward and respond."
Everyone looked on with expectation. The various masters asked: "Are you practicing Chan? Are you practicing the Way? Are you practicing for the Buddha? Are you practicing for the Dharma?

Are you practicing for Vairocana, the Master of the Dharmakāya? Or are you practicing the matter that transcends the Buddha—the phrase beyond Nirvāṇa? If you are truly practicing this, you will not have committed a great falsehood."
To call this "the aspiration for higher realization" is to have no connection at all with the various *ho-shangs*.
Zen Master Fengxue Zhao was asked by a monk, "What is the point of intimacy for a student?
The Master said, "On the southern side of Mount Sumeru they beat the drums together; on Mount Helan they kick leather balls."
Touzi Qing’s verse says: "Intimately, I once extended my inquiry to the old man; The East Mountain sings and the North Mountain chants.
To play with the tide, one must be a traveler from Jiangnan; For other words, he returns them to the people of Hanland."
Chan Master Shoushan Nian was asked by a monk, "What is the place where a student applies the mind? The Master said, "I find it strange that your question is so late.
Tiantong Qing composed a verse on this:
Before a word is spoken, it is difficult to clarify the sentiments of delusion and enlightenment; Only when speech is uttered does one manifest the person of sincere heart.
They greedily seek the jade of progress and fame; who would believe that the numinous sprout does not require the spring?
Whenever Chan Master Wuzu Yan encountered a monk seeking instruction, he would simply say, "I have no leisure for such things."
Foyan Yuan’s verse says: "Neither side shall bear the burden of mutual offense; the practitioner shall never lose their hook or awl.
Though I do not blind the eyes of sentient beings, I am well able to strike their mouths with my fist."
The Fifth Patriarch said, "For over ten years I have traveled to study, visiting dozens of spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
I thought I had reached a definitive understanding; yet when I came before Yuanjian of Fushan, I could not open my mouth again. Finally, I arrived at Baiyun."
Because he bit into a single iron sour dumpling, it was truly replete with a hundred flavors. But tell me, how would you express the single phrase regarding the stuffing?
The flower blooms like a cockscomb, enchanting the early autumn; who can dye its purple silk head?
Sometimes the wind stirs and they lean against one another repeatedly, as if vying before the steps without ceasing.
Xichan Xu said, "The Old Monk Wuzu speaking in such a manner is much like a beggar seeing small profit.
Songyuan Yue said, "Wuzu speaking in such a manner still lacks awakening."
The verse by Yue’an Guo says: "White clouds and iron-stewed dumplings—difficult for monks to bring to their mouths.
Suddenly, when one bites through them, one lets out a great lion’s roar."
While on a visit to Chan Master Yunyan Cheng, Daowu returned from Nanquan to Yaoshan.
The Master asked Yaoshan, "What is it to walk among those of different species? Yaoshan said, "I am weary today; wait until another time to come. The Master said:
"Such-and-such a person brought this object for this purpose and came to the mountain," [the guest] said. The Master replied, "Go on for now. The Master then went out.
Hearing from outside the abbot’s quarters that the Master had not recognized [the guest's meaning], Dao Wu unconsciously bit his finger until it bled. Dao Wu then came down and asked the Master.
"Brother Teacher, go ask the Master there; what is the karmic cause? The teacher said, "He will not speak for my sake.
I then bowed my head. Danxia Chun’s verse says: "Hungry, he eats tender grass as he goes to the distant mountains; Thirsty, he drinks cold spring water as he returns from the winding ravine."
Wandering and dissolute, one does not till the empty land of the kalpa. At twilight, what need is there to urge with songs of herding?
One day, an old friend came to visit Master An Chan of Luofu and asked, "In the blink of an eye, several years have passed; where have you been escaping hardship?
The Master replied, "I have been right here in the midst of the marketplace. The friend said, "Why do you not go to a place where there are no people? The Master replied, "There are none."
"What difficulty is there for a person to dwell in the midst of departure? [The student] asked, "Suppose, for instance, one were in the midst of a bustling marketplace; how could one escape it?

The Master said, "Though one may be in the midst of a bustling marketplace, nevertheless, no one recognizes him. Thus, the person was at a loss. He asked again, "Regarding the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven..."

At this point, the local man transmitted one person’s teaching. [The man] asked, “What if neither side condescends to bend? The Master said, “An old rustic does not speak of court affairs at his gate.

[The man] asked, “What matters, then, should he discuss? The Master said, “Unless one meets someone different, one never opens their fist. [The man] asked, “If someone who has not come from the court should meet him, would he still speak of it? The Master said: *Note:
This dialogue is a classic example of the "encounter dialogue" (wenda) style of Chan Buddhism, where the Master uses metaphors and paradoxical statements to test and guide the interlocutor.*
Those whose capacities lie beyond the reach of measurement merely exhaust themselves by witnessing; thus, no one can respond.
A monk from Luopu asked, "When a student intends to return to his hometown, what then? The Master said, "The house is ruined and the people are gone;
where would you go, my son? The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall not return. The Master said, "The remaining snow before the courtyard melts under the sun; the room..."
Who shall sweep away the internal dust of the mundane world?
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "The road to the peaceful realm is vast and far; My longing for home is deep, beyond the reach of thought.
Having cast off all to arrive home, what is there to possess? The crystal jewel-palace locks in the moonlight."
The Wayman Heshangxi came to visit Chan Master Luopu An. An asked, "Since we parted at Li Creek, how many years have passed now? The Wayman replied, "Master, you still remember events from long ago.
An said, "I am told that waymen generally forget the passage of years and months. The Wayman said, "Master, your administrative duties are many; allow me to observe carefully first. An said: *Note:

This dialogue is a classic example of the "encounter dialogue" (wenda) style of Chan literature, where the master’s response is intended to test or provoke the student's realization rather than provide information.*
When struck, he struck back; such is the Chan adept. The other said, "I am capable of it. An said, "The practitioner’s mountain affairs are many.
Danxia Zhiqian’s verse says: "Such news is not ordinary; from every branch of the moon-bright cassia, far-reaching fragrance spreads."
Last night, Lady Cháng’ē displayed her ingenuity; her eyes gaze directly upward at the embroidered mandarin ducks.
Guokong Master Cheng was asked by a monk, “What is one’s original father and mother? The Master replied, “One whose hair does not turn white.”
The guest asked, "What shall I offer? The Master said, "A sincere meal of rice-less gruel; before the hall, one does not inquire after kin. Danxia Chun offered this verse:
"Stepping out the door, the entire world lacks a true friend; Entering the gate, what fills the eyes is no relative."
In the empty chamber, the night is cold; what is there within? The bright moon in the azure sky serves as its neighbor.

When Chan Master Baizhang Hai returned from accompanying Mazu on a mountain excursion, he suddenly wept. His colleagues asked him, "Are you thinking of your parents?
The Master replied, "No. They asked, "Were you insulted by someone? The Master replied, "No. They then asked, "Why are you weeping? The Master said, "Go ask the Master.
The colleagues went to ask Mazu, to whom Mazu replied, "Go back and ask him yourself. The colleagues returned.
He went to the quarters and saw the Master laughing heartily. A fellow practitioner asked, "Just now you were crying;
why are you laughing now? The Master replied, "Just now I was crying; now I am laughing. The fellow practitioner was left bewildered.
Foyan Yuan’s verse says: "A single thought stirs the spirit once; Unawares, it turns into a fresh laugh.
Clouds atop the ridge peak never rest; Water flowing down the ravine is too busy. Gushan Gui said:
Worldly fame and profit, leisure, honor, and disgrace—clouds and rain falling in profusion, shifting with a single hand.
Sorrow and joy follow one another, beyond the power of words to describe. When the staff has no eyes, the yellow millet is ripe. Jingshan Gaofeng said: "Sometimes laughing, sometimes weeping;
sorrow and joy mingle, urging one on in secret. How can this principle be explained to others? A broken string must..."

"Obtaining luan-bird glue to mend [the broken strings]. Songyuan Yue said: "Weeping does not reach its end; laughing does not reach its end. I turn my belly inside out and pour forth my entrails to tell you:
father and son are not kin—those who know do not know. Lifting up the head, there are three catties of iron behind it."
Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Zhaozhou asked him, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To Min. Zhaozhou said, "The military forces there are numerous;
you must avoid them before you can proceed. The monk asked, "Where should I go to avoid them? Zhaozhou said, "Just so."
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: The monk went south toward Min; the road was not far. He reported that the troops were clamoring and noisy.
When asked where the Master had taken refuge to avoid them, He was sleeping soundly just as the sun reached its zenith. Fohui Quan said:
On the road back to the Seven Fujians, eyes clash in combat; to avoid them, one must ensure no trace remains. Where exactly is the place to hide?
Ten thousand layers of green mountains beyond the clouds. Zhengjue Yi said: "I have heard it said that the troops in Fujian are numerous;
I urge travelers to first avoid the weapons of war. At the parting of ways, he pointed out a place to hide—limitless and heroic.
The Master could not help it.
When Chan Master Changsha Cen returned from wandering the mountains and reached the gate, the Head Seat asked, "Where have you come from, Reverend?
The Master said, "I have come from wandering the mountains. The Head Seat asked, "To what places did you go? The Master said, "At first I followed the fragrant grasses; then again I followed..."
The falling flowers turn back. The assembly said, "It is very much like the spirit of spring. The Master said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping onto lotuses.
Xuedou Xian said, "Thank you, Master, for your response. Baizhang Yuan said, "Assembly, tell me:
was Changsha within the four seasons—spring, summer, autumn, and winter—or was he outside of them? Do you wish to understand? A single breath does not..."
The words contain the image: where can the myriad spirits offer thanks for such impartiality?
Xuedou’s verse says: "The great earth is free from even a speck of dust; who has not opened their eyes? At first they follow the fragrant grasses away."
Again, returning with the falling flowers: a weary crane perches upon a cold tree; a mad monkey howls atop an ancient terrace.
How boundless is the sentiment of Changsha! *Du!* Fangyi of Shangfang said: "Fluttering mountain fragrances fly everywhere along the path; Wildflowers fall away, the grasses grow disheveled.
The spring breeze holds boundless, profound meaning— If the yellow oriole cannot speak it, to whom shall it be told? Fojian.
Qin Yun said: Walking alone, he never spoke a word; Meeting people, his mouth would open at once. At first he followed the fragrant grasses away;

Then again he pursued the falling flowers back. Thin mist filters the crimson sun; Light smoke mingles with the green moss. If you seek to understand this through poetic lines, You bury the genius of the Dharma King.
Chan Master Zhuyou asked a monk, "Ācārya, have you come here to roam the mountains and enjoy the waters, or have you come to seek the Way and study Chan?
The monk said, "Venerable Sir, please try to say something. The Master said, "Carving oysters and engraving clams—you do not avoid the mud; it is a waste of your effort to have traveled so far.
The monk said, "Though my whole body is made of iron, I am still struck by this single pole. The Master said, "When an army surrenders, its soldiers are not executed."
Yuangwu Keqin said: "Gathering before the word; killing after the phrase. Steep and swift, not permitting even a breath of wind to pass.
Even with a beak like a nail and a tongue of iron, there would be no place to peck or bite. But tell me, why is it so? It is because no one can find an advantage."
An ancient worthy composed this verse: Wandering through mountains and playing by the waters is but an ordinary affair; Returning at dawn, my hair is already like hoarfrost.
Treading through my straw sandals, I turn my head to look back: The cry of a few monkeys resounds through the land of white clouds.
Chan Master Yangshan Ji asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Mount Lu. The Master said, "Have you ever been to the Five Elders Peak?
The monk replied, "I have not been there. The Master said, "Then you, Reverend, have never truly traveled the mountains."
Yunmen said: "These words are all due to compassion; they are talk that descends into the weeds. Weishan Xiu said:
"People nowadays all say that because of compassion there is talk that descends into the weeds. They only know how to grasp at the moon, yet they do not realize the depth of the water.
Had Yunmen been careful with his lips at that time, I wonder how later generations would have dealt with it?"
This is indeed a conversation. However, the water jelly has no eyes; in seeking food, it must rely upon the shrimp.
Huanglong Xin said, "Yunmen and Yangshan had only the heart to accept the jade tablet, yet lacked the intention to cut the city walls.
Little did he know that this monk had already led him astray all at once. Today, Huanglong is once again attempting to treat a dead horse with medicine. He then picked up his whisk.
Yangshan was about to give [the staff] to the assembly; as the monks were about to receive it, the Master struck him. Dayue Zhe said:

"Yangshan may truly be said to have outshone his predecessors and surpassed those who came after. Although Yunmen grasps the essential principles of the school and serves as a bolt for all the monks under heaven, how can he avoid raising waves where there is no wind?
Do you recognize this monk? He has come directly from Mount Lu."
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: Entering the weeds and emerging from the weeds—who can discern this? Layer upon layer of white clouds;
the red sun shines brightly. Looking left, there is no flaw; looking right, one is already old. Do you not see? Hanshanzi set out far too early.
For ten years he could not return; he forgot the path by which he came.
A monk from the Great Sui dynasty took his leave, and the Master asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Wutai to pay homage to Mañjuśrī.
The Master held up his whisk and said, "Both Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are right here. The monk drew a circle and tossed it behind his back.
Afterwards, he spread out both hands. The Master said, "Attendant, give this monk a cup of tea.
Baofu Zhan said, "Had there not been those subsequent words, one would have laughed at this patch-robed monk.
Yunmen spoke differently, saying, "In India they cut off heads and arms; here, take it yourself and go out. Wuzu Jie said, "It was not because of Da Sui..."
"One matter does not increase one's wisdom. Xuedou Xian said, "The sword that kills and the sword that gives life—discern them with the eye of realization.
Weishan Xiuzhou said, "The tea of Daisui is not of the same kind as the tea of Zhaozhou.
Since it is not of the same kind as Zhaozhou’s tea, those who obtain it are few. This monk has obtained it; yet what excellence does he possess? Nevertheless..."
"Yi’s wealth is to me like floating clouds. Tiantong Jue said: "He who recognizes the law fears;
he who deceives his enemy perishes. To select milk from water, one must be a king of geese."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: The light flashes from the tip of the staff; The folds are wrinkled within the monk’s robe. Shoulder-crossed and back-burdened, he strides out the gate;
It is well that no one dares to detain him. An ancient worthy said: "A single bright moon shines upon the Xiao and Xiang rivers;
No longer meeting anyone, he asks not of his hometown. By nature, he is accustomed to wandering at the ends of the earth."
Guest: "Let the monkey cry until it breaks one's heart.
Yantou was asked by a monk who was taking his leave: "Where are you going? The monk replied: "I am going into the mountains to pay my respects to Xuefeng.
Yantou said: "If Xuefeng asks about me, simply tell him that these days I have been at the lakeside in Ezhou."
"Stay! Just buy a black old woman for three coins and spend your days every day catching shrimp and clams;
just pass your time like that. A monk went to Xuefeng and recounted these words. Xuefeng said, "That poor little ghost is so utterly happy!
(The *Lian Deng* records this as: "Buy a shrimp-catcher.")
Master Yiyun said: "Since you are a destitute ghost-child, why are you not thoroughly happy?
Have you not heard it said that 'a guest who enjoys himself is not as good as a host who suffers'? Nevertheless, for now we remain upon the vast ocean;
who knows but that we may yet hook a Kun or a Jing?"
The *Haixin Xin* (Seal of the Ocean) verse says: "For now, I gather shrimp and clams by the lakeshore; I do not cast my line for the giant tortoise in the vast ocean.
With a single-leaf boat and a single straw raincoat, I sit idly with leisurely eyes, letting the winds and waves take their course.
An ancient worthy said: "Three coins bought me a virtuous wife; Gathering clams and shrimp upon the fishing boat. Old Xue does not yet know the ultimate life."
[The Master] calculated: "In appearance, this is not worth even half a coin.
When Chan Master Caoshan Benji took his leave of Dongshan, Dongshan asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am going to the place where there is no change or transformation.
Dongshan said, "In a place of no change or transformation, how can there be going? The Master replied, "Even going does not change."
Dana Chun’s verse says: "At every door, the moon of the toad is hidden; everywhere, the oriole sings in the willow wind.
If you claim there is no change or variation in this纵横 (zōnghéng, 'transverse and vertical' expanse), it is like brandishing a sword at empty space."
Chan Master Yunmen Wenyan was asked by a monk, "What is the student’s own self? The Master replied, "Wandering through mountains and enjoying the waters.
Fohui Quan composed a verse on this: Before Mount Nanyue and behind Mount Jing, The sound of the waterfall roars like thunder.
"Cast off the straw hat and walk with the head bare; tread through the grass shoes and run with feet uncovered. Dizang En said:
"Walking on moss beneath the *li* forest, the weary life of toil has not yet opened its eyes.
How wonderful it is that falling flowers follow the clear water, all flowing out together from within the cave. Kaifu Ning said: "The matter of wandering the mountains and playing by the waters."

Ordinary and commonplace. Returning morning and evening, one’s hair is nearly white with frost. Treading through worn-out straw sandals, one turns the head to gaze upon the land of white clouds where the monkeys cry out several times.
Master Wúwéi said: "When a student travels to mountains and plays by the waters, they know only to tread through worn-out straw sandals;
they forget their age when they first set out."
A monk asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still any fault? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru.
Wuzu Fayan said, "Sometimes when I question a monk, he may raise a finger, or take a step forward, or let out a shout, or brush his sleeves and depart.
Yet you, Venerable One, have not yet attained it. Why? Because in the Great Peace, I have never yet directed [my attention toward it]."
"In the second or third month, a final flurry of snow falls upon you all. Suppose there were a man who came forth and said, 'Old Monk, do not act so capriciously;
it is not right that you are doing this now. Then [the Master] would extend his hand and say, 'Finished.'"
Ying’an Hua said: "Yunmen’s statement is indeed correct, yet it ultimately falls into the secondary position.
If it were Minggao, it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask: 'If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression?
He would simply reply: 'Bring forth your question.'"
Dongshan Chong’s verse says: "If not a single thought arises, how can one penetrate the source? Truth and falsehood are distinguished within a single phrase.
When one strikes the eye of wisdom, even the mouth is stilled; Mount Sumeru stands face-to-face as a screen. Baoning Yong said:
Standing before the ten-thousand-fathom peak is a great violation; in the blink of an eye, one falls over the precipice.
He whose entire body is not harmed by even a single hair—how could Heaven or Earth dare to bury him? Master Wujin said: "A single thought, deep and silent, transcends existence and non-existence;
stretching across the void, he brings forth Mount Sumeru. Even if the jade hare and golden crow (sun and moon) were to rush forward, the palaces..."
While on a pilgrimage, the journey was cut short midway.

Gu had no reply. The Master said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a single horse does not have twin foals."
Later, a monk cited this to Shushan. Shushan said, "A stone ox blocks the ancient road; a single horse gives birth to three tigers. Gushan Gui’s verse says:
"Not treading the path before the gate, spring returns once more for another year. Falling flowers cover the ground in red;
fragrant grasses stretch green to the heavens. Jingshan Daokai says: "Stepping out the door, we shake hands and speak of parting. The ancients...

The road stretches far away; once gone, it cannot be pursued. One might as well laugh at the man who lost his sword in the waves, who needlessly marks the spot on the boat’s side to remember the moment he left it behind.
While Chan Master Baofu Zhan was strolling with Changqing through the mountains, the Master pointed toward the old monastery of Xuefeng and said:
"Teaching the wondrous peak of the Middle Way—do not think that this very place is it. Qingsong said, "It is indeed so, yet it is a pity.
Later, he mentioned this to Jingqing. Jingqing said, "If it were not for Master Sun, we would see skulls scattered across the wilds."
(With slight variations in one edition) A monk asked Gushan, "As for Master Leng speaking thus, what was his meaning?
Gushan said, "If Lord Sun had not uttered these words, it could be said that skulls would cover the wilds and bleached bones would stretch across the mountains. — Xuedou Xian.
He said, "Today, what is the point of wandering the mountains with this fellow? He added, "After hundreds or thousands of years, it will not be said that there is none at all;
it is simply that there will be less."
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: "Having ascended the high crag to its very summit, the monk has already completed his inquiry.
This is indeed most regrettable; I only fear that though the voices are the same, they wander in different places. Cudong Qing said:
Eighty-four thousand, not just one by one; within the Seven Golden Mountains, the seas flow on and on. The summit of Mount Sumeru is as level as the palm of a hand.
Who holds the long pole to fish for the giant turtle? Xuedou said: "On the solitary peak of the Wondrous Mountain, the grass grows lush and thick.
Picking it up clearly, to whom would you give it? Were it not for Master Sun’s ability to discern the essential point, skulls would be strewn upon the ground."
How many people know? Fuxinmu said: "Hand in hand we walk together, who else can go with us? Before our eyes we see only Mount Sumeru;
clouds and earth do not separate the path we came by. Entrust it to your descendants to look upon wherever they may be."
Ciming asked a monk, "One who travels on pilgrimage must know that there is a matter of pilgrimage. What is this matter of pilgrimage? The monk said, "I know it.
The Master said, "What is this matter that you know? The monk said, "The mountains are high and the waters are deep. The Master said, "I take pity on you for having come from so far away."
"Sit down and drink tea. The monk replied, "Yes, yes. The monk asked, "What is it like when one travels on foot and does not encounter anyone?
The Master said, "A fishing line twisting through the water.
Shitian Dong wrote a verse in praise: "The aged and decrepit Ciming points out the way for the lost; The fishing line twisting through the water brings forth all manner of wondrous functions."
At that time, people were so intent on gazing at the white reeds that they did not see the sandpipers flying across the shore.
(From the *Niansong Ji*, "Sound") When Chan Master Guoyi Qin received a letter sent by Mazu, the letter contained a circle drawn within it. The Master...
Upon opening the seal, he saw [the letter] and consequently placed a single dot within the circle before sealing it back and returning it.
Later, when National Teacher Zhong heard of this, he remarked, "Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma."
Baofu Zhan said, "Where is the place of delusion? How can one avoid being deluded?
Xuedou Xian said, "Setting aside the fact that Jingshan was deluded, if you were to present this to National Teacher Huizhong, what other skillful means would you employ to avoid being deluded?
An old master said, "At that time, he should have simply sat still and let it be. Others have also said:
He merely drew a line across it. If that is how you see it, you are simply shameless;
how dare you claim that the teachers of the world all possess the vajra-eye and can perform vast supernatural transformations? Could they have avoided this?
I want everyone to know where Xuedou stands: even when Master Ma drew that line at that time, he was already deluded himself.
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said, "Two colors, one match. He also said, "When three people point the way, what do you intend to do?
Daopei Zhe said, "Do you all recognize Mazu and Jingshan? A single drop of ink forms two dragons.
National Teacher Daoqin was still deluded by Master Mazu; this can truly be called "the same breeze from a thousand miles away. Not so.
"Seeing the Way, one holds the Night-Bright Talisman in hand; how many know the dawn? Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Master Mazu’s was the bitter cold of mid-winter;
Master Qin’s was the gradual heat of early summer. Although the cold and heat differ, both did not miss their proper seasons.
Why, then, did National Teacher Zhong say that Master Qin was still deluded by Master Mazu? Do you understand?"
Do you understand thoroughly? "The lotus leaf moves though there is no wind; it is certain that a fish is swimming beneath.
In Yuan’s verse on the Buddha-seal, he says: "When Mazu saw Jingshan at that time, a subtle, secret mechanism was slightly revealed through their shared style."
Without cause, he was instead deceived by the Old Man of Nanyang, who leveled a trap on flat ground as if in jest.
Zhaojue said in total: "The words of being deluded have their origins. A spiritual communion across a thousand li is like a mustard seed meeting a needle.
Who says that clouds can be made to convey messages? I do not agree; even stones nod their heads. Dizang En said: "From south to north, from self to self..."
From west to east, though the streams and mountains differ, the clouds and moon remain the same. Why does this old man of Nanyang cause people such restless agitation?
Master Nanquan Yuan wrote a letter to Zhuyou, saying: "Principle follows the transformation of phenomena; its vast expanse is not external. Phenomena...
The monk attained a profound understanding of the principle that "the silent void is not within. The monk then asked, "What is it that is vast and expansive, yet not without?

Nan-yü said, "To ask one and receive a hundred answers is no hindrance. The monk then asked, "What is it that is silent and void, yet not within? Nan-yü said, "To perceive through forms and sounds is not the work of a skilled hand. The monk then questioned Changsha.
Changsha stared at him with wide-open eyes for a long while, and when the monk further offered his subsequent question, [Changsha remained silent].
Sha-nian closed his eyes to indicate this to him. The monk then asked Zhaozhou another question; Zhaozhou made the gesture of eating a meal.

When the monk presented the subsequent question, Zhaozhou wiped his mouth with his hand. Later, the monk related these instances to the Master (Linji), who said, "These three men are not mistaken; they are truly my disciples."
Fojian Qin said: "Although Nanquan had the karmic conditions for raising a son, he was so fond of his child that he failed to notice his ugliness.
He did not realize that among these three people, one has feet but no eyes, one has eyes but no feet, and one has neither feet nor eyes.
Nevertheless, all three could serve as teachers to Nanquan. Why is this so?"

The facts and the principle are clear. Chengtian Jian said: "Of these three people, one has obtained the skin, one has obtained the flesh, and one is neither collected by Qin nor managed by Wei. Nantang Jing said: "What fine father and son are Nanquan and his heir!"
"Great Assembly! If it were the South Hall, it would not be so. What is 'principle changing according to phenomena'?
When washing brocade at the head of the Washed Brocade River, the peach blossoms are like brocade and the willows are like eyebrows. What is 'phenomena merging with principle'?
The Three Hundred and Sixty Thousand Acres of Lake Tai—when the moon is in the heart of the waves, to whom does it speak? What is 'vast and expansive, yet not...'"
[The Master] stepped outside. He then took up his staff and leaned it against his left side. [He asked: "What is it that is silent and secluded, yet not internal?
He then took up the staff again and leaned it against his right side, saying: "Do not touch it; if you touch it, you shall receive thirty blows."
An ancient worthy composed this verse: "Serene and resonant is the zither upon my knees; How profound is the ancient spirit it conceals!
In the frosty sky, the moon shines as the west wind blows swift; The sound of autumn waters echoes from the fallen banks and broken cliffs."
Chan Master Xuansha Shibei instructed a monk to deliver a letter to Xuefeng. Upon opening the seal, Xuefeng saw three sheets of blank white paper.
He presented them to the assembly and asked, "Do you understand? After a long silence, he said, "Has it not been said that 'the gentleman shares the same breeze from a thousand miles away'?
When the monk returned and reported this to Master [Xuansha], the Master said, "That old fellow at the mountain head has missed the mark, and he does not even realize it."
Dongshan Shouzhi said: "Where did you go wrong? If you have indeed gone wrong, how could the Master not understand the disciple's meaning?
If you do not understand it in this way, then what is the meaning of Xuansha’s intent? If you understand, then investigate Xuansha for yourself.
Wuzu Fayan stepped forward and said: "I thought his beard was red. Huanglong Nan said:
Xuefeng did not say he had no points of excellence; yet, having been exposed by Xuansha, he has remained "snowless" (unable to manifest his realization) until this very day.
Haoyin Xin said, "When one's wisdom is equal to the teacher’s, one loses half the teacher’s virtue; only when one's wisdom surpasses the teacher’s is one fit for transmission.
However, there is still one move lacking. Kaishan Xian said, "Xuansha’s white paper—how can it compete?"

Now that the patterns and colors have already become manifest, since Xuefeng said, "A thousand miles share the same wind," why did he not realize it and thus miss the mark? Have you not heard it said:
"When raising a child, do not let him grow too large"? Once he has grown large, he becomes a master thief.
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: "He sent a messenger with a letter to convey his far-reaching message; He did not rely on written words to reveal his family style.
Upon returning, he reported Xuefeng’s words; Having missed the mark, he clearly sealed the principle once more. Foxing Tai said:
Three sheets of white paper were sent as a communication. Unfolding them across a thousand *li*, they share the same wind. The "Spring Radiance" has turned into a *huqia* flute melody;
it is not a different tune blown by the wind. Fuxincai said: "He capsizes the fishing boat to inherit the family legacy;
laughing out from amidst the reeds, the moon is perfectly full. Earth vast and heaven long—these three sheets of paper share the same wind across a thousand *li*."
Li asked, "For whom do you proclaim this? Cishou Shenyan said: "Xuansha’s elephant-bone eyes are black; three sheets of white paper should suffice for the writing.
Those who share the same breeze from a thousand miles away mostly misunderstand; two people together must support a single staff."

Regarding the story of Master Huijue (Hua Bao) of Baoshou Temple: Once, when he was still at Baoshou, he was asked, "Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face. The Master stood there until deep into the night, yet his responses did not accord with the truth. The following day, he took his leave. Baoshou said, "Why have you left? [The Master replied: "I have no other teacher. Baoshou said, "If that is so, why do you not stay? The Master replied, "Because my teacher is already here. Baoshou then asked, "Who is your teacher? The Master replied, "It is you, Master. Baoshou said, "How can this be? The Master said, "If it were anyone else, I would indeed have left. Baoshou then said, "Bring me your original face before your parents were born. The Master immediately bowed. Baoshou said, "This is the face after birth; where is the one before birth? The Master again bowed. Baoshou said, "Both of these are faces after birth; where is the one before birth? The Master remained silent. Baoshou said, "You have finally brought me your original face. The Master then composed a verse: "Before my parents were born, I was already here; / After my parents were born, I am still here. / Before and after, there is no difference; / It is simply the bright moon shining on the water. Baoshou said, "You have truly brought me your original face. This is recorded in the *Biyan Lu* (Blue Cliff Record), Case 19. It is also cited in the *Wumen Guan* (Gateless Barrier), Case 26.
