He departed. The Master said, "Yesterday I asked you a question, but you did not accord with it. I am going south to visit spiritual teachers.
Shoushan said, "In the south they prohibit the summer retreat but not the winter; here we prohibit the winter but not the summer.

For now, go about the streets as a wandering monk and pass the summer retreat there. As for the Buddha-dharma, it is constantly being preached even amidst the bustling crowds and the vast dust of the marketplace."
The Master did not dare disobey the Dharma. One day, seeing two people quarreling on the street, he struck out a single punch and said, "How can you be so shameless?
At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment. He hurried to see Master Baoshou, but before he could speak, Baoshou said, "You have understood; there is no need to say anything."
Wuzu Yan said: "If a person knows the point of landing here, one may say they are conducting public business or private business.
Great assembly, listen to this verse; it is most wondrous, truly most wondrous. To know one's very life and nature here—strike the nose and give a punch!"
At that moment, he struck him and stopped. Nanhua Bing said: "A single punch delivers one who is without face;
the blue-eyed barbarian monk cannot gaze upon him enough. In autumn, yellow leaves fall in profusion; six times six turns into thirty-six."
Withered trees form clouds; north, south, east, and west, he wanders everywhere. Deeper still, he returns home as the moon is like a hook.
A gust of spring wind scatters the flowers in disarray; unconsciously reflecting, he nods his head in the dark. — Fuxing Tai said.
With one punch, he topples the Yellow Crane Tower; with one kick, he overturns the Parrot Isle.

Fortunately, there is a bystander who exerts effort for him, while he himself sits upright watching Yangzhou. Dreaman Xin said: "Two spiritual friends meeting in a bustling marketplace—no coming, no going, their faces are too much trouble to scrutinize.
Even grinding one's bones to powder would not suffice as recompense. One phrase brings it all to an end."
However, he transcended [the ordinary] by billions of times.

He was the manifested incarnation of Pùdàng Héshàng in Míngzhōu; his family name and origins are unknown. His physical form was stout and fleshy, and he frequented the main thoroughfares and bustling markets.
Someone asked, "What are you doing here? He replied, "I am waiting for that person to come. When the man said, "The person has arrived," he replied, "You are not that person.
Sometimes he untied his cloth bag, revealing all manner of objects within. Sometimes he would pick something up and show it to someone, saying, "This is from the Inner Court of Tuṣita.
Or he would reach into the bag and offer a fruit to a monk; as the monk reached out to take it, the Master would suddenly withdraw his hand.
Shou said, "You are not this person. Or, seeing a monk pass by, he would strike him once on the back;
when the monk turned his head, he would say, "Give me one coin. At other times, he would lean against a cloth bag and sleep soundly all day long.
Sometimes he would go among the market stalls, where children would clamor and chase after him; he would then play with them, giving them either a staff or a rosary. There was once a monk...
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? He then dropped his cloth bag, stood with his hands folded, and the monk said, "Is there anything else besides this?
Thereupon, he picked up the cloth bag, slung it over his shoulder, and departed. (In some versions, the text differs.
Baoning Yong composed a verse on this: "Hah! This foolish leather bag, With coarse brows and a large girth, Spends all day in the street."
Head. Walking through the marketplace, there is no buying or selling. A-he-he! Return! Give back the money you borrowed.
Fohuiquan said: "Pick it up and you walk; let it go and you rest. This drowsy monk makes a fool of himself by trying to be clever."
Who can know the intent of the Buddhas and the intent of the Patriarchs? A skirt and a narrow shirt, patched in a hundred ways; sometimes standing alone, who is the one who understands?
Return! A single sky of bright moon. Yuantong Xiu said: "In a thousand ways and ten thousand forms, who can truly comprehend them?
This old monk, dozing off, gathers his things into a full bag. When the mind is free from all sensations, every place is samādhi."
At the ends of alleys and on the streets, they buy high and sell low.
When Master Puhua heard that there was a vegetarian feast at Linji Monastery, he went to the Wooden Pagoda in Heyang and sat with Linji inside the monks' hall.
As soon as the topic of the Master’s daily antics—running wild and acting crazily in the marketplaces—was mentioned, [Puhua] asked, "I do not know whether he is a sage or a commoner."
Shengji said, "Wait for him to come, and then I will ask about this transgression. After a short while, the Master entered. Ji immediately asked, "Is Puhua an ordinary man or a sage?
The Master replied, "Tell me, are you an ordinary man or a sage? Ji then gave a shout. The Master then pointed to the two venerable elders and said, "The bride of He-yang;
the grandmotherly Zen of the wooden pagoda; and Linji, that little fellow—he alone possesses the single [eye]."
Yan said, "This thief! The Master called out, "Thief! Thief! and then ran out.
Haiyin Xin composed a verse on this: "The distinction between a thoroughbred and a common horse is rarely discerned; their depth and color of coat are the same."
If it were not for Bo Le, who bestowed his refined discernment, a horse that chases the wind across a thousand li would not be easy to ride.
When a monk asked Chan Master Cōng of Dòngshān, "Since you are the Great Sage of Sīzhōu, why do you appear in Yángzhōu?
the Master said, "A gentleman loves wealth, but he takes it by the right means."
Cimengyuan’s verse says: "Sizhou suddenly manifested in Yangzhou; The ancestral teachers of the world abound in their teaching paths.
A gentleman loves wealth but takes it only through the right way; The Persian from the South Sea has a coarse nostril."

The World-Honored One of Divine Marvels was questioned by a seer possessing the five supernormal powers (pañcābhijñā). "The World-Honored One possesses six supernormal powers; I possess five. What is that one [remaining] power?
The Buddha called out, "O seer with five supernormal powers! The seer with five supernormal powers responded, "Yes. The Buddha said, "That one power—do you have it?"
When asked about me, Xuedou Xian said, "The Old Barbarian originally did not know that there was even one such attainment; instead, he struck the orthodox because of the heterodox.
Langya Jue said, "The World-Honored One did not know; this can be called striking the heterodox because of the orthodox. The five supernatural powers are due to the heterodox."
[The Master] struck him squarely. Cuiyan Zhi said, "The Five Supernatural Powers asked thus, and the World-Honored One answered thus;
yet, fundamentally, they did not understand even one of those powers. Yunfeng Yue said, "Great Gautama has been thoroughly exposed by the outsider.
Is there anyone here who cannot bear this? Come forward! I want to ask you: what is that?"
One Penetration. Yun’gai’s original text says: “The World-Honored One summoned thus; the Five Penetrations responded thus.
What is this ‘One Penetration’? After a long silence, he said: “The young maiden has already returned to the celestial void;
the foolish lad still crouches by the fire.”
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "Throughout immeasurable kalpas, never before encountered; How can one reach its midst without moving?
Do not say that the Buddha-dharma has little substance; Most grievous is that Gautama lacks even a single penetration. Yunxi Gong says:
Question: How is it that the Buddha attained that one penetration? The World-Honored One pointed directly at the face to reveal the traces of delusion. Dense auspicious clouds bring a light drizzle;
The great thundering sound of the Dharma-voice is like a wind sweeping across the earth. Changling Zhuo said: "You ask how—this question is direct.
The plum on the ridge and the willows by the river share the fragrance of spring. One who carries stolen goods need not undergo a search; He has already been caught in the act."
"The hall reveals the thief’s body. Zhengjue Yi said: "That one penetration—ask me! It makes Śākyamuni the Old Man feel ashamed;
he only knows how to step on red lotuses at every turn, yet he fails to realize that he has wandered blindly into the wild weeds.
Foyin Yuan said: "The Immortal’s single question is fully prepared, yet Gautama possesses not a single thing. He calls it..."
The rabbit comes and is released as before; how many mountain ghosts call out to one another in the dark?
Once, when the World-Honored One was with Jīvaka, who was skilled at distinguishing sounds, they came upon a cemetery where he saw three skulls.
He then struck one skull and asked Jīvaka, "Where was this person born? Jīvaka replied, "This person was born into the human realm. He struck another and asked again:
"Where was this life spent? The old woman replied, "This life was spent in the heavenly realm. The World-Honored One struck again with another question: "Where was this life spent?
The old woman was ignorant of where she had been born.
The *Tuduce* (Poison-Smeared Whip) Verse says: "The Tathāgata’s single blow few recognize; Directly beneath, who is it that is clearly manifest?
Boundless moonlight follows the water away; A single fragment of cloud turns back toward its old mountain."
Before Aṅgulimāla had left the household life, he was a follower of external paths who received instruction from Kośika.
Kośika desired to ascend the throne as king and used the thumbs of a thousand people to fashion a flower crown; he had obtained nine hundred and ninety-nine, lacking only one finger.
He then intended to kill his mother to take her finger. At that time, the Buddha was on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa and observed this with his divine eye.
He then manifested as a śramaṇa standing before Aṅgulimāla. Aṅgulimāla then released his mother, intending instead to kill the Buddha. The Buddha walked slowly, while Aṅgulimāla hurried along.
When he could not catch up, he called out, "Gautama! Stop, stop! The Buddha said, "I have long since stopped; it is you who do not stop.

Upon hearing this, Aṅgulimāla’s mind was suddenly awakened. He then cast away his blade, went forth as a monk under the Buddha, and the Buddha immediately conferred upon him the tonsure and the robes.
The verse by Fodeng Xun says: "Whether walking fast or slow, there is no before or after; One simply treads the single path of Chang’an.

When Aṅgulimāla suddenly knows his dwelling place, He can walk with steady steps upon the clouds and mists. A flower crown requires no fingers born of a mother; Beard and hair need not trouble one to shake them with effort.
It is most wonderful that when moving flowers, butterflies arrive along with them; In the midst of such leisure, one purchases..."
The stone gains abundance from the clouds; Shushan is like the clouds themselves. When Aṅgulimāla was fierce and bold, his valor was sharp and keen;

when Gautama remained still, he stilled the wind and waves. Killing a man to become a Buddha—this is a piercing point right before one’s eyes; overturning rain and turning clouds occurs in a single kṣaṇa.
Aṅgulimāla, while entering the city with his alms bowl, arrived at the house of a certain elder. He encountered the elder’s wife in the throes of a difficult childbirth.
The elder said to him, "Śramaṇa, you are a disciple of the Buddha. What skillful means do you have to save my wife from this childbirth crisis?
Aṅgulimāla replied, "I have only recently entered the Path and am not yet familiar with this matter. I shall go to ask the Buddha and return to inform you. Thereupon, he hurried away.
He returned and reported these matters to the Buddha in full detail. The Buddha told him, "Go quickly and tell them:

'Since I followed the Dharma of the Worthy and Holy Ones, I have never killed a living being. When Aṅgulimāla delivered the Buddha’s words to the elder, the elder’s wife heard them and was immediately delivered from her distress;
both mother and son were safe and well.
Juehai’s *Yuan Song* says: "The Sage Dharma has never, from the beginning, killed living beings; Fundamentally there is no killing or being born, only pervasive clarity and brilliance.
All these persons and selves are empty marks; All enemies and kin are merely provisional names. When the nectar-dew first moistens them, the feverish afflictions are removed;
The jade lotus and golden child both flourish together. Gushan Gui says: "The Lady of Chang’e within the moon..."
Painting her brows, she uses only clouds and mist for her gauze robe. Unaware that her dream has followed the azure phoenix away, she still returns with flower branches covering her face.
Jingshan Gaofeng said: "Before the Huayin Mountains lies a hundred-foot well; within it, cold spring water pierces the bones.
Whose daughter comes to reflect her image? She does not look at anything else, but gazes at the side of her neck."

The Prince Nanda dismembered his own flesh and returned it to his mother; he dismembered his own bones and returned them to his father. Thereupon, manifesting his true form and exercising great supernormal powers, he preached the Dharma for his parents.
Foyuan said: "Since the flesh has returned to the mother and the bones have returned to the father, what constitutes the body?
A student of the Way, if you can see through this point, will sweep away the five aggregates and swallow up the ten directions.
He then spoke a verse: Bones return to the father; Flesh returns to the mother. What, then, is the body? Listen clearly: The mountains, rivers, and the lands.
The entire body manifests; the worlds of the ten directions are contained within it. Through ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes, coming and going are severed.
This teaching of the mountain monk is not mere words. Jingshan Gaofeng said: "When flesh and bone have all been returned to one's parents, who knows which is the Nārāyaṇa?
With a single turn of the body upon the tip of a hair, every single hair-tip is perfectly unerring."

Chan Master Po-zao-duo once visited a temple on Mount Song that was renowned for its spiritual efficacy. Within the hall stood only a single hearth, to which offerings were made incessantly from near and far.
The Master struck the hearth three times with his staff and said, "Tsk! This hearth is merely composed of clay and tiles.
From where does the 'saint' come? From where does the 'spirit' arise? Yet you thus slaughter living beings! He then struck it thirty more times.
The hearth then tilted, broke apart, and fell down. In a moment, a person in green robes and a tall black cap appeared and bowed, saying: "I was originally the stove deity of this temple.
Having long endured the retribution of my karma, I have now been granted the Dharma of non-arising by the Zen Master; I have escaped this place and shall be reborn in heaven."
He came specifically to offer his thanks. The Master said, "This is your own inherent nature; it is not something I have spoken of by force. The spirit bowed twice and vanished.
Later, a monk asked the Master, "I have long served at your side, yet I have not received any instruction.
What principle did the stove god realize that he was reborn in heaven? The Master said, "I simply told him that it is composed of clay and tiles; there is nothing else."
The monk was at a loss. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master asked, "Why do you not understand your own inherently present nature? The monk bowed. The Master said, "He has fallen! He has fallen! He is shattered! He is shattered!
Later, another monk related this to National Teacher An. The National Teacher sighed and said, "This man has realized that all things and the self are of one suchness."
It was said that he was like the bright moon in the sky, such that there was no one who did not see it; yet the lineage of his words was difficult to grasp.
The monk bowed his head, joined his palms, and asked, "I do not understand: what kind of person can grasp the lineage of his words? An said, "One who does not know."

Foyan Yuan’s verse says: "Calamity and fortune, majesty and sternness do not manifest their own numinous power; A leftover cup and cold meat—whom do they serve? Since he departed long ago, there has been no news;
Yet the village elder still beats the sacrificial drum. It also says: "The spring chill is biting and piercing; it freezes the young to death.
Be careful not to let them be like the stars Shen and Shang (at odds). There is nothing else marvelous: Serve with bowed head, and you will find joy."
Inquiry: "Discussing the Buddha-dharma has cost you your life. Fodeng Xun said: "Relying on the hearth, the so-called 'spirit' is no spirit at all;
Spirit arises from the place of severance as a heap of dust. The wild elder does not come to beat the sacrificial drum;
By striking the orthodox, the heterodox is transformed—this is another spring."
One day, Chan Master Yangshan Ji suddenly saw a strange monk arrive through the air. The monk paid his respects and stood before him.
The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "I left Western Heaven this morning. The Master said, "Why so late?

The monk said, "I was traveling among the mountains and enjoying the waters. The Master said, "While your supernatural powers and wondrous functions are indeed beyond reproach, as for the Buddha-dharma, it must be returned to the old man."
The monk said, "I have come specifically to the Eastern Land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I have instead encountered a minor Śākyamuni.
He then took out a *bīḍa* leaf from Western India and gave it to the Master; having prostrated, he ascended into the sky on a cloud and departed.
Donglin Zong said: "The deliberations of various quarters are as numerous as hemp and millet;

**The Lute, Go (Calligraphy, Painting, and Music appended)** Chan Master Zong of Muzhou was visited by a scholar who came to seek instruction. The Master asked, "What arts do you, a man of learning, possess? The scholar replied, "I am proficient in the twenty-four styles of calligraphy. The Master pointed a single dot in the air with his staff and said, "Understood? The scholar was speechless. The Master then struck him once with the staff and drove him out. **Commentary:** The Master’s pointing of the dot in the air was intended to test whether the scholar could perceive the ultimate principle beyond the conventional forms of the twenty-four calligraphic styles. When the scholar failed to respond, the Master struck him to reveal that the Way transcends all such worldly skills. This episode illustrates how Chan masters employ the mundane arts as skillful means to probe the depth of a student's realization. As for the appended categories of painting and music, they function similarly; the ancients used these sensory expressions to trigger awakening, yet they too must be transcended to realize the true source. Thus, while the ancients utilized the lute, the board game, and other arts to guide others, one must ultimately let go of them to see the fundamental nature. This is why it is said: "If you wish to know the Buddha, look at the common person. Only when one has thoroughly investigated and exhausted the various arts can one truly understand the meaning of "the twenty-four styles of calligraphy. If one does not investigate to the end, one will merely remain stuck in the realm of the ordinary. Therefore, the ancients did not merely teach people to practice the arts; they used them to point directly to the mind-ground. Those who study the Way today should take this as a model. If one does not investigate to the very bottom, one will never attain liberation. This is why the ancients were so diligent—they did not allow themselves to be deceived by appearances. If you can investigate to the point where there is no longer even a single hair's breadth of doubt, you will naturally understand the meaning of this story. Otherwise, you will merely be adding another layer of delusion. This is why the ancients said, "If you do not meet a true teacher, you will surely fall into the pit of views. You must be careful not to mistake the finger for the moon. If you can see through this story, you will have attained some small measure of understanding. If you cannot, you must continue to investigate until you reach the bottom. Do not be like those who merely recite the words without realizing their intent. If you can penetrate this matter, you will know that the twenty-four styles of calligraphy are nothing more than empty names. [This was] given to Sanbo. Muan Yong said: "The master sees the servant's earnestness. Gushan Gui’s verse says:

"When we meet and speak, the principle is not lacking; yet in an ordinary turn of the head, he strikes us away."
Once the divergent waters must flow toward the sea; when their journey ends, the clouds will surely seek the mountains to return.
One day, Chan Master Zheng of Baizhang said to the assembly, "When you have finished clearing the fields for me, I shall explain the Great Meaning to you.
When the monks had finished clearing the fields, they said, "We request the Master to explain the Great Meaning. The Master then opened both hands.

Baizhang said, "The Great Meaning has been fully explained here. Where has the sentence regarding the second visit to Mazu gone? If one says there is more to it, one cannot avoid painting legs on a snake. Furthermore— (Some erroneously refer to this as "Sea Chan Master.

Baizhang Wendeng said: "Baizhang’s exposition of the Great Meaning ends right here. As for the phrase concerning his second visit to Mazu at that time—where has it gone? If you say there is something further, you cannot avoid drawing legs on a snake. And so forth.
"How can one know where the old man Baizhang stands? he asked. He then said: "When guests arrive, there is no tea;

mugwort soup serves as the ritual offering. Daowei Zhe said: "Baizhang expounded a great meaning that can truly be called rarely heard in ancient or modern times, illuminating what came before and surpassing what comes after.
Daowei, however, would not have it so; he simply says: 'The labor of clearing the fields—please [accept this]. "
Return to the hall to rest. This will cause the monks of the world to be rendered tongue-tied by its sharp edge.
Why? A crane may have nine hollows on its neck, yet it cannot spread its wings; a horse may lack the thousand-li stride, yet it vainly pursues the wind. Ying’an Hua said:
"Baizhang wishing to see the principle of Mazu’s 'second visit'—this is truly laughable. One must laugh for thirty years. Furthermore:
How can one know where Baizhang stood? He too laughed for thirty years.
When guests arrived and there was no tea, he prepared the ritual with mugwort decoction; he too laughed for thirty years. Three laughs thus make ninety years.
Is this laughter because you have not yet mastered Baiyun’s critique, or is there some other principle? You all—
If you can examine this and grasp it, I shall hand over my staff to you with both hands.
But if you have not yet reached this state, how many times have you returned home drunk on moonlit nights, led by the sound of pipes and songs into the painted hall?
Baizhang Yuanwen’s verse says: "I have always admired Baizhang for opening up the field; It has been transmitted through the hands of practitioners, past and present.
Who would say his tongue never moved? The five notes and six scales revolve in perfect harmony. Foyan Wenyuan said:
Daitian expounded the Great Meaning; later generations must not treat it with ease. Baizhang’s gate of total retention is plain yet possesses flavor.
A monk of Changsha asked, "How can one transform the mountains, rivers, and the great earth into oneself? The Master said, "How?"
He transformed himself into the mountains, rivers, and the great earth. A monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "In the cities of Hunan, the people are well-nourished;
rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful, sufficient for all four neighbors."
Tiantong Jue said: "Although host and guest alternate, the mud and water remain undifferentiated.
Even if one were to twist the nostrils, neither 'it is so' nor 'it is not so' will suffice. Furthermore, how should it be? Now the royal decree is strict;
no one is permitted to interfere with the market or seize another's stall. Jingshan Guangzhao said: "The mountains and rivers are turned over."
It is easy to bring the earth back to oneself; it is difficult to turn oneself back into the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
If someone can utter a phrase that is neither difficult nor easy, they may come before Jingshan’s hands to beg for a blow of the staff.
Ying’an Hua said: "Jiangshan has rendered a judgment according to his capacity; yet even the great Changsha could not break through this monk."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: In every dust mote and land, this ordinary body is revealed; When doubt arises and emotion stirs, one sees the distinction between the distant and the near.
What has always been the case within the city of Hunan: Rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful, enough for all four neighbors.
When Chan Master Yangshan Ji was asked by Guishan, "Where have you come from? the Master replied, "From the fields. Guishan asked, "How many people are there in the fields?
Yangshan thrust his spade into the ground and stood with his hands folded behind his back. Guishan said, "Today on South Mountain there are many people mowing thatch.
Yangshan pulled his spade and walked away.
Xuansha said, "If I had seen it, I would have kicked the spade over. Jingqing was once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of planting the spade?
Jingqing said, "A dog carrying an imperial pardon; the feudal lords clear their paths for him. He was asked again, "What is the meaning of Xuansha kicking the spade over?
Jingqing said, "When the boat cannot be saved, one breaks the scoop. He was asked yet again, "What about Nan... [The text here is truncated].
When asked, "How about cutting grass on the mountain? Qing said, "Third Elder Li Jing has long experienced the ranks of battle.
Xuedou Xian said, "The venerable masters of all quarters all claim that the 'scoop-in-the-ditch' story is extraordinary; this is much like following the heterodox and pursuing the evil."
According to Xuedou’s perspective, when Yangshan was questioned by Guishan, he was so thoroughly bound by his own "grass ropes" that he was on the verge of death.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Yangshan only obtained a single peg; you all must have another way of understanding.
Wushan Gao said, "To act secretly and apply [the teaching] subtly is the mark of a true master of one's own station; whether releasing or..."

To gather [the essence], one must be a person of thorough penetration who illuminates themselves. But tell me, what matter does this illumination concern? Only after drinking dry the waters of the West River can one clarify that single point of mind.
Touzi Qing’s verse says: “In Miaoxin’s place of questioning, few find a true知音 (zhinyin); he thrusts it into the ground as his response, while Buddhas and Patriarchs sink away.”
Treading down Xuansha’s “Beside, he will not consent,” one avoids letting the lush greenery bear the weight of deep spring.
Baoning Yong said: "Shallow sowing and deep plowing are exactly in season; entering the mud and entering the water—who else can share this?
On the southern mountain, many people harvest the thatch grass; it is known only by father and son alone. Foxin Cai said: "The golden whip strikes, shaking the azure..."
The Dragon’s Cave: Spewing mist that supports the void as it emerges from the ocean gates; Sucking the vast seas dry, it ascends into the heavens.
Now only thunder and lightning remain, filling the mountains and rivers. Foyan Yuan said: "The numbers are distinct, yet difficult to bring forth;
No patch-robed monk fails to have his hair stand on end. You must know there is still a path within the alchemical flask; Simply look beyond the summit of Mount Sumeru."
Tiantong Jue said: "I, the old Jue, am full of worldly sentiment and think only of my descendants; now I feel shame before the lineage of our house.
You must remember the words of Nanshan: 'Carve them into your bones and engrave them upon your flesh, together repaying this kindness.'"
At the end of the summer retreat, Yangshan went to inquire after Muzhou (Weishan). Muzhou said, "I have not seen you for an entire summer.
What were you doing down there? The Master replied, "Down there, I cleared a patch of fallow land with a hoe and sowed a measure of millet.
Muzhou said, "This summer you have not spent in vain. The Master then asked, "What did the Master accomplish this summer?"
Mo. Baizhang said, "Eating once at midday and sleeping once after nightfall. Baizhang said, "Master, you have not spent this summer in vain either.
Having said this, he stuck out his tongue. Baizhang said, "Ji, why do you thus endanger your own life?"
Daguang Zhe said: "Yangshan’s eye illuminates the four quarters of the world, yet when he arrives before Dayuan, he stumbles upon the pure ground.
Dayuan may indeed be called one who provides for his child, yet he cannot avoid becoming a subject for the lips and teeth of future generations."
Foyuan said: "O Great Assembly! The ordinary encounters between Master and Son at Mount Gui were a playful exercise of spiritual powers, no small matter.
Is there anyone who understands this? If not, let the mountain monk explain it for you all."
Open up a field; dense and continuous. With two meals of gruel, the Way reveals itself.

This summer, this mountain monk has been in audience with you all, yet it is simply that you have not realized it. If you were to realize it, it would become a single expanse—look at the arrow at the gate!
Tiantong Jue said: "When young, one should exert effort; when old, one ought to let the mind rest. This—
Summer never passes in vain. Why did Yangshan stick out his tongue after speaking? If you can examine this thoroughly, then calamity shall not enter the door of a prudent household.
Dongshan Cōng’s verse says: “How could Yangshan have been so overly earnest? He stuck out his tongue in bewilderment, yet again leaked the secret.
It was best that Guishan’s words rebuked him; Thus he came to feel shame and recognize his error. Fodeng Xun said:
One mu of field yields three shi of grain; at the time of the fast, there is rice and morning congee. For one lifetime, father and son discuss the family tradition;
fame and achievement shall be passed down through the *Lamp Records* for ten thousand ages. You followers of the Chan school, observe closely! Do not say these words are coarse and vulgar;
they are like the white stones on Mount Jing—there will surely come a Bian He who knows them to be jade.
When Chan Master Linji Xuan was attending a communal labor session at the tea garden, Huangbo arrived late.
After the Master had finished his greetings, he stood with his hoe planted in the ground. Huangbo said, "Are you exhausted? The Master replied, "I have only just begun to dig;

why do you speak of exhaustion? Huangbo took up his staff and struck him. The Master seized the staff and threw him down. Huangbo then called for the *vina* (chant leader), saying, "Pull me up! The *vina*...
Nanyue pulled him up by the hair, saying, "How can you, Reverend, tolerate such a madman? Ba then gave Weinan a slap.
The Master then struck the ground with his hoe and said, "In other places they burn the dead; here, we bury them alive."
Guishan asked Yangshan, "At that time, what was the meaning behind Huangbo and Linji? Yangshan said, "The thief has run away;
the pursuer takes the beating. Guishan said, "So it is, so it is. Daming Zhe said, "Huangbo falls to the ground;
the rector helps him up. Cremation and burial alive—this pure wind has not yet ceased."
Zhenguanwen’s verse says: "Seizing the banner and pulling the drum requires spirit; though father and son are close, the Dharma is not close.
To report this to the Chan guests from the four quarters: do not casually act like one who waits by a stump. Fojian Qin said:
Among a hundred horses, there is one mule; though it kicks and stamps about in every direction, there is nothing that can be done.
Today, Linji’s wind-crazed madness is such that he instead ordered Huangbo to beat the rector.

Chan Master Xuansha Bei said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a single plot of land whose boundaries on all four sides have already been demarcated and sold to others by means of a formal contract.
Only the tree in the center still belongs to me, the old monk."
Gushan Gui’s verse says: "Ten thousand matters depend on the Old Teacher; the tree seedling does not yet belong to you. The broad-faced butcher becomes a Buddha;
the Great Master, the Second Patriarch, pays his debts. Jingshan Hongzhi says: "The ancestral fields and gardens have all been sold;
the boundaries on all four sides have not been left behind. Alas, there is still that central tree, causing such disturbance!"
The spring breeze has not yet ceased.
One day, while Zen Master Dizang Chen was planting rice in the fields, he saw a newly arrived monk and asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From the South. The Master asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma in the South? The monk said, "It is all in a state of bustling debate. The Master...
The Master said, "How can this compare to my way here: planting fields and earning my own food to eat? The monk asked, "What about the three realms?
The Master said, "What do you call 'the three realms'? The monk was speechless.
Daguizhe said: "In purity there is constant joy; in turbidity there is much sorrow. Yunfeng Yue’s verse says:
"To till the fields and earn one's meal—who can discern the truth within these words? After noon, the meal bell tolls;
even true gold has never lost its luster. Lingyuan Qing said: "To till the fields and earn one's meal—this is the essential point of the Buddha-dharma."
Deliberation: To transcend the three realms in a single word, the numinous faculty emits wondrous light. Yunyan therefore said: "There is a reason for tilling the fields to earn one's meal;
it is to avoid the trivial toil of seeking outward. Do not say that because the mind is weary, the body must also be weary."
For the most part, one must fully embrace both skill and clumsiness. The Ancient Buddha Min said: "Planting fields to earn a meal awaits those yet to come;
let them speculate as they please on this profound mystery. Upon the shadowless tree hang the sun and moon—how many people here have their minds extinguished?"
Chan Master Cheshi of Shimen was asked by a monk, "How does one advance on the ground of ultimate reality? The Master said, "The bird-path has no front.
The monk followed up with a verse: "In the deep valley, white clouds conceal the white sparrow; when the mind intends to settle there, the mountain stands between and all is lost."
Shimen Cong’s alternative verse says: "The mind of dwelling does not dwell upon the ground of dwelling; Beyond all things, moving freely, one rests in the leisure of the Dharma.
Xichan Xu’s eulogy says: "In the secluded valley, white clouds hide the white pheasant; Where the mind intends to settle, the mountains block the way."
"Even if you do not dwell in the place where the mind rests, you still fall into the second level of Yishan’s teaching.
(Grass and trees [bamboo included]).
National Teacher Nanyang Zhong asked the Imperial Attendant Zilin, "Where have you come from? The Attendant replied, "I have come from south of the city. The Master said:
"What color is the grass south of the city? He replied, "It is yellow. The Master then asked the boy, "What color is the grass south of the city?
The boy said, "It is yellow. The Master said, "This very boy could have been granted the purple robe before the imperial curtain and discourse on the profound mystery in the presence of the Emperor."
Daguang Zhe said: "The National Teacher asked in such a manner; the Attendant and the Boy answered in such a manner.
Tell me, was there any point of advantage or disadvantage here? If you can discern it, I grant that you have personally seen the National Teacher; if you have not yet realized it,"
The weeds south of the city wall remain their former yellow color.
In the "Eulogy on Chang" by Yuet Tang, it says: "Familiar with the ferryboat at the headland, I have now lost count of the years.
Enduring the violence of wind and waves, Only then am I pursuing coarse coin."
One day, Zen Master Yaoshan Yan was walking in the mountains with Daowu, Yunyan, and the novice Gao.
They saw two trees, one flourishing and one withered. The Master asked, "Which is the flourishing one? Which is the withered one? Daowu said, "The withered one. The Master said, "That is so;
it causes all things everywhere to become withered and bland. The Master then asked Yunyan, and Yunyan said, "The flourishing one."
"Yes," the Master said. "Ensure that it is radiant and brilliant in every respect. He then asked the śrāmaṇera, who replied, "Let the withered wither for its own sake;
let the flourishing flourish for its own sake. The Master turned back to Daowu and Yunyan and said, "Not so, not so."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "Dreaming within a dream, layer upon layer.
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "Powdered on the clay mold and wrapped in cloth once more; it all depends on the pull of the master weaver's thread."
The drums and war-drums have been beaten, the melodies have been played to their conclusion; gather up all and return home to rest. Fohuiquan said:
"One branch flourishes, one branch withers; in the center, green leaves grow even more lush.
Let the yellow oriole utter its myriad songs as it pleases, so that there is no need for bystanders to shoot at it. Haiyin Xin said: "Yellow leaves falling from the clouds turn to gold."
Money. When a foolish, crying child sees it, he is delighted; having caught it, he offers it to his mother, and everyone says how good it is.
None know who is laughing at the onlookers. Yunyan then said: "Old in years and solitary at heart, I laugh at Yaoshan. The sons sit together in a circle, forgetting even to return.
Only when asked from the beginning about matters of prosperity and decline do we find that their nostrils have always been of one kind. Chu.
Anfang said: "Few people can support Yaoshan’s way of acting. It is laughable that Yunyan and Dagui still produce intellectual interpretations based on flourishing and decay;
how could they know that Panlang rides his donkey backward?"

Master Daomian of Daguang addressed the assembly, saying: "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning are like a vine leaning against a tree. When Shushan heard this, he went directly to him to inquire about it.
He encountered the Master while he was plastering a wall; Shushan immediately asked, "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning are like a vine leaning against a tree."
"Is this not what the Master said? The Master replied, "Yes. Shushan said, "What if one suddenly encounters the time when the tree falls and the vines wither?
The Master set down his mud-platter, laughed heartily, and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Shushan followed after him and said, "I sold my cotton robe and traveled three thousand *li* specifically for this occasion. Why does the Master deceive me? The Master—
He said, "Attendant, go and get some money and return it to him. He then instructed him, saying, "In the future, there will be 'One-Eyed Dragon' who will pierce through your delusions for you.
Later, when he reached Mingzhao, he recounted the previous conversation. Mingzhao said, "Dagu can truly be called straight from head to tail."
"It was simply that he did not meet with one who could appreciate him. Mount Shàn then asked, "When the tree falls and the vines wither, what then?
Zhāo said, "This will cause Míngzhào to laugh even more freshly. Because of this, Mount Shàn attained realization and remarked, "Míngzhào, it turns out, has a blade hidden within his laughter."
Thereupon, he prostrated from afar and repented his transgressions. (In one manuscript, there is a slight variation.
The *Haixin Xin* verse states: "The tree falls and the vines wither; I offer this single question. He lets out a great laugh—there is a reason for it."
The pronged antelope hangs from its horns; there is no place to seek it. Even until now, the laughter has not ceased. Wenshu said:
"When the tree falls and the vines wither—ask Daomai. He laughs heartily, revealing his total capacity.
Having sold his bedding and exhausted his travel funds, to whom can he speak on this cold autumn night? Dahong Yu said: "A cold blade, polished to a razor’s edge. Laughter.
Coming from within, the *śakara* eye admits no alteration. A single eye, like a golden dragon, once raised its claw;
the skull felt the pain, and the crown of the head opened. Kumu Cheng said: Leisurely casting a straight hook by the riverbank, There comes a time when the golden-scaled fish takes the bait.
If it can leap three times and ascend through spiritual transformation, The old fisherman need not frown with his brows.
Chuanfeng said: "This adds to the ever-fresh smile of Guishan. At that time, he presented it directly to you.
Mingzhao leaked Guishan’s secret; boundless brilliance was bestowed upon others. Jingshan Daokai said:
"If one uses these words to establish the fundamental tenets, one fails Mingzhao, the One-Eyed Dragon. Within his smile, he suddenly distinguished between mud and water."
On the road, one finally realizes that a thousand li share the same wind.
Chan Master Xiangyan Xian uttered this saying: "It is like a person climbing a tree, with a branch held in his mouth, yet neither hand grasping a branch."
His feet did not touch the tree. Suddenly, while he was beneath it, someone asked him about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West.
To not answer would have been to disregard the question; yet to answer would have meant losing his life. At such a moment, what was to be done?
Then, the Venerable Houtou stepped forward and said, "I do not ask about having climbed the tree; please, Master, speak before you have climbed it. The Master [said]: [This is the point].
He laughed heartily. Xuedou Xian said:
"To speak while on the tree is easy; to speak while under the tree is difficult. I, this old monk, shall climb the tree;
bring forth a question! Cuiyan Zhi said: "The questioner and the respondent cannot avoid losing their lives."
"Life! Now, how would you, a patch-robed monk, handle this? Tiantong Jue said: "Upāda the Elder is a wicked thief;
he uses his 'unrighteous hand' to strike where one cannot guard. Even if one were a master of true substance, one would often fail to manage one's own hands and feet.
Xuedou was a man who could discern circumstances and recognize fortune or misfortune; even when he reached this point,"
One can only hide one's body while exposing one's shadow. Do you understand Xiangyan’s way of acting? Where are the two thousand swordsmen now?
To Zhuang Zhou alone is granted the vision of a time of great peace.
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "The ancient adept devised many stratagems; How could one branch sprout yet another?
Like a fine horse glimpsing the shadow of the whip, Chasing clods of earth is no work for a lion’s cub. Fohuiquan says:
A great laugh—no needle or awl! How is it when one is up in the tree compared to when one has not yet climbed?
Even if Xiangyan possessed many skills, bystanders could not help but knit their brows. Dizang En said: "Xiangyan’s hanging words are truly worthy of appreciation.
With his mouth clutching a branch, he hangs suspended in the tree. At this moment, we do not ask about the mechanism of the Patriarchs; tell me, what do you say?"
As for my own appearance: Master Yi of Shangfang said: "Turning around on a narrow path is difficult; East and west are entirely mountains.
Where the traveler does not go, The fallen flowers lie still when the wind ceases. Master Yi of Shimen said: "The ancient sages, with hearts of compassion, benefit those who come after;
They hold a branch-tip dripping with dew, revealing their entire being. Even if there were no news on the profound path, One could not avoid..."
When Master Linji Xuan was planting pine and cypress trees at Huangbo, Huangbo asked, "What are you doing planting so many trees in the deep mountains?
The Master replied, "First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate; second, to serve as a landmark for future generations."
Dao’iao struck the ground once with his hoe. Huangbo said, "Even so, you have already received twenty blows from me.
The Master struck the ground once again and said, "Hehe. Huangbo said, "My school will flourish greatly in the world because of you."
Guishan asked Yangshan, "At that time, Huangbo entrusted only Linji with his instructions; was there anyone else?
Yangshan replied, "There was, but the years have been so many that I do not wish to mention it to you, Master.
Guishan said, "Even so, I still wish to know. Just speak of it. Yangshan said, "One person pointed the way south; the command reached Wu and Yue."
As they were traveling, they encountered a great wind and stopped. Daowei Zhe said, "Linji acting like this is much like tripping on level ground.
Nevertheless, only one who does not change in the face of danger can be called a true man. Huangbo said, "My lineage has reached you and shall flourish greatly in the world.
This too is like loving a child so much that one fails to notice their ugliness. Ying’an Hua said, "Huangbo..."
Although the Way is thus, you have already received twenty blows from me. Such is the natural course of raising a child.
Although Linji’s true command was being carried out, it is a pity that he allowed himself to be buried alive by the side of his hoe.
Yangshan’s understanding has not yet emerged from the common stream; how could it stop merely upon encountering a great wind?
Why did he not say at that time: "Only when the entire realm of empty space is exhausted will this story finally go far"?
Is this not having both head and tail straight? Today, Jiangshan pulls down his face-skin and intends to meet everyone. Suddenly—
He held up his staff, struck it once, and said: "To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the victor, one must be a lion’s cub.
Cuiyan’s true verse says: "The mountains and rivers were bound by oaths of fealty, and the territories were mapped out; beneath the Han Gao Emperor stood Zhang Liang."
"Of a thousand words and ten thousand phrases, no one understands; yet they follow the warbling orioles over the low wall.
Master Duofu was asked by a monk, "What is the single grove of bamboo at Duofu? The Master said, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, curved."
Huanglong Xin said: "If it is slanted, let it be slanted; if it is curved, let it be curved. What do you call 'a cluster of bamboo'?
Songyuan Yue said: "A leap year once every three years. He gave a shout.
Ying’an Hua’s verse says: “One stem, two stems leaning; their intent is as venomous as a snake. Three stems, four stems bent;
there is no doubt they will enter hell. If one realizes this is wrong upon hearing these words, one returns home having passed the imperial examination with an empty mind.
How laughable is the old man of Jiangshan, who for no reason has entered the wild weeds.”

Exhausting all profound dialectics, it would be like placing a single hair in the great void; exhausting all the world’s pivotal mechanisms, it would be like casting a single drop into a vast abyss.
He then burned his commentaries and sub-commentaries, paid his respects, took his leave, and departed.
Baizhang Yuan’s verse says: “The interplay of light and darkness is not worth mentioning; To have even a hair’s breadth of understanding is not yet intimate.
When the paper lamp suddenly goes out, the eyes emerge— The Great Tang is shattered, and there is not a single person left. Baoning Yong said:
A single cascade falls before the rocky cliff; at midnight, the golden sun shines upon the palm.
Opening his great mouth, he adds to his spirit and vigor; with whom shall he traverse the world together? Master Shangfang Yi said:

Tianning Lian said: "The 'cracking and pecking' kōan of Deqiao and Longtan is like a mustard seed and a needle meeting in perfect accord within the profound mystery.
Perched atop a solitary peak, he sits with his head shrouded; he does not look back at the green mountains, yet the clouds return of their own accord."
A monk asked Zen Master Yunyan Cheng, "For twenty years you served as attendant at Baizhang; why was the lamp of your mind not transmitted?
The Master said, "The jeweled flower crown upon my head. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'the jeweled flower crown upon my head'?"
The Master said, "The Emperor of the Great Tang and the King of the Netherworld. Later, a monk raised this question to Chan Master Jiugong Qian:
"What is the meaning of 'the Emperor of the Great Tang and the King of the Netherworld'? Qian replied, "I am reminded of the words of Dongshan."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: The jade whip raised high strikes the golden gate, Drawing forth the coral whose price is beyond measure.
The ancient Wheel-Turning King displays his full majesty; Without manifesting the precious seal, he is naturally honored.
Chan Master Xianglin Yuan was asked by a monk, "What is the single lamp within the room? The Master said, "Three people testify that a tortoise becomes a turtle.
(Alternatively, this is attributed to Dawsui.
Touzi Qing’s verse on this says: "When six ears conspire, the matter can be accomplished; speaking directly expresses the person of sincere heart."
"Who has come to nudge the lamp-flame within the chamber? A white-haired child with two newly sprouted tufts of hair.
Xichan Xu said: "Three people have testified that a tortoise is a turtle. They have just leaked the celestial mechanism. The wooden man sings atop the ridge;
the stone woman sheds blood from her eyes."
When Chan Master Ciming Yuan was among the assembly, he went to the quarters of Master Zhi.
While Zhi sat there opening and closing his box and lighting incense, the Master asked, "How do you burn this? Zhi then placed it into the incense burner and lit it.
The Master said, "The clumsy fellow has gone off again like that."
Baizhang Yuanwen’s verse says: "A thousand people, ten thousand people, walk a single path; How many move their bodies without moving a step?
Facing one another, they take up the incense burner and offer it as incense; Yet these clumsy fellows act just like this."

Chan Master Bānsǎodǐ (Banshao Didu) received the imperial edict from Jiangxi. He concealed his name and, whenever students came to question him, he would indicate his answer only by striking the ground with his staff.
Consequently, he was known at the time as "Master Didu" (Staff-Striking Ground). One day, a monk hid his staff away.

Thereupon, he questioned [the Master]. The Master merely opened his mouth. A monk asked the Master’s attendant, "As for the meaning of the Master's striking the ground whenever someone asks him a question—what is its intent?
The attendant immediately took a piece of firewood from beneath the hearth and threw it into the cauldron.
When Chan Master Zhaozhou Shen saw a monk sweeping the floor, he asked, "Sweeping like this, will you ever get it clean?
The monk said, "The more I sweep, the more there is. The Master said, "Is there no one who can shake off the dust? The monk asked, "Who is it that shakes off the dust?"
The Master looked at him and asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go ask Yunju.
Later, that monk asked Yunju, "What is one who brushes away the dust? Yunju said, "This blind fellow!"
Cao Shan Benji Chanshi asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from sweeping the floor.
The Master said, "Did you sweep before the Buddha or after the Buddha? The monk said, "I swept both before and after at the same time. The Master said, "Then hand me my kashaya robe."
Wuzu Keqin cited the words of a monk, saying: "What kind of mental activity is this, O Master?
Fenyang Shanzhao composed a verse on it, which says: "His capacity and measure are square and round; I see him clearly. I ask you: sweeping the floor is an act of compassion."
"Sweeping away both past and present at once— this too is the second function brought forth.
Once, while Master Xuefeng Cun was carrying a bundle of rattan during a communal work session, he encountered a monk on the road and simply threw it down.
The monk stood below with his hands joined in *añjali*. As the Master was about to take hold of him, the Master stepped on him and knocked him over.

Upon returning, he reported this to Changsheng, saying, "Today I have kicked that monk; it felt truly exhilarating. Changsheng said, "Only then will you have truly sent this monk to the Nirvana Hall. The Master then desisted.
At Fayen Monastery, there were two monks who each presented their own reasoning and requested the Master to adjudicate.
The Master said, "Both of you monks enter the Nirvana Hall at once. Xuanjue said, "Where is the place where one monk takes the other's place to enter the Nirvana Hall?
Xuedou Xian said, "This is much like when a member of the eastern family dies, and the western family offers condolences."
"It would also be well to give him one kick. Baizhang Yuan said, "Xuefeng wins five hundred outside, but loses one thousand within the house.
Chongshou Zhou said, "This turn of phrase, however, belongs back to you, elder brother."
Dongchan Qi said: "As for Changsheng’s meaning—how is it? Nantang Jing said: "Xuefeng’s one kick transmitted the separate teaching outside the scriptures;
Xuedou’s one kick has had no peer for a thousand ages. Changsheng’s response was like losing money and then suffering punishment.
If anyone can examine this thoroughly, I, this old monk, will simply laugh loudly. But tell me, what is he laughing at?"
"Is this the same as 'stepping,' or is it different? After a long silence, he said, "Investigate!
Then Fangyi added a verse: "A fragrant bait is cast in secret by the riverbank; Indeed, a golden-scaled fish is caught and brought home."
It was not that the silken line was reeled in too quickly; it was nearly lost to the herons. Fodeng Xun said: "How magnificent!
Old Master Xue, a hero among the Dharma. The firewood on his shoulder is presented face-to-face.

Had he not recognized it before him as the direct blow, his whole body would have been kicked over and his bag emptied. Only by realizing the burden was heavy because of the bundles of wood could he naturally [attain liberation]."
The heavy does not become light. What Mountain [Shan] reports to all fellow practitioners of Chan: A child must indeed be one’s own biological offspring.
Chan Master Xingjiao Shou, while at the abode of National Teacher Yao of Tiantai, attained awakening one day when a load of firewood he was carrying fell.
He then composed a verse, saying: "Crashing down, it is no other thing; Spreading out, it is not dust. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth..."

Lion and elephant; dragon and tiger; ox and deer; cat, dog, tortoise, and fish;
hare and snake; flying and running lions and elephants.
Master Yunyan Cheng was once asked by Yaoshan, "I have heard that you are skilled at performing the lion dance; is this true? The Master replied, "It is.
Yaoshan asked, "How many performances have you performed? The Master said, "I have performed six. Yaoshan said, "I can also perform it.
The Master asked, "How many performances have you performed, Preceptor? Yaoshan said, "I have performed one. The Master said, "One is six; six is one."
1. Later, the Master arrived at Mt. Gui. Gui asked, "I hear that you were playing with lions at Yaoshan; is this true? The Master said, "It is.
Gui said, "If you play with them constantly, will there ever be a time to set them down? The Master said, "If I wish to play, I play; if I wish to set them down, I set them down."
Yangshan said, "When you set it aside, where is the lion? The Master said, "Set it aside! Set it aside! Fachang said, "What a magnificent lion!
It is simply that he has managed it so as to have a head but no tail. [Fachang continued:
"At that time, had he seen Yangshan say, 'When you set it aside, where is the lion? he would have immediately let loose the golden lion crouching on the ground."
The "Hairy Lion" (Mao Shizi). This leaves even Guishan with no way to hide his body. Zantang Zhun said:
"Yaoshan and Yunyan have frustrated people to death; these two sons cannot even manage to play with their father’s one lion.
If it were I, Upāsaka Zhun, I would need only to play with it alone and drag it out—taking its head for its tail, and taking its tail for its head."
Twirling his two golden eyes and clutching his iron talons, he lets out a roar that causes all beasts within a hundred *li* to hide their tracks and all birds in the sky to fall in disarray.

Before the Venerable Zhun has even displayed his lion, I ask the assembly to open your eyes wide and watch first as I establish the opening scene. With his staff, he hurls it down and says: "Within this..."
"O messenger, how many people can truly know you? [He] lets out a shout.
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "The nun addresses the cub of the golden-haired lion; beneath the sandalwood forest, amidst the green sedge."
Set it down! Set it down! His majesty is complete in itself. One exit, six exits, the eyebrows are kicked up. Not to be grasped; how many who know the subtle?
When the stars stream forth, one need not ask of three thousand miles. When the wind clears beyond the heavens and he bellows, for you I shall suck dry the waters of the West River. *Duḥ!*
When Chan Master Yangshan Ji saw a snow lion, he pointed at it and said, "Is there anyone who can pass through this color?
The assembly had no reply.
Yunmen said, "At that moment, he should have simply pushed it over. Xuedou Xian said, "Yunmen only understood..."
He pushed it over, but did not know how to lift it back up. Lanxi Jue said, "I now ask you all: how far apart are 'pushing over' and 'lifting up'?
The staff has passed right through the eyebrows and nostrils! He let out a great laugh and threw down the staff.
Lingyin Chang said, "To push it over is wrong; to lift it up is also wrong. Furthermore—"
"Does the Way have anything that surpasses this form?
Tiantong Jue’s verse says: "One fall and one rise; the lion in the snowy courtyard is cautious in its transgressions yet harbors benevolence."
Brave in action yet seeing only the righteous; clear light shines before the eyes, yet one seems lost in the home. Turning with clarity, one still falls back into a position.
For the patch-robed monk, there is nothing to rely upon. Dying together and living together—what "this" and what "that"?
The warm news breaks through the plum blossoms as spring reaches the cold branches; the cool breeze sheds the leaves as autumn clarifies the turbid waters.
When Chan Master Huangbo Yun of Longhu was asked by Baizhang, "Where have you come from? the Master replied, "I have come from gathering mushrooms at Mount Daxiong.
Baizhang asked, "Did you see the tiger? The Master then let out a tiger's roar. Baizhang raised his axe and made a motion as if to strike.
Baizhang said, "The situation is such. The Master then gave Baizhang a single slap. Baizhang laughed heartily and returned.

Ascending the seat, he addressed the assembly, saying, "At the foot of Mount Daxiong there is a great beast; you all must watch out for it. Today, the old fellow Baizhang has been personally caught by its mouth."
Miaoshan asked Yangshan. Yang said, "How would you have handled it, Master? Miaoshan said, "At that time, Baizhang should have struck him dead with a single blow of his axe.
Why did things come to this? Yang said, "Not so. Miaoshan said, "And what about you, my son?
Yang said, "Baizhang not only could ride the tiger’s head; he also knew how to grasp the tiger’s tail. Miaoshan said, "My son..."
There is a line concerning a precipitous cliff. Wuzu Ke said, "Baizhang is much like a thief whose heart is filled with trepidation;
Huangbo is one who finds it difficult to forget what he is most familiar with.
Foyan Yuan composed a verse on this: "The striped tiger beneath Mount Daxiong—when touched, it wounds; who dares to look upon it?"
A mother’s heart, though she has encountered but a single word; when has she ever laid her axe upon her waist?
When Chan Master Xinxin of Longtan first arrived to visit Deshan, Deshan asked him: "I have long heard of Longtan.
Now that you have actually arrived, neither the pond is seen nor the dragon appears. The Master said, "You have truly reached Longtan. Deshan then prostrated himself.
He then withdrew. Xuánjué said: "As for Dàoshān, did he approve Lóngtán or not? If he approved him, where was Dàoshān’s eye?
If he did not approve him, why did he become his successor? Xuědòu Xiǎn said: "Bring it forth!"

"Taking a mistake for a mistake. Huanglong Xin said, "Xuedou speaks thus because he does not know that Deshan takes a mistake for a mistake, and Longtan takes a mistake for a mistake. A monk who recognizes good and ill fortune must know where this leads;
those who have not yet passed through the barrier should also investigate this clearly. Do you understand? Even if you were to plant and cultivate it, it would still not be so."
"Material for a ridgepole. Yunfeng Yue said, "Great and small De-shan were both drowned in a jar of minced fish.

Baoning Yong, acting on behalf of De-shan, said, "It would have been better to let him go. Wuzu Yan said, "The old man Longtan may truly be called one who rides the thief's horse to pursue the thief."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: Vast and profound, it receives all streams; In vain one holds fragrant bait and casts the golden hook.
Wind and clouds gather, thunder rolls— One must surely wonder why the Dragon King does not emerge. Luohan Nan said:
Having personally reached the dragon pool, the dragon is not seen; this perfectly accords with the realization of the sublime mystery by those who have awakened first.

A thatched hut is nestled upon a solitary peak, where one sits in stillness facing the cold moon hanging in the azure sky. Foguo said: "Having personally reached the dragon pool, the dragon is not seen.
The dragon of the dragon pool does not reside within the pool itself. Under the blue sky and bright sun, clouds and rain arise; thus it has been for thousands of ages.
Laughing along with Old Master Shaye. Changling Zhuo said: "The pool is not seen; the dragon does not appear. Having personally reached the dragon pool, one meets with a blemish.
In a flash he returns, his tusks like swords; from the tip of the staff, blazing flames are cast forth."
Chan Master Yantou Huo was asked by a monk, "What is it like when one encounters a fierce tiger on the road?
The Master said, "Press! Wenyuan Qian said, "The heavens have no four walls; the earth has no eight directions.

Even if you were to have ten thousand arrows piercing your heart and a thousand spears striking your body, you still could not withstand this single pivot. Do you understand? Six times six is originally..."
Thirty-six. A former verse by Po’an says: "A single pressure from Yantou causes empty space to shatter; this is the wondrous secret of the immortals, not transmitted even between father and son."
When Chan Master Xuansha Beizhu and Tianlong were working together at Haikeng to chop firewood, they encountered a tiger. Tianlong said, "That is a tiger ahead.
The Master said, "It is your tiger. When Tianlong returned to the monastery, he asked, "Just now in the mountains we saw a tiger, and you said it was 'your' tiger.
I do not know what your venerable intention was, Master. The Master replied, "In this Sahā world, there are four kinds [of tigers]."
This is a heavy obstruction. If a person can penetrate it, I grant that you have emerged from the realms of the aggregates (*skandha*).
Dongchan Qi said, "Venerable Elder, when the ancients saw through this, they said, 'My body and mind are like the great earth and empty space.'"
"Can people today still penetrate this? Xuedou Xian said, "If you wish to act as a teacher to gods and men, there is truly a tiger ahead.
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "A fierce tiger stands alone in the path, its majesty shaking; its claws and fangs are indeed sharp as needles."
"Pitiful are those who do not realize they are losing their lives; how truly lamentable it is to gather up their shattered bones!

Master Fohui Quan said: 'Tiger before, tiger behind—there is an urgent need to look! His fierce and majestic wind, his raw and savage claws and talons. Through ancient times and the present, how many woodcutters have failed to look back?
How many have lost their bodies and forfeited their lives? Had they but looked back, he would have sat majestically, cutting off the mountain.'"
The Path Ahead. Foyuan Yuan said: "The Master’s expedient means are too compassionate. Your words are truly those of an ancient sage.
When the divine light of ten thousand miles surges from behind the crown of your head, how could you possibly use birth and death to frighten the ignorant?"
Chan Master Mingzhao Qian asked a monk, "A tiger gives birth to seven cubs; which one has no tail? The monk replied, "The seventh one has no tail.
Gushan Gui composed a verse on this: "A tailless tiger is difficult to approach; To draw near is to bring harm to one's life."
Unless one personally understands how to seize the tiger’s head, naturally the head will be straight and the tail will follow. Jingshan Hongzhi said:
"The seventh [stage] is a smoke-eating fox with no tail; its 'ox-devouring' breath is already enough to boast of.
The monastic communities clamor and dispute over words and lips; how many travelers have actually reached home?"
When a monk asked Great Putong Chan Master, "How can one obtain the pearl from beneath the chin of a black dragon? the Master clapped his hands and blinked at him.
Huanglong Nan Chan Master said, "When it comes to chanting praises atop the bell tower and planting vegetables beneath the bed frame, what then? Huang—
Chan Master Hesheng said: "A fierce tiger sits blocking the road. Gushan Gui’s verse says:
"A fierce tiger sits blocking the road; Wandering fish pass beneath its paws.
I will not emulate Old Zihu, Who instead struck Liu Tiemo. Jingshan Daokai said: "Directly out, directly in—yet one does not recognize it face-to-face."
What more can be proposed? Why such a desperate hurry? Baizhang Yuan said:
"When the autumn wind moves the wutong trees, the leaves fall first; at sunset, one sits long in the mountain hut.
Rising at dawn and looking back, everywhere the scenery is seen within a torn paper curtain. (This is found in the *Ji ningsu*).
A monk asked Nanquan Puyuan, "After you pass away, where will you go? The Master said, "I shall become a water buffalo.
The monk asked, "May I follow you there? The Master said, "If you come, you must carry my halter."
"A stalk of grass is brought. Fenyang Zao’s verse says: "Within the category it is difficult to discern; one must distinguish it clearly. Horned and hairy, one is still not yet awake.
Only when the grass is taken in the mouth does movement truly begin; head and all things are spontaneously true and numinous. Fohui Quan said:
Moving freely among those of different species, Dragged through the nostrils, it is difficult to restrain.

When meeting one who has caught a blade of grass in its mouth, One lies high in the deep clouds, letting the hair turn white. Foyin Yuan said: "His conduct has always been among those of different species;
I know not with whom his horns and tusks match. If he comes to meet you carrying water and grass in his mouth, He will wag his tail and shake..."
The wind blows across the four wilds.
At Yueshan’s evening *can*, he did not light the lamp. The Master said, "I have a phrase; I will tell it to you when a calf gives birth to a calf.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "A calf has given birth to a calf; it is simply that you, Master, do not speak."
The Master called to his attendant, "Bring the lamp here. The monk then withdrew his body and entered the assembly.
Dongshan said, "This monk understands; he simply refuses to prostrate. Faldeng Qin said:
"Those born are the male calves and female calves. Another gloss says: "Born twins. Cuiyan Zhi said: "I do not say so.
