It is secret. But alas, this monk has administered a dose of castor oil, causing his heart, liver, and five viscera to be vomited out all at once.
Even if one were to find fire, it would already be the break of dawn in the middle of the night.
Foyan Yuan’s verse says: A young bull knows its calf quite well; Both eyes are a deep crimson, like indigo.
Though one holds a torch to search for it, there is no place to be found; Everyone, let us all go together and investigate at once.
Cen Master Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Where does a person who knows 'it' go?
Nanquan replied, "He goes to become a water buffalo at the house of a donor before the mountains. The Master said, "Thank you for your instruction.
Nanquan said, "Last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window."
Yunfeng Yue said, "Had it not been for Nanquan, Caizhou would have been utterly destroyed.
Fojian Qin said, "If one were to shed tears again and again, even the Eastern Sea would surely run dry. Jingshan Guangqiao said, "The old man Yunfeng lost one of his eyes;
he did not realize that it was precisely because of those later words that Caizhou was destroyed on the spot."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: “Having yanked off the tip of the nose, where is it? Mud and water are tossed about wildly, flowing freely.
As the sun sets, he rides back home, sitting backward; Then again, a sliver of moon rises over the Eastern Mountain. Baofeng Xiangyun says:
The golden-haired lion emerges from its cave and seizes his father’s stratagem; with a simultaneous roar, the foxes are filled with doubt.
At the third watch, the moon through the window is like broad daylight; who would dare come again to dally with such peril? Gushan Gui said: "Seen often before the eyes, it is but ordinary;
it does not startle, yet it endures for a long time. It preserves the moon of the cold window at night, following [the master] at the third watch."

Regarding the phrase "The old thatched hall," Jingshan Daowu said: "Cutting the cloth according to the body's dimensions, measuring the water to drive the pestle—there is not even a hair’s breadth of error;
yet, for now, one must remain outside the gate."
Chan Master Guishan Lingyou addressed the assembly, saying: "After I am gone, I shall become a water buffalo at the home of a lay patron below the mountain.
On its left flank, I will write five characters: 'The monk so-and-so of Guishan.
At that time, if you call me the monk of Guishan, I am still the water buffalo; if you call me the water buffalo, I am still the monk of Guishan."
"O so-and-so! Tell me, what should you call this? Yangshan came forward, bowed, and departed.
Yunju Ying said, "The Master has no other title. Zifu, acting on his behalf, drew a perfect circle and held it up.
Xinluo Qing made this mudra-gesture [the "ox"] in his place and presented it. He further said: "Only those on the same path know. Nantang Yong said:
"The one thousand five hundred good spiritual friends obtained only half.
Banzhao Che made this mudra-gesture in his place at that time and presented it. He further said: "The preaching has been preached; the commentary has been commented upon."
"Wuqu (Wuquan) said, 'Excellent! Baoning Yong said, "In one stroke, they enter the mud and wade through the water.
Jingzhong Yue said, "Although Mushi was a good cause, he invited an evil fruit; he will certainly become a water buffalo.
Had I seen him at that time, I would have said, 'Where has this old ox gone? I guarantee it would have been quite a scene."
*Moluo*. Da Miao Zhi said, "He has blinded the eyes of the monks of the world. Dao Wu Zhen’s verse says:
"The water buffalo of Mount Miao is a direct mechanism; clearly manifesting the human form, it reveals the profound wonder."
"From both sides, words emerge from the place where the emanations appear; night birds fly into the forest at dusk and take flight again at dawn.
Baizhang Yuan said: "I do not say it is not Mount Huishan, nor do I say it is not the ox. Clearly, where can one discern the traces?
To miss the path by even a hair’s breadth, for ten thousand kalpas there will be no way to emerge. Baoning Yong said: "To alter one's appearance and change one's form..."
Turning his head away—how could one conceal his traces when facing the light? Though the names "donkey" and "horse" may be called out, how many bystanders are filled with shame?
Zhenru Zhe said: Horns and hooves are distinct; he is present everywhere. No need for managing or binding;
no need for gathering or storing. One simply knows not to trespass upon another’s crops; Following conditions as they arise, one finds freedom in water and grass.
Buddha-Mind said: "With a mere thought, he turns his hand and writes characters in the air; they are already complete. In the midst of bustling confusion, people ask about the clarity of both ends.
Had Qu Yuan not encountered the fisherman, who in ten thousand ages would have discussed his solitary sobriety? Haiyin Xin said: "A cow on the mountain below, a monk on the mountain above;
though the names differ as many as the sands of the Ganges, this is not yet the ultimate ability. I always love the evening clouds returning before sunset."
Combined: Far-off mountains, boundless, in endless layers of blue. Master Wu-jin said: "The wild paths and steep crags deceive and ruin people;
long ago they have already plowed through the vast fields of spring. Sometimes they fall into the weeds where no trace can be found—this is the manifestation of the old man of Mt. Mui."
One day, while Master Huangbo Yun was walking with Minister Pei, they saw a farmer plowing a field.
The mud was so deep that the ox could not move forward, so the farmer beat it. Minister Pei felt pity for him. The Master said, "He beats it cruelly.
Minister Pei asked, "How can a great virtuous teacher (dà shàn zhīshí) be like this? The Master replied, "His two legs cannot do the plowing."
A verse by Shui’an says: Master Yun and Prime Minister Pei shared a compassionate heart for others; They disregarded whether the mud was deep or the water was deep.
With painful blows and fierce hammers, they acted among the various species; Let their skin be made to bleed profusely.
Chan Master Deshan Xuanjian was asked by a monk, "What is the white ox on the open ground? The Master said, "Hūṃ, hūṃ.
The monk asked, "What does it eat? The Master said, "It eats."
Dongshan Cóng’s verse says: A jade-horned, frost-haired ox on open ground, Manifesting its traces throughout the human and celestial realms.
Unlike the one on the Snowy Ridge that roars constantly, Nor like the one at Mount Míng which is gathered in daily.
As National Teacher Shenshan Mimi and Dongshan were walking along, they suddenly saw a white deer run past. The Master said, "How spirited! Dongshan asked, "What do you mean?
The Master said, "It is much like a commoner being invested as a high minister. Dongshan said, "Even you, so old and venerable, speak such words.
The Master asked, "And what about you? Dongshan said, "A family of generations of official rank, fallen into obscurity for a brief moment."
(Alternatively, he became a white rabbit.
Master Tiantong Jue’s verse says: "Resisting the power of frost and snow, walking with ease through the clouds and mists. Xie Hui was dismissed from the state; Sima Xiangru crossed the bridge.
Xiao He and Cao Cao’s strategies were able to establish the Han nest. Xu You wished to avoid Yao’s favor; honor and disgrace are like..."
Startled by the profundity, he gained deep self-confidence. His true feelings mingled with the traces of the world, blending among fishermen and woodcutters.
When a monk asked Touzi Tongchan, "What is the white ox on the open ground? the Master said, "Chit-chit.
The monk asked, "What does it eat? The Master said, "Chi-chi."
The *Gāndīng Huìjué Sòng* says: "The white ox on the open ground raises the question; At every opportunity he barks, his fangs and teeth chilling.
One knows not what it is that he consumes; With every bite, he dries up the vast blue sea."
Chan Master Yongquan Xin was tending cattle at his monastery during the suppression of the Buddhist teachings by Emperor Wuzong of the Tang dynasty.

At that time, two Chan travelers named Jiang and De encountered him on the road; seeing the Master riding the ox, they did not recognize him and said, "The hooves and horns are quite distinct, yet we cannot help but fail to recognize the rider.
The Master spurred the ox away, and the two travelers subsequently rested beneath a tree to brew tea.
"Tea," the Master said, turning back. As the two monks approached the ox, he greeted them, offered them seats, and served them tea.
The Master then asked, "Where have you two Zen guests recently departed from? They replied, "From over there. The Master asked, "What is the matter of 'over there'?
One of the Zen guests lifted his tea cup. The Master said, "This is still 'over here. What is the matter of 'over there'? The two were speechless. The Master said:
Do not say that the one riding the ox does not recognize what is good.
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "The lush green grass stretches far—how could it change with autumn? The cowherd boy and the white ox roam at their ease."
On a road amidst the heterodox, it is difficult for people to see; they turn around and say that one who rides an ox does not recognize the ox.
When a monk asked Chan Master Fengxue Zhao, "Deer and elk move in herds; how can one shoot the leader among them? the Master said:
The fishing boat carries [the fish] to the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers; with a choked breath, there is no one to ask the white herons.
Touzi Qing’s verse says: In the inner chambers of the forbidden palace, sight and hearing are perilous; Thinking askance, standing to one side, he lets the crimson line hang down.
Clouds break over the Han village; the marsh islands stretch far away. At twilight on the ridge, the gibbons cry as the solitary moon follows them.
When a monk asked Master Cheshen of Shimen, "What is the meaning of Yunguang’s statement, 'The intention behind acting as an ox'? The Master said:
"In the humble alley, he does not ride a golden horse; returning to his path, he puts on his tattered robe."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: Amidst the clusters of auspicious grass, I am loath to sleep; Wandering slowly everywhere, I am utterly serene.
Clad in fur and bearing horns, I am difficult for people to recognize; I tell the boy with the staff: there is no need for the whip.

Regarding the story of Chan Master Nanquan Yuan of the Cats and Dogs: Once, when the two head monks of the two halls were disputing over a cat, the Master picked it up and said, "Monks, if you can speak, you shall save it;
if you cannot speak, I shall kill it. The assembly had no reply, so the Master then killed it. Upon returning—
In the evening, when Zhaozhou returned from outside, the Master related the incident to him. Zhaozhou then took off his sandals, placed them on his head, and went out.
The Master said, "If you had been here, you would have saved the cat."
Baofu Zhan said, "Even so, this is still just tearing one's straw sandals.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Big and small Zhaozhou can only save themselves. Baoning Yong, acting on their behalf, simply extended his neck toward Nanquan.
Fenyang Shanzhao’s verse says: "The two hall-senior monks have not yet opened their blind eyes; Each cat must struggle for its own share.
Nanquan’s hand cuts them in two pieces; The straw sandals remain for later practitioners. Xuedou Xian said:
Both halls were occupied by Chan monks; they stirred up dust and smoke, leaving no recourse. Fortunately, Nanquan was able to issue the command;
with one stroke, he cut them in two, regardless of partiality. It is further said: When the public case is resolved, go ask Zhaozhou.
Wander at leisure within the city of Chang’an. No one understands the straw sandals worn upon his head; once you have returned to your home mountain, then—
Rest. Luohan Nan said: "The Master acts with sovereign mastery, severing ten thousand functions.
When Zhaozhou wore straw sandals upon his head, the precious mirror on its stand shone without partiality; how could the golden blade from its scabbard be wielded recklessly?
Yuantong Xian said: "Observe the military strategy where the smoke of war rises; were it not for the General, who would discern him? One blade, two pieces."
Huaiyi issued his command; his majestic influence remains a foundation of hegemonic heroism for a thousand ages. Foyuan said: "The strings of Boya can be mended with phoenix glue;
the melodies are ancient and the style is pure, such that the frosty moon may be gathered in one's palms. Nanquan, Nanquan—dragons and elephants follow in his footsteps. Foyan Yuan said:
"To bring peace to the state and peace to the people does not depend on military force; even a single arrow from Ru Lian was sufficient."
Sentiment: Where are the three thousand swordsmen now? Only you, General, are permitted to establish the Great Peace.
Chan Master Zhaozhou Sheng was asked by a monk, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? The Master said, "No.

The monk said, "All sentient beings, including even the wriggling insects, possess Buddha-nature. Why does the dog have none? The Master said, "Because it possesses the consciousness of karma (*karmavijñāna*)."
The nature remains. Furthermore, another monk asked the Master, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature? The Master said, "It has.
[The monk] asked, "If it has, why does it enter this skin-bag? The Master said, "Knowing it yet deliberately transgressing."
Cuiyan Zhi said: "To speak of existence and to speak of non-existence—these two colors are but one game. Now, what do you say? Wuzu Yan said:
"O assembly, how do you all understand this? In my ordinary practice, I simply bring up the word 'Mu' (無) and let it rest.
If you can penetrate this single word, no one in the world will be able to withstand you."
"How do you all penetrate this? Is there anyone who can penetrate it thoroughly? If there is, come forward and speak!
I do not want you to say 'it exists,' nor do I want you to say 'it does not exist,' nor do I want you to say 'it neither exists nor does not exist. How will you speak? Be careful!"
The verse by Zhenjing Wen says: "Though one speaks of the presence of karmic consciousness, who would say the meaning is not profound?

When the sea dries up, its bottom is finally seen; when a person dies, their mind remains unknown. Yuantong Xiu says: "In youth, I studied interpretations and was obscured from the path of the school;

In old age, I rely on them yet remain stuck in existence and non-existence. The ancient Buddhas are pure gold—who can discern their color? Deluded by intellectual cleverness, they compete in hesitation."
Chu. Puyong Ping said: "Existence and non-existence are both released and both gathered. Old Zhao’s mechanism is peerless in this world.
Try looking out from the high gate of the sea; a thousand rivers and ten thousand streams all flow eastward.
Shushan Ru said: "The dog has no Buddha-nature. His compassion is as deep as the ocean. Those who seek words and chase phrases are buried beneath a *zhang*."
Regarding the mind: Cishou Shen said, "Zhaozhou’s mouth contains realgar; who can discern its strengths and weaknesses beneath these words?
It is laughable how many are like dogs chasing clods of earth, barking pointlessly in the empty hall at night.
Jingshan Daokai said, "When someone asked about the Buddha-nature of the dog, Zhaozhou replied, 'It has none. To speak thus was to annihilate the Hu race in a single stroke. Yet, it still remains...
"Not a true man.
Zen Master Zihu Zong set up a wooden plaque at his gate. On the plaque it was written:

"Zihu has a dog that seizes people by the head when they come from above, seizes them by the waist when they come from the middle, and seizes them by the feet when they come from below. To hesitate for even a moment is to lose one's body and life. Or, if a newcomer arrives...
As soon as they looked at each other, the Master shouted, "Look out for the dog! As the monk turned his head, the Master returned to his quarters.
Later, a monk asked, "What is the Purple Lake Dog? The Master said, "Bark! Bark! (Hao hao).
Xuedou Xian said: "Everyone in the assembly says this monk was bitten by a mouthful. Indeed, he was bitten, but how is it that this monk still remains?
I dare ask you all: at Purple Lake, a dog kills anyone who is bitten; why then does this monk still remain?
If there were no one with the eye of wisdom to save this monk, even if Purple Lake were to appear in the world and bite him again—"
"What benefit is there in killing hundreds of thousands of people? Had I seen him at that time, I would have first cut down his signboard and then entered the hall;
waiting for this old fellow to shout 'Watch out for the dog!', I would have let loose a tawny-tailed tiger upon him."
If you all wish to see it now, the sun is already setting; return to the hall.
A verse by Foguo says: "The dog of Zihu is most fierce and terrifying; those who come should seek the light and not walk in darkness."
When you look toward the Way, it is as if not seen; when you bite down right at its head, your whole life is lost.
Zhengjue Yi said: "In the hall of Zihu, no one passes; it is only because the dog before the hall is fierce. Seeing its shadow or hearing its sound, one’s heart and gall are struck with terror;
facing it directly, how can one avoid losing one's wretched life? Foyuan Yuan said: "The Great Master of old was gone."
Bah! The circumstances of raising a dog are far too trivial. If a Zen guest comes seeking to snatch away the plaque, how could a dull blade ever compete with a hair-cutting razor?
Chan Master Caoshan Benji was asked by a monk, "What thing in the world is most precious? The Master replied, "A dead cat."
"Most precious. [A monk] asked, "Why is a dead cat so precious? The Master said, "No one puts a price on it. Tiantong Jue said:
"Caoshan’s wares do not enter the marketplace. Look closely, and you will see they are not worth even a single coin.
Caoshan finds value in what is cheap; in my place, I find value in what is expensive. Now tell me, is this so?"
Is there any contradiction here?
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "Foul-smelling and raw red, unfit for intimacy; A slight touch and the body is stained with blood.
Why is it that no one offers a price? Because it is not a treasure of this world."
The Great Sui Chan Master Zhen had a tortoise by his hermitage. A monk pointed at the tortoise and asked, "All sentient beings have skin wrapped around their bones;
why does this sentient being have bones wrapped around its skin? The Master picked up his straw sandals and covered them over the tortoise's back.
Baizhang Yuan’s verse says: "Clearly visible, the bones upon the skin are rounded; The layered lines of the hexagrams are even more worth beholding.
Picking up his straw sandals, he covers them all over; Da Sui was, however, deceived by this monk. Baoning Yong said:
Baring one's feet and hiding one's head—how strange and laughable! Who would say that after a thousand years this is a numinous tortoise?
When the rain pours down, it does not know how to flow away; when meeting floating wood, when will it ever happen again? The ancient Buddha Min said:

"The son of Lǎn'ān, the Great Master Suí—take this one move at the head and do not doubt further. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are all covered over; let him [the Master] wear his patched robe."
The disciple lowered his needle and awl. Heishan Fang said: "A clear reputation for a thousand ages, yet he is but an old man from the Sui dynasty.
His spiritual edge stands like a sheer cliff, utterly difficult to fathom. Failing to transcend the ordinary and the sage directly, he merely says to cover a tortoise with his shoes."
Zhaojue said in general: "I once took my skin and bones to question the Great Sui; yet at the very first stroke, I remained full of doubt.
How pitiable are those who endlessly seek traces of sound; they fail to realize the moment when the antelope hangs by its horns."
Cen Huiran of Sansheng asked Xuefeng, "I wonder what food a golden fish that has passed through the net eats?
Xuefeng said, "Wait until it comes out of the net, and then I will tell you. The Master said, "A teacher of fifteen hundred people and yet he does not even recognize the point of this question!
Xuefeng said, "The old monk’s administrative duties are too many."
Baofu Zhan said, "In contention there is insufficiency; in yielding there is abundance. Xuedou Xian said, "A pity he let him off.
He ought to have been given thirty blows. Not even one blow of this staff can be spared; it is truly rare to encounter such a master."
Chengtianzong said: "To cast a net that covers the heavens requires Xuefeng; to enter deep into the tiger’s den belongs to Sansheng.
Among the assembly, there are those who deliberate, saying, "Xuefeng was within the net, while Sansheng was outside the net.
How tragic, how tragic! This deeply wrongs the ancients. Were it not for these two masters, they could not have acted with such horizontal mastery."
He traveled throughout the world. Daowei Zhe said: "Sansheng may truly be described as one who has long been a guest at the Ten-Thousand-Fathom Dragon Gate;
Xuefeng is much like Mengchang—when the gate is opened, how could he fear a distinguished guest?"
Fenyang Zhao’s verse says: A fish that has passed through the net knows not the hook; Greedy for wandering in the waves, it mistakes the floating head [of the line] for its own.
To the one sitting on the high bank, fishing with compassion extended, It turns its tail and draws in the line, then boards the boat. Zhenjing Wen says:
The aged fisherman sits upon his fishing platform; golden-scaled dragons surge forth, drumming the waves. The sea-gate is vast and empty, yet he has just cast his net;
with a single thunderclap, heaven and earth are rent open. Zhenru Zhe said: "The golden-scaled dragon that pierces the net is a mechanism as swift as a flash of lightning;
do not say it lingers in the water or drags through the mud. With a single strike of thunder, the blue heavens tremble—what need is there to overturn the mountain torrents?"
The dwelling is not vast or overflowing. Wang Zu-yuan said: "Within the cave, there is no cloud; there is a separate heaven. Peach blossoms are like brocade;
willows are like cotton-wool. The immortals do not know how to discuss spring or summer; when the rocks crumble and the pines wither, it has been a year."
An ancient worthy said: "This day has passed, and life likewise diminishes accordingly; like a fish in scant water, what joy can there be in this? Shending Yin said:
"The ancients spoke thus not because it was beneficial, nor because it was not beneficial. Shending, however, does not agree.
This day has passed, and life likewise diminishes accordingly; like a fish in scant water, what is there that is not joyful?"
Now tell me: did he go against the ancients or follow them? Try to examine this closely. Take care.
The two senior monks, Shenming and Shenyue, once arrived at the Huai River and saw people pulling in a net. A carp had escaped through the mesh. Shenming said:
"Brother Shen, how excellent! You are truly like a monk. Shen said, "Even so, it would have been better had I not walked right into this net at the beginning.
Ming said, "Brother Shen, you still lack awakening. Only after traveling thirty li did Shen come to his senses.
(With slight variations in one version) Hujing Long said:
"The Senior Monk Ming has bait on his hook; the old Chan master Shen caught him on the very first cast.
At that time, if Hujing had seen him say, "Brother Shen, you still lack enlightenment," he would have simply replied: "Today..."

I have caught one in my net. This not only serves to shut the mouth of Master Ming, but also ensures that for a thousand ages to come, people will be spared from ridicule. I, too, possess a net that covers the heavens.
He then raised his whisk and said, "Do you see it? I have already called it a whisk; what do you all call it? If you call it...
It is made into a whisk, yet it remains within the net of this mountain monk. If you do not call it a whisk, where is the eye of the traveling monk?
Do you all see how Tiger Hill acts for others? Three surging waves rise high, thundering with a clap of lightning;
in one sound, it passes through the Dragon Gate of Yu.
Gushan Gui’s verse says: "Leaping out of the net, he soars away; what a fine, naturally gifted monk!
How could this compare to before he entered the net? Only upon awakening does one truly become a connoisseur. Jingshan Gao said:
How magnificent! With a single leap, he penetrates the deep abyss; like a thunderclap, he pursues his way and does not look back. One must laugh at those who burn their tails at the Dragon Gate;
they remain as before, with their foreheads marked by failure amidst the waves.

While Chan Master Guizong Chang was weeding grass, a presiding lecturer (zuozhu) came to visit him. By chance, he saw a snake passing by, whereupon the Master cut it with his hoe. The lecturer said, "I have long admired Guizong; I never expected you to be such a coarse monk. The Master replied: "I am not a coarse monk. You are the one who is coarse. When you saw the snake, did you see the snake, or did you see me? The lecturer said, "I saw both the snake and you, Master. The Master said, "If you saw both the snake and me, then you are indeed a coarse person. If you had seen neither the snake nor me, you would be a fine fellow. The lecturer said, "I saw neither the snake nor you, Master.

The Master said, "If you saw neither the snake nor me, then why do you call me a coarse monk? The lecturer was speechless. The Master then said, "You have come from afar seeking the Way, yet you have already lost it at the very outset. The lecturer bowed deeply and departed. The Master then recited this verse: "The snake is cut off; the weeds are cleared away. The weeds are cleared away; the snake is cut off. The weeds are not the weeds; the snake is not the snake. Weeds and snake are both cut off; Who is it that cuts them off?"
"You are coarse; I am coarse. The Master asked, "What is coarseness? The Master held up his hoe. The Master asked, "What is subtlety?
The Master made the gesture of slaying a snake. The Master said, "If that is so, then I shall follow it and act accordingly.
The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment following it and acting accordingly—where did you see me slay a snake? The Master had no reply.
Xuefeng asked Deshan, "What was the meaning behind the ancients' act of slaying a snake? Deshan struck him immediately. Xuefeng ran off.

Deshan called out, "Robe-wearing fellow! Xuefeng turned his head back. Deshan said, "In the future, when you attain awakening, you will finally understand that this old man’s heart is one of thoroughgoing, grandmotherly compassion.
Xuedou Xian commented: "Guizong only knew how to be cautious at the beginning; he could not protect [the teaching] until the end."
[The Master] said, "At the end, Deshan was indeed able to uphold the command, yet he had not yet clearly understood the 'Slaying the Snake.
He then said, 'Great assembly, watch as Cui-feng today slays three or five [snakes],' and with his staff, he struck them all at once, dispersing them.

Fo-jian Qin said, "Although Gui-zong’s approach was coarse, there was subtlety within the coarseness; although the Dharma-master’s approach was subtle, there was coarseness within the subtlety. One must attain both the coarse and the subtle."
"Let both be forgotten. You must first grasp the meaning of 'slaying the snake' before you can succeed. If you have grasped it, feel free to act in accordance with it.
If you have not yet grasped it, each of you must look carefully at your own feet. [He threw down his staff and descended from his seat.]
Fenyang Zhao’s verse says: "The Master of Mount Lu received those of superior capacity; He displayed compassion by slaying a snake on purpose.
When the Master Mao was startled and terrified, He instead said, 'You were careless and mistaken in your judgment. Haixin Xin says:
The great function, sweeping across and intersecting like a flash of lightning, leaves even the Śakra-eye blurred and sticky.
Deluded followers argue over lips and teeth in their dreams; yet I recall following him, one step at a time. Nanhua Bing said:
"Performing somersaults atop a thousand-fathom pole, casting a fishing hook into the heart of the great ocean waves. His great substance possesses fine bone and flesh; he needs no rouge."
How elegant! Once, while Master Zhenshi of Daisui was burning a mountain, he saw a snake.
Taking his staff, the Master prodded it toward the fire and shouted, "This physical form still refuses to let go! Die right here! It was like finding a lamp in the darkness.
At that time, a monk asked, "At such a moment as this, is there still sin or not? The Master said, "When the stone tiger roars, the mountain valleys echo;
where the wooden man bellows, the iron ox is startled."
The Verse by Nantang Jing says: At the beginning and end of kalpas, the Dharma is weak and Māra is strong. Old Master Dingguang forges his backbone of iron;
with civil classics as warp and martial arts as woof, he secures the borders. Blue heavens disperse the clouds, and the Patriarchal Wind cools;
the Buddha-sun’s radiance shines, longer than the days of Emperor Shun.
Cen Master Xuefeng addressed the assembly, saying: "On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake;
you all must look at it very carefully. Changqing stepped forward and said: "Today, many in this hall will lose their lives.
Yunmen then brandished his staff toward the Master and made a gesture of fear. A monk reported this to Xuansha, who said: "It must..."
"This was first attained by Lingxiong's elder brother. Nevertheless, I do not act in this way. The monk asked, "How about you, Master?
The Master said, "What need is there for the Southern Mountain?"
Zhenjing’s text says: "How extraordinary! To know well the source and destination is not something a father can produce in his son.
He then suddenly picked up his staff, called to the assembly, and said, "The 'tortoise-nose snake' of Nanshan is right here! He then threw down the staff and said:
It would seem that one would immediately lose one's body and life.
Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "The Elephant Bone Cliff—people do not go there; those who do must be snake-handlers.
Masters Leng and Master Bei were at their wits' end; how much loss of body and life was there? Shaoyang Zhi knew this and struck again.
Grass. Nowhere in the south, north, east, or west can it be sought. Suddenly it protrudes from the tip of the staff; it is cast toward Xuefeng, who opens his mouth wide.
This wide-open mouth is like a flash of lightning; even when one raises one's eyebrows, it is not seen.
Now it is hidden before Lufeng Peak; let every visitor examine this expedient means. The Master raised his voice and shouted, "Look at the feet!"
Xiaobai said: "The elephant bone and the turtle-snake lie across the main road; Master Leng is to be pitied for having lost his life so easily.
Although Yunmen managed to bring it back to life, how can that compare to Nanshan, who does not even need to exert himself?
Zhijinwen said: "Beating the drum and playing the lute, they meet as one family. Yunmen was able to harmonize the melody; Changqing understood."
Following what is perverse; ancient melodies are not true music. As for the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain, who knows its secret technique?
Its offspring is Xuansha. Tiantong Jue said: "Xuansha was too rigid; Changqing lacked courage. The turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain died useless.
When wind and clouds meet, its horns emerge. Indeed, we see Shaoyang take up the task and play with it. Below...
Playing with it in one’s hands, one observes its shifting movements amidst flashing lightning. Within oneself, one can dispatch and summon;
toward the other, one can capture and release. To whom is this matter entrusted now? A cold mouth wounds others without knowing their pain.
Chan Master Dongshan Xuanjian was asked by a monk, "What is it like when a student goes directly forward? The Master said, "A dead snake lies across the main road;
I urge you not to step over it. The monk asked, "What happens if one steps over it? The Master said, "You lose your life-root. The monk asked, "What happens if one does not step over it?
The Master said, "There is likewise no place to avoid it. The monk asked, "At such a time as this, what is it like? The Master—
[The monk] said, "It has been lost. [The monk] asked, "I do not understand; where has it gone? The Master said, "The grass is deep; there is no place to find it.
[The monk] said, "The Master must also be on guard. The Master clapped his hands and said, "In one sense, they are all equally poisonous vapors."
Danxia Chun’s verse says: "The long river is clear and transparent, reflecting the moon’s flowers; The pure light filling one’s eyes is not yet the home.
I ask: where does the fisherman’s boat go? At night deep, it still lodges among the reeds. Tiantong Jue says:
The three old men silently turn and drag the solitary boat. At night, I turn my head back: the reeds on both banks are like snow; the misty waters of the river are autumn itself.
With the wind’s power supporting the sail, we travel without rowing; the sound of the flute calls us down to the moonlit isles.
One day, while the World-Honored One was sitting, he saw two men carrying a pig past him and asked, "What is this?
They replied, "The Buddha possesses all-encompassing wisdom; yet you do not even recognize a piglet. The World-Honored One said, "You must ask me about it."
Ming’an said: "It was not because of the World-Honored One’s question; it ended up being forgotten. Dizang En said:
"This old fellow Gautama is also groundless; he is much like one who forcibly creates knots upon existing joints.
If, suddenly, those two were to burst into loud laughter and carry off the pig and depart, that too would be a scene of utter embarrassment.
The Verse by Chan Master Mu’an Qiong: Having abandoned the raft, he harbors the intent to save all; Encountering those plowing, he again asks for the ford.
He then takes his own unreturned intention And speaks it to those on the path of desire.
Once, while Chan Master Baizhang Hai was attending upon Mazu as they were walking along, he suddenly saw a flock of wild ducks fly past.
Mazu asked, "What is that? The Master replied, "Wild ducks. Mazu asked, "Where have they gone? The Master replied, "They flew away."
The Patriarch then seized the Master by the nose; the Master, overcome with pain, let out a cry of "A-ya! A-ya!
The Patriarch said, "You just said it flew away, yet it was all along right here. The Master was so struck that sweat poured down his back; from this he attained realization.
Fenyang Zao’s verse says: "A wild duck flies through the sky, yet he asks the monk: 'How shall the ancestral seal be transmitted and the heart-lamp entrusted?
Though responding to the occasion, he remains unmoving; As soon as he seizes the essential thread, the Way may flourish. Xuedou Xian says:
The wild duck—where do you think it has gone? Mazu saw it coming and spoke with it; they exhausted their discourse on the sentiments of mountain clouds and ocean moons.
Yet, still not understanding, it flew away. Just as it was about to fly away, he seized it and said, "Speak!
Speak! Foyan Yuan said: "Ordinary things within the weeds are myriad and manifold. To say it 'flew away'—how could this have been in vain? The tip of the nose is [the place to look]."
The leather and fur are exceedingly leisurely; let them pass through the vertical and horizontal crossroads as they will. Fojian Qin said:
"Master Mazu took pity on you for lacking knowledge, so he borrowed a wild duck to convey a message.

As the duck flies and cries, a thought suddenly arises; how can the nostrils be pulled back to accomplish anything? At midday in Silla, it strikes three in the night.

In this manner, it is called from all six windows and responds to each. Yangshan bows in thanks and rises, saying:

Yunju Xi said: "If Zhongyi had not received this single phrase from Yangshan at that time, where would there be a Zhongyi?
Chongshou Chou said: "Is there anyone who can settle this principle?

When the austere is brought forth, there is dull stupidity; when dull stupidity is let loose, there is austerity. Although the monkey has fallen asleep, it remains alert within its belly.

Do you all wish to see the absurdity of these two elders? Each one has a face three inches thick. Xinxiang Xian said:

One day, Chan Master Xuefeng Cun saw a macaque and pointed at it, saying, "Each of these macaques wears an ancient mirror.
Sansheng asked, "Throughout kalpas they have been nameless; why do you designate them as 'ancient mirrors'? The Master replied, "Flaws."
Sheng said, "The Holy One [Yunmen] was a spiritual friend to fifteen hundred people, yet he did not even recognize the 'critical phrase' (huatou).
The Master said, "This old monk’s duties as abbot are too numerous."
Xuedou Xian said, "He deserves twenty blows; not even one blow is too few. Truly, such a person is rarely encountered.
Yet, it would be better to let this blow pass, so as to avoid compounding error with error. Tiantong Jue said:
If, at that time, you had seen Xuefeng say, "The flaw has arisen," you should simply have stepped forward and said, "Yes, yes.
But tell me, why was it so? When one cannot prevail through contention, yielding is more than sufficient.
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "How laughable is this mountain elder, who knows no shame; He places a head atop another head.
Leaping about before the crags, he leaves no trace to be found; A single fragment of lingering dawn-light remains ungrasped at daybreak. Zuyin Ming says:
The great earth serves as the furnace; in what year was the forging completed? Its roundness is equal to the faces of all Buddhas;

If you wish to know the state of pure, penetrating, and perfect luminosity, long and short, blue and yellow—all are without error."

An ancient worthy composed a verse: "Cold geese fly high through the chilly clouds; Their reflections fall upon the cold river, yet they do not know it.
The river water has no feelings, and the geese have no intent; Traveling among different species is just like this."
In the meditation hall, Chan Master Bian questioned a monk: "Why does the earthworm transform into a lily? He then offered this verse himself:
"My body has grown old dwelling on the mountain; Worldly affairs may run contrary as they will. For years there has been no attendant; When guests arrive, I burn incense myself."
